en: Do not praise anything else at all, O friends; do not suffer harm.
Praise only Indra, the bull, together with the pressed juice; recite your hymns repeatedly.

Like a bull that strikes down the aged, like a cow that conquers the people, he is the one who causes hatred and the one who brings about reconciliation; he is the most bountiful, bestowing both [worlds].
For although these people here invoke you in various ways for aid,
O Indra, let this our prayer be your strengthener throughout all the days.
O Maghavan, the inspired singers of the noble folk vie with one another in their songs;
come hither, bring us strength in many forms, most near for our protection.
O wielder of the stone, even for a great price I would not give you away—
for a thousand, nor for ten thousand, O wielder of the thunderbolt, nor for a hundred, O you whose wealth consists of hundreds.

O Indra, you are more excellent than my father and even than my brother who does not enjoy [wealth]. O Vasu, both you and my mother appear to me alike for the sake of providing wealth and for the granting of bounty.
Where are you? Where are you? For your mind is indeed in many places. You rush forth, O warrior, stirrer of the fray, breaker of forts; the *gāyatrī* verses have been sung aloud.
Sing forth the *gāyatra* hymn to him, the one who is ever-active and the destroyer of fortresses;
may the wielder of the thunderbolt come to sit upon the sacred grass of Kaṇva and shatter the strongholds.
Those horses of yours that are in tens, in hundreds, and in thousands— those stallions of yours that are vigorous and swift-footed— with them come quickly to us!
Today I call hither Indra, who is like a cow that yields nectar, who stirs the *gāyatrī* hymn, the well-milking milch-cow, and another nourishment that is wide-streaming and ready at hand.
When the Sun struck down Etaśa with the two bending, winged arrows of the wind,
the Lord of a Hundred Powers bore away Kutsa, the son of Arjuni, as he overtook the invincible Gandharva.
He who, even without a bandage, before the joints are pierced,
is the restorer of the fracture— Maghavan, the possessor of many riches, he heals what was shattered again.
O Indra, let us not be like strangers to you, nor like those who are alien; O wielder of the stone, we have thought ourselves as difficult to satisfy as forests abandoned by their owners.
O slayer of Vṛtra, we were indeed slow and lacking in strength;
yet, O Hero, through your one great bounty, may we rejoice in accordance with your hymn of praise.
If Indra hears my hymn, may our drops,
having flowed through the filter, swift ones who increase the strength of Tugra’s son, exhilarate him.
Come today to this joint praise; come from your friend, you who are praised by many.
May the laudation of the wealthy patrons favor you; I desire to offer you a beautiful hymn of praise.
For the presser has pressed the Soma with the stones; wash him now in the waters.
Like garments seeking cattle, the men have clothed him; they have milked him from his vital springs.
Whether from the earth or from the light of the great heaven, grow strong with this body and my song; O you of noble will, fill us with the beings that have been born.
For Indra, press the most intoxicating and excellent Soma;
may Śakra cause it to swell, as it is urged forth by every prayer like one seeking booty.
May I not, by constantly entreating you with my song at the flowing of the Soma,
provoke you like a wild beast at the libations— who indeed would not entreat one who is powerful?
Impelled by exhilaration, [you are] a fierce intoxication with fierce power;
the overcomer of all, distilling rapture—for in exhilaration you indeed grant us [our share].
The God, praised by all and extolled by many, bestows many desirable things upon the mortal who offers oblations; he grants gifts to him who presses the juice and praises him.
O Indra, come and rejoice with wondrous bounty, O God! Like pouring into a lake, fill your vast and capacious belly with Soma-draughts for our shared libations.
May a thousand, may a hundred horses, yoked to your golden chariot— tawny, long-maned steeds harnessed by prayer— bring you, O Indra, for the drinking of the Soma.
May the two bay steeds with tails like peacocks' feathers, their backs white, bring you upon the golden chariot to drink of the exhilarating, sweet-scented soma-juice.
Drink of this pressed juice, O lover of songs, like one who drinks first;
this well-prepared draught of the flavorful juice, beautiful for exhilaration, is now offered.
He who alone by his wondrous power is great and fierce through his holy ordinances—may he, the fair-cheeked one, come;
may he not stay away, but come to our call and not pass us by.
With your weapons, you crushed the moving fortress of Śuṣṇa;
you followed after the light from of old, O Indra, when you became worthy of invocation.
My hymns of praise have turned toward you, O Vasu, at the rising of the sun, at midday, and at the onset of evening and the following night.
Praise him! Praise him indeed! These are truly the most generous among the wealthy patrons—Ninditāśva, Prapathin, Paramajyā, and Medhyātithi, O Maghavan.
When I mounted the chariot with faith, bringing horses that desire the woods,
then he who possesses the wealth of the Yadus, even the cattle, takes note of it.
He who has bestowed upon me two chestnut horses together with golden trappings—
may this chariot of Saṅga, which resounds like thunder, surpass all blessings.
Then Plāyogi surpassed all others; Āsaṅga, O Agni, [gave] with ten thousand.
Ten bright ones stood up for me like reeds from a lake, O Adhokṣaṇa.
His massive [thigh] was seen from the front; boneless, it hung down like a thigh.
The eternal woman, looking upon him, said: "O noble one, you bear a most auspicious meal."
O Vasu, drink this pressed juice; fill your belly completely. O fearless one, we have offered it to you.
Shaken by men, pressed with stones, purified through the sheep’s wool filter, he is like a horse washed in the rivers.
We have made this [Soma] sweet for you with milk, as if it were barley, while we mix it;
O Indra, be present at this shared feast.
Indra alone is the drinker of Soma; Indra, the sustainer of all life, is the drinker of the pressed juice, situated between the gods and mortals.
Neither the bright [Soma], nor the ill-mixed, nor the parched [grains] can satisfy him who is wide-extending and kind-hearted.
When others, like hunters seeking game, pursue him with their cattle,
they approach him with milch-cows.
May there be three pressed Soma draughts for the god Indra, in his own dwelling, for the drinker of the pressed juice.
Three reservoirs drip forth; three ladles are well-filled, resting upon a common support.
You are pure, established in many places; you are mixed with milk in the middle, and with curd, O hero, you are most exhilarating.
These Soma juices of yours, O Indra, are strong and pressed for us here;
clear, they beg for the milk-mixture.
O Indra, mix this *āśir*, the sacrificial cake, and this Soma;
for I hear that you are wealthy.
Having drunk [the soma], they fight within their hearts like those intoxicated by liquor;
like naked men, they groan at the udder.
O wealthy one, the praiser of a bountiful patron like you would indeed be prosperous; O Lord of the Bay Horses, let him be preeminent among those renowned for their fame.
Even the hymn being recited, the enemy who possesses no cattle does not perceive; nor does he perceive the *gāyatra* song being sung.
O Indra, do not deliver us over to the scorner nor to the arrogant; O possessor of power, grant us aid with your powers.
O Indra, we indeed, as your friends devoted to you, praise you for that very purpose; the Kaṇvas laud you with hymns.
O Wielder of the Thunderbolt, I have thought of nothing else than your deeds in this newest song; indeed, I have perceived your hymn of praise.
The gods desire one who presses the soma; they do not long for sleep. Unwearied, they go forth against negligence.
Come forth quickly with your strengths; do not be angry with us, like a great man who has a young wife.
May he not, being ill-tempered, cause us harm today or this evening; like an unlovely son-in-law, may he stay far away from us.
For we know the bountiful favor of this hero,
who is born in the three [worlds] and whose intentions are manifold.
Pour forth [the soma] for Kaṇva; indeed, we know none more glorious than the powerful one who possesses a hundredfold aid.
O presser, bring the Soma for Indra, the hero, the powerful Śakra— the preeminent one— for him to drink, the manly one.
He who is most well-known among those who do not falter, [bestows] wealth consisting of horses upon his singers,
and booty consisting of cattle upon his praisers.
O pressers,
pour out the most excellent Soma for the exhilaration of the heroic, brave hero.
May the slayer of Vṛtra, the protector, come to our dwelling to drink the pressed juice; he who possesses a hundredfold aid draws near.
May the two powerful bay steeds, yoked by prayer, bring their friend here; may they bring the one renowned by songs, the lover of song, through our hymns.
Sweet are the Soma juices; come hither! The Soma juices are prepared;
come hither, O fair-cheeked one, O seer-like one, O powerful one, toward this common feast.
And those hymns which, when praised, increase thee for great bounty and manly strength— O Indra, they cause the doer of deeds to prosper.
O you who are borne by songs, these hymns and these recitations which are for you— these have truly established your powers.
Truly, this one of many exploits, the wielder of the thunderbolt in his hand, alone bestows strengths from of old,
remaining unharmed.
Indra, the much-invoked, the great by his mighty powers, slays Vṛtra with his right hand.
In whom all people, as well as great deeds and expanses, find their delight; he, the exhilarating one, follows after the wealthy patrons.
Indra has performed all these deeds— he who is renowned as surpassing all,
the bestower of booty upon the wealthy patrons.
He brings forward the chariot seeking cattle, even from afar, for whomsoever he protects; for as a lord of wealth, he is the one who carries it.
The inspired sage is a winner with his steeds; the hero is a slayer of Vṛtra with his men; he is the true protector of the one who serves him.
Worship this Indra with a concentrated mind, O Priyamedhas—
he who has truly become exhilarated by the Soma juices.
O Kaṇvas, sing praise to Gāthāśravas, the lord of the virtuous, who desires glory, who is full of courage, and who possesses great strength.
The powerful friend who, even without footprints, gives back the cows to men,
to those who have fixed their desire upon him.
Thus, O wielder of the stone, you went toward Medhyātithi, the son of Kaṇva, who was possessed of inspired thought, having become a ram as you approached him.
O Vibhindu, bestow upon him four tens of thousands;
eight thousand more besides.
And truly, those two daughters of delight, who increase the milk,
have bestowed themselves for the sake of procreation.
Drink of the flavorful pressed juice; O Indra, exhilarate yourself with our soma mixed with milk. Be our kinsman and a sharer of the feast for our prosperity; may your insights protect us.
May we, as possessors of strength, abide in your favor; do not abandon us to the assault of the enemy. Favor us with your wondrous aids; lead us toward your blessings.
O Lord of abundant wealth, may these songs of mine increase your strength;
the wise ones, pure and bright as fire, have celebrated you with hymns of praise.
This one, made powerful by a thousand seers, has spread himself out like the ocean. True is that greatness of his; his might is praised at the sacrifices in the kingdom of the inspired poets.
Indra alone we invoke for the service of the gods; Indra, as the sacrifice proceeds;
Indra, we who long for victory invoke in the encounter; Indra, for the winning of wealth.
By his greatness Indra spread out the two worlds, heaven and earth; by his might Indra caused the sun to shine.
In Indra all beings have found their support; in Indra the pressed drops find their rest.
O Indra, for the first draught, the Āyus have called out to you with hymns;
the R̥bhus, coming together, have raised their voices, and the Rudras have sung in praise of the ancient one.
In the exhilaration of this pressed juice, Indra increased his manly power and his might;
today, as in former times, men praise that greatness of his.
I beg of you that heroic power, that sacred prayer for the sake of first thought,
by which you helped the Yatis and Bhr̥gu when the prize was staked, and by which you protected Praskaṇva.
O Indra, that by which you released the ocean and the great waters—that is your virile power.
That majesty of his cannot be fully grasped, even though the worlds have roared after it.
Be gracious to us, O Indra, since I entreat you for wealth and for heroic strength.
Be gracious for the sake of booty to him who desires to win it first; be gracious, O Primal One, for our hymn of praise.
Be gracious to this prayer of ours, O Indra, for you have protected Paura who desired to win;
be gracious, O Indra, just as you protected Ruśama, Śyāvaka, Kṛpa, and Svarṇara.
What newest hymn shall the mortal sing for the swift one among the flaxen plants?
For those who praise his greatness and his Indra-power have not yet attained the light of heaven.
When do those praising you strive for the gods? Who among the seers is considered a sage?
When, O Indra Maghavan, will you come to the call of the one who presses the soma, and when to the one who praises you?
Upward rise these most honey-sweet songs, these hymns of praise,
like chariots seeking booty— ever-conquering, winners of wealth, with inexhaustible aid, and striving for victory.
Like the Kaṇvas, like the Bhr̥gus, like the Suns, they have attained every desire;
magnifying Indra with hymns, the Āyus and the Priyamedhas have raised their voices.
Yoke, O Indra, best slayer of Vṛtra, your two bay steeds from afar;
come hither, O Maghavan, for the drinking of Soma, O fierce one, with the exalted ones.
For these singers of yours have yearned with their prayer, as inspired poets for the winning of the prize;
so, O bounteous Indra, lover of songs, hear our call like a longing suitor.
O Indra, you hurled Vṛtra down from the lofty mountains;
you drove out the cattle from Arbuda, from the guileful Mṛgaya, and from the mountain.
The fires shone forth, and the sun shone forth, and the Soma, the essence of Indra, shone forth;
from the mid-air you blew away the great serpent—this, O Indra, was your manly deed.
Him whom Indra and the Maruts gave to me— Pākasthāman Kaurayāṇa—
the most beautiful of all by his own nature, as if running toward heaven.
Pākasthāman has given me a red horse, easy to harness, filling out its girths, and awakening my wealth.
To whom ten other draft-horses carry the yoke,
as birds [carry] Tugrya to his home.
The self is the father’s body, the garment is the giver of vigor, and the ointment is the fourth; I have declared Pākasthāman to be the liberal giver of the ruddy steed.
O Indra, whether you are invoked by men in the east, the west, the north, or the south—being impelled by many heroes, you are with Ānava; O bold one, you are with Turvaśa.
Or whether you, O Indra, delight yourself with Ruma, Ruśama, Śyāvaka, and Kṛpa—O Indra, the Kaṇvas, bringing hymns of praise through their sacred prayers, draw you hither; come!
Just as a wild bull, thirsty, goes to a water-hole that has been dug out, so come quickly to us at the beginning and at the end of our journey; drink well among the Kaṇvas.
O Maghavan Indra, may these drops gladden you for the sake of bestowing wealth upon the one who presses the juice.
You drank the Soma pressed in the ladle from that [pressing]; you have established that supreme power.
By his might he displayed his power; by his strength he shattered the fury [of the foe].
O Indra, O youth, all those who sought battle against you have bowed down like trees.
He who has offered praise to you is accompanied as if by a thousand young warriors;
he makes his son preeminent in heroic strength and serves with words of homage.
Let us not fear, let us not grow weary in the friendship of you, the fierce one.
O Bull, let us behold your great deed worthy of being gazed upon—that you have protected Turvaśa and Yadu.
The bull has settled upon his left hip; his gift does not provoke anger.
The cows are blended with honey from the bee; come quickly, run hither, and drink!
O Indra, your friend is indeed possessed of horses, chariots, fine form, and cattle; sharing in strengthening vigor, he always dwells with it, and radiant, he goes to the assembly hall.
Like a thirsty antelope coming to a watering hole, come and drink the Soma according to your desire;
raining down day after day, O Maghavan, you possess the most powerful strength.
O Adhvaryu, pour forth the Soma; Indra thirsts for it.
He has now indeed yoked his two vigorous bay steeds, and the slayer of Vṛtra has arrived.
Even that person considers himself a donor where you satisfy yourself with Soma; this is your fitting food, sprinkled together—come here, hasten forward, and drink!
O Adhvaryus, press the Soma for Indra who stands upon his chariot;
from above the ruddy mountain, the pressing-stones look on as they perform the sacrifice for the giver.
Let the two beloved, vigorous bay horses carry Indra toward the reddish-brown [soma] during the rites;
let the seven steeds, the ornaments of the sacrifice, bring you hither to the pressings.
We choose Pūṣan, the possessor of many riches, for our alliance. O powerful one, invoked by many, O liberator, grant us through our prayer strength and wealth.
Sharpen us like a razor in the hands of a barber; grant us wealth, O Deliverer!
With you, this wealth of the sun-dappled cows is easy for us to find, for you impel that mortal man toward it.
I desire you, O Pūṣan, for your favor; I desire to praise you, O Radiant One.
I do not desire that which belongs to another, for it is alien, O Vasu; I praise the *sāman* for the sake of Pajra.
The cows have gone forth to some pasture, O glowing one; our wealth is eternal, O immortal Pūṣan. Be our gracious protector, most bountiful, for the winning of booty.
We have celebrated the massive gift of a hundred horses from King Kuruṅga at the dawn-sacrifices,
among the Turvaśas, during the offerings of that brilliant and fortunate king.
Through the inspired hymns of the victorious Kaṇva, and through the Priyamedhas who reach toward heaven,
the seer won sixty thousand and drove out the herds of cattle from Nirmaja.
Even the trees rejoiced at my arrival;
they obtained cattle in abundance, they obtained horses in abundance.
When he, whose form is ruddy, has manifested from afar as if from nearby, he has spread his light in every direction.
O wondrous Aśvins, like heroes on a mind-yoked chariot of broad radiance, you accompany the Dawn.
O you two who possess abundant wealth, the hymns of praise have appeared before you both;
I have uttered this speech like a messenger.
The Kaṇvas praise the Aśvins, who are beloved by many, most gladdening, and possessors of abundant wealth, for our protection.
Most bountiful, best at winning booty, impellers, lords of splendor,
you who go to the house of the donor.
For the liberal donor who is well-disposed toward the gods, sprinkle the pasture with clarified butter— [a pasture] that is rich in wisdom and free from crossing over.
Come swiftly to our hymn of praise with your rapid falcons;
come, O Aśvins, with your horses.
With those [horses] by which you traverse the three distant realms, all the luminous spheres of heaven,
and the three nights.
And may you, O finders of the day, open up for us paths rich in cattle and full of gain,
so that we may win booty.
O Aśvins, bring to us wealth consisting of cattle, excellent heroes, and fine chariots; bring us food accompanied by horses.
Increasing in strength, O Lords of Splendor, wonder-workers with golden paths,
drink the Soma-mead.
O you two who possess wealth in horses, grant us and our liberal patrons a wide-reaching,
invincible shelter.
Come quickly indeed to that prayer of the people which most effectively reaches you;
do not stay with others!
O Aśvins, you who are worthy of our devotion, drink of this lovely,
exhilarating draught of honey that has been offered to you.
Bring to us wealth consisting of hundreds and thousands,
abounding in food, and providing sustenance for all.
For in many places indeed, O Heroes, the wise invoke you;
O Aśvins, come with the worshippers.
O Aśvins, the people who have spread the sacrificial grass, who possess oblations, and who have prepared the offerings, call upon you both.
O Aśvins, may this hymn of ours today be most effective for you and closest to your hearts. May it be for you both.
O Aśvins, that skin-bag of honey which has been placed upon your chariot for the sake of the people— drink from it!
O you who possess abundant wealth, bring us with that [gift] well-being for our cattle, our offspring, and our kine; bring us plenteous nourishments.
And may you, O finders of the day, rain down for us celestial refreshments and the rivers, as if opening two doors.
When will the son of Tugra, cast away upon the sea, worship you, O heroes,
so that your chariot may fly with its winged steeds?
O Nāsatyas, you have constantly granted aids to Kaṇva, the seer who was confined within his dwelling.
Come hither with those most recent aids and excellent praises,
O you two possessors of rain-wealth, when I call upon you.
Just as you protected Kaṇva, Priyamedha, and Upastuta, O Aśvins, so protect Atri and Śiñjāra.
And as [you helped] Aṃśu for the sake of wealth to be won, and Agastya for the sake of cattle; or as you helped Sobhari in the contests for booty.
O Aśvins, possessors of bull-like wealth, we who sing your praises seek from you this much, or even more than this, of your favor.
O Aśvins, mount the chariot with its golden seat and golden reins,
for it reaches unto the heavens.
Golden is your supporting pole, golden the axle,
and both wheels are golden.
Therefore, O you who possess abundant wealth, come to us even from afar,
to this my well-spoken hymn of praise.
O immortal Aśvins, you two come from afar, consuming many offerings belonging to the Dāsas.
Come to us with splendors, with renown, and with riches, O Aśvins,
Nāsatyas who possess manifold light!
May the dappled-winged birds carry you both hither,
toward the people who perform the perfect sacrifice.
I sing after your chariot, which rolls along with its provision;
no obstacle hinders its wheel.
On a golden chariot with swift-footed horses, O Nāsatyas, you who are impelled by our prayers.
O you two of bull-like wealth, you enjoy the wakeful wild beast;
as such, provide us with nourishment and riches.
O Aśvins, take note of these new gifts of mine,
just as Kaśu, the son of Cedi, gave a hundred camels and ten thousand cattle.
He who bestowed upon me ten kings as bright as gold— beneath the feet of Caidya are the subjects, and all the people around are like those treading on skins.
Let no one go upon that path by which these Cedis travel; let no other patron, however much he may bestow, claim to be a man who gives more abundantly than he.
Great is Indra, who by his might is like Parjanya rich in rain;
he has grown strong through the hymns of Vatsa.
When the bearers bring forward the offspring of the *ṛta*,
the inspired poets fulfill it by means of the vehicle of the *ṛta*.
When the Kaṇvas have made Indra the accomplisher of the sacrifice with their hymns of praise, they proclaim his kinship as their own weapon.
All the tribes, all the peoples, bow down before his wrath,
just as rivers flow toward the ocean.
His vital power blazed forth when Indra rolled together both worlds like two skins.
With his hundred-jointed, virile thunderbolt, he indeed split asunder the head of the violently shaking Vṛtra.
We praise these [songs] aloud; these thoughts are at the forefront of inspired prayers, like the flashing brilliance of Agni’s flame.
The thoughts, shining forth by themselves from their secret place,
have been offered with the stream of Truth by the Kaṇvas.
O Indra, may we obtain from you that wealth consisting of cattle and horses; may our prayer be foremost for the sake of your mindful regard.
For I have indeed received from my father the wisdom of the Eternal Order;
I have been born like the Sun.
With an ancient hymn, I adorn my songs like Kaṇva,
by which Indra has indeed assumed his strength.
O Indra, whether those seers who have not praised you or those who have praised you,
increase for me alone when well-praised.
When his wrath thundered, shattering Vṛtra limb by limb,
he sent the waters toward the ocean.
O Indra, you struck down the firm thunderbolt upon the Dasyu Śuṣṇa; for you, O fierce one, are renowned as a bull.
Neither the heavens nor the mid-air regions, nor the earths, can contain Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, by reason of his might.
O Indra, him who lay prostrate, obstructing your mighty waters—
you struck him down upon his feet.
O Indra, him who has seized these two great worlds, heaven and earth, together— you have hidden him in darkness.
O Indra, you whom the Yadus and the Bhr̥gus have praised—
O fierce one, hear my invocation!
O Indra, let these spotted cows yield for you clarified butter and milk-mixtures;
may they swell with the abundance of this sacred rite.
O Indra, those female serpents who by their power have brought forth the embryo, have encompassed it as the sun is surrounded by its laws.
O Lord of Might, the Kaṇvas have magnified you with their hymn;
the pressed Soma drops have exalted you.
O Indra, wielder of the stone, under your guidance and your praise, the sacrifice is to be extended far and wide.
O Indra, burst open for us great nourishment like a fortress rich in cattle,
as well as progeny and heroic strength.
And that famous wealth of horses, O Indra,
which shone forth of old among the tribes of the Nahuṣas.
Like a cowpen, you have extended [your protection] before our eyes, O Sūrya, when you,
O Indra, show us mercy.
O Indra, since you, the truly mighty one, rule over the peoples,
you are great and boundless in your power.
To you, who possess wide-reaching speed, the people bearing oblations cry out for protection with their drops.
In the shelter of the mountains and at the confluence of the rivers,
the sage was born through inspired thought.
From there, the wise one looks down upon the ocean from the heights,
from where he stirs when drinking the soma-libations.
Then indeed they behold the morning light of the ancient seed, which is kindled beyond the sky.
O Indra, all the Kaṇvas increase your thought and your manly power; and also, O most mighty one, your virile strength.
O Indra, take pleasure in this well-spoken hymn of mine;
protect me well, and further increase my inspired thought.
Moreover, O mighty wielder of the thunderbolt, we inspired singers have fashioned these prayers for you so that we may live.
The Kaṇvas have sung forth to Indra, like waters flowing down a slope; their hymn is full of longing for him.
Hymns have magnified Indra, as rivers swell the ocean—
the undecaying one whose fury is unsurpassed.
Come to us from afar with your two beloved bay horses;
O Indra, drink this pressed soma.
O best slayer of Vṛtra, people who have spread the sacrificial grass invoke you alone for the winning of booty.
Both worlds follow you as the two wheels follow the steed Etaśa;
so too do the pressed Soma drops follow you.
Rejoice well, O Indra, most skilled in noble deeds, at Śaryaṇāvat;
exhilarate yourself with the hymns of Vivasvat.
Growing great unto heaven, the bull, wielder of the thunderbolt, has roared;
the slayer of Vṛtra, the greatest drinker of Soma.
For you, O Indra, are the first-born seer, the sole ruler by your might; you bring forth wealth for us.
May our hundred bay horses with smooth backs carry you toward the pressed juices and the offerings.
The Kaṇvas have magnified with their hymn this ancient prayer, which overflows with honey and clarified butter.
Among the great ones, let the mortal choose Indra at the sacrifice;
let him who desires to win choose Indra for his protection.
O you who are praised by many, may the two bay steeds, lauded by the Priyamedhas,
bring you hither to drink the Soma.
A hundred have I received from Tirindira, and a thousand from Parśu—
gifts from the Yadus.
Three hundred steeds and ten thousand kine were given by the Pajras to Sāman for his song.
The preeminent one has reached up to heaven, bestowing camels yoked in teams of four,
surpassing the Yadu people in renown.
When the inspired singer has poured forth for you, O Maruts, the *triṣṭubh* hymn as nourishment,
you shine forth across the mountains.
O truly powerful and radiant ones, when you have determined your course,
even the mountains have bowed down.
Roaring with the winds, the sons of Pṛśni have risen up;
they have milked forth swelling nourishment.
The Maruts sow the mist; they cause the mountains to tremble when they go on their journey with the winds.
When the mountain and the rivers have yielded to your march, to your ordinance,
and to your great impetuous might.
We invoke you by night for our protection, and we invoke you by day;
we invoke you as the sacrifice proceeds.
Up rise those red-hued ones, brilliant in their courses;
lowing, they move across the ridge of heaven.
They release the ray with power, a path for the sun to travel;
they have spread themselves out with their beams.
O Maruts, accept this song of mine; O Ṛbhukṣans, accept this hymn of praise; accept this my invocation.
The dappled cows have milked three lakes of honey for the wielder of the thunderbolt: a well, a water-skin, and a fountain.
O Maruts, when we call upon you from heaven seeking your favor,
come quickly to us.
For you, O bounteous Rudras, lords of the *Ṛbhus*, abide in the home; and you are wise in the exhilaration of the soma-draught.
O Maruts, send us from heaven wealth that distills joy, abounding in food and providing sustenance for all.
When you, O radiant ones, have determined your course as if over the mountains,
you exhilarate yourselves with the pressed drops.
Even for so much as this, a mortal should beg for their favor,
through hymns, from that which is invincible.
Those who, like drops, blow through both heaven and earth with their rains,
milking the inexhaustible spring.
Up they have risen with their shouts, up with their chariots, and up with the winds—
the sons of Pṛśni, along with their hymns of praise.
By which [you protected] Turvaśa and Yadu, by which you protected Kaṇva who won the prize— may we meditate well upon that [power] for the sake of wealth.
O bounteous givers, may these nourishments, swelling like clarified butter, increase through the hymns of Kāṇva for you.
Where now do you, the bounteous givers for whom the sacrificial grass is strewn, rejoice?
Which priest honors you?
For indeed, O you for whom the sacrificial grass is trimmed, it has not been so since of old that you have gladdened the hosts of the Cosmic Order with our hymns of praise.
Together they have brought these great waters together, together the two worlds, and together the sun; they have joined the thunderbolt joint by joint.
They have rent Vṛtra limb from limb and split apart the mountain ranges that lacked a king, performing manly deeds of heroism.
They followed the strength and the will of Trita as he fought,
and they followed Indra in the conquest of Vṛtra.
With lightning in their hands, reaching toward heaven, with golden helmets upon their heads, the radiant ones have adorned themselves for glory.
When Uśanas came from afar to the cavern of the bull,
he roared with fear like the sky.
O gods, come to us for the giving of the sacrifice, with your horses that have golden hooves.
When the spotted deer and the ruddy steed draw as the leader at their chariot,
the brilliant ones go forth, letting the waters flow.
To the Sushoma, to the Sharyanavat, to the Arjika with its dwellings—
the men have gone with their low-rolling chariot.
O Maruts, when will you come to the inspired singer who thus invokes you, with your mercies, to him who implores you?
What now? How is it that you, who were once so dear, have abandoned Indra? Who among you can now boast of your friendship?
O Kaṇvas, let us indeed praise Agni together with the Maruts, who hold the thunderbolt in their hands and possess golden axes.
O, may I turn hither the vigorous ones, worthy of worship, who possess wondrous strength, toward new and auspicious fortune.
Even the mountains bow down, thinking themselves to be mere clods;
even the rocky peaks submit.
Moving crosswise, they carry [the offerings] as they fly through the mid-air;
the Ordainers bestow vital strength upon the one who praises them.
For Agni was born as the first, like the Sun with his radiance through his splendor;
they have spread themselves abroad with their beams.
Come to us with all your aids, O Aśvins;
O wonder-workers on golden paths, drink the Soma-mead.
Come now, O Aśvins, on your chariot with a sun-bright skin;
you who enjoy [the offerings], adorned with gold, O poets of profound insight.
Come hither from the Nahuṣas and from the mid-air with our well-fashioned hymns;
O Aśvins, drink the sweet mead pressed at the libation of the Kaṇvas.
Come to us from heaven and from the mid-air, O you who are dear to the heart;
here the son of Kaṇva has pressed for you the sweet Soma juice.
O Aśvins, having heard us, come to us for the drinking of Soma;
Svāhā! O sages, O heroes, you who increase the hymn through our prayers.
For whenever the seers of old invoked you for protection, O Heroes, come hither, O Aśvins; come to this my well-spoken hymn of praise.
Even from the luminous realm of heaven, come to us, O finders of the light, through our prayers—
O you who are mindful of Vatsa, awakened by our hymns, and hearers of our call.
Why do others sit around you with their hymns, O Aśvins?
Vatsa, the seer and son of Kaṇva, has magnified you both with his songs.
The inspired singer has invoked you both here for protection with hymns, O Aśvins.
You who are stainless and the greatest slayers of Vṛtra—be the bringers of joy to us.
When the maiden mounted your chariot, O you who possess abundant wealth,
you Aśvins reached all our prayers.
From there, O Aśvins, come on your chariot adorned with a thousand ornaments;
Vatsa, the seer and sage, has recited a honeyed hymn for you.
O Aśvins, you who are much-gladdening, possessors of many riches, and discoverers of wealth— O bearers of the sacrifice, may you both respond favorably to this hymn of mine.
O Aśvins, bestow upon us all gifts that are beyond reproach; act for us as those who observe the sacred seasons, and do not deliver us over to the censurer.
Whether you are in the distance, O Nāsatyas, or whether you are in the sky above,
come from there on your chariot adorned with a thousand ornaments, O Aśvins.
O Nāsatyas, to that seer Vatsa who has magnified you with his songs,
bestow food that is adorned with a thousand ornaments and dripping with clarity.
O Aśvins, you two bestow upon him strength that drips with ghee,
he who has praised you for the sake of favor and seeks wealth, O Lords of Bounty.
Come to us, O destroyers of enemies, to this hymn of praise, O you who possess many enjoyments! O heroes, bestow upon us great glory and grant us these things for our protection.
The Priyamedhas have invoked you both with all your aids,
O Aśvins, you who rule over the sacrifices at the calls of departure.
Come to us, O Aśvins, you who bring happiness and well-being,
for Vatsa, the praiser, has magnified you with his prayers, meditations, and songs.
With those [powers] by which you helped Kaṇva Medhātithi, with those by which you helped Vaśa Daśavraja, and with those by which you protected Gośarya— with those, O heroes, protect us.
With those aids by which, O Heroes, you protected Trasadasyu in the struggle for prize-winning wealth— with those, O Aśvins, protect us well for the winning of booty.
O Aśvins, may our hymns, well-fashioned praises, and songs increase you;
O greatest slayers of Vṛtra, being sought by many, be such to us as we desire.
The three steps of the Aśvins, which were hidden in secret, have become manifest beyond; O sages, by the paths of Truth, come hither from among the living.
O Aśvins, come now indeed for the protection of Vatsa; grant him a wide, secure shelter free from danger, and drive away those who are hostile.
Whatever manly strength is in the mid-air, whatever is in heaven, and whatever is among the five tribes of men— that, O Aśvins, bestow upon us.
O Aśvins, just as the sages have grasped your wondrous deeds,
so indeed take heed of Kaṇva.
O Aśvins, this hot offering is poured out for you with a hymn of praise;
this is the honeyed Soma, O lords of wealth, by which you take notice of Vṛtra.
Whatever [you] have done, O you of many wondrous deeds, in the waters, in the tree, or in the plants—
with that, O Aśvins, protect me.
Whether you hasten forth, O Nāsatyas, or whether you practice healing as gods,
this Vatsa does not fail to win you with his prayers, for you go to him who possesses the oblation.
Now indeed the seer has envisioned a hymn for the Aśvins with skill;
let him pour out the most honey-sweet Soma and the heated milk-oblation for Atharvan.
O Aśvins, mount now upon your chariot that moves swiftly;
may these hymns of mine cause you to hasten hither like a cloud.
O Nāsatyas, whether we have stirred you today with hymns of praise, or with songs of the voice, O Aśvins, take heed of Kaṇva’s call.
Whether Kakṣīvat invoked you, or the seer Vyaśva, or Dīrghatamas called upon you,
or whether Pṛthī Vainya did so at the sacrificial seats— O Aśvins, from this very invocation may you take heed.
Come as protectors of our dwelling and be our defenders against the foe; be the guardians of our world and the protectors of our bodies.
Come on your path for the sake of our children and grandchildren.
O Aśvins, whether you travel on the same chariot with Indra, or whether you share a common dwelling with Vāyu,
or whether you are in harmony with the Ādityas and the Ṛbhus, or whether you stand in the wide strides of Viṣṇu— [we call upon you].
If today, O Aśvins, I should invoke you for the winning of booty, or if to overcome [the enemy] in battles— that most excellent aid of the Aśvins is what I seek.
Come now, O Aśvins, to these oblations prepared for you;
these Soma-draughts are for you among the Turvaśas, and here they are among the Kaṇvas as well.
O Nāsatyas, whatever healing medicine exists for you in the distance or nearby,
with that, O wise ones, grant protection now to Vimada and to Vatsa.
I have awakened together with the divine speech of the Aśvins;
O Goddess, you have disclosed the thought and the gift for mortals.
Awaken the Aśvins, O Uṣas; awaken them, O great Goddess Sūnṛtā!
O Hotṛ of the sacrifice, awaken them in due order for the sake of exhilaration and lofty renown.
O Uṣas, when you come with your radiance, you shine together with Sūrya;
then this chariot of the Aśvins comes to the dwelling that protects men.
When the pressed stalks have been milked like cows with their udders,
or when the voices of those seeking the gods have sounded forth, O Aśvins.
Forward for glory, forward for power, forward for protection that overcomes men,
and forward for skill, O ye two wise ones!
O Aśvins, whether you now sit upon the father’s seat with your inspired thoughts, or whether you are there with blessings, O you who are worthy of praise.
Whether you two are in Dīrghaprasadman, or in the luminous realm of heaven,
or in a house fashioned upon the ocean— from there, O Aśvins, come hither!
Or if you have prepared the sacrifice for Manu, even so take heed of Kaṇva.
I invoke Bṛhaspati, all the gods, Indra and Viṣṇu, and the Aśvins who possess swift horses.
I now invoke those two Aśvins, the doers of wondrous deeds, who have been made ready for capture;
with whom our friendship exists, and whose kinship extends even among the gods.
Upon whom the sacrifices depend, and upon whom the wise patrons abide even in the darkness—
those two who are the conscious observers of the sacrifice and the rite, who by their own inherent power drink the Soma-sweetness.
O Aśvins, whether you are now in the west or in the east, O lords of ample wealth;
whether you are with the Druhyus, the Anus, the Turvaśas, or the Yadus—I call upon you both, so come to me!
Whether you fly through the mid-air, O you who enjoy many things, or whether you traverse these two worlds,
or whether you mount your chariot by your own powers, come hither from there, O Aśvins!
O Agni, you are the guardian of vows, a god among mortals;
you are to be praised at the sacrifices.
O mighty one, you are to be praised in the assemblies;
O Agni, you are the charioteer of the sacrifices.
As such, O Jātavedas, drive away from us our enemies; O Agni, ward off godless hostilities.
O Jātavedas, you do not attend the sacrifice of a mortal enemy, even though it is right before you.
We mortals meditate upon the many names of you, the immortal one, O Jātavedas, as we are inspired sages.
We sages invoke with our songs Agni, the sage, for protection; we mortals invoke the god for aid.
May Vatsa draw your mind hither, even from the most distant dwelling,
O Agni, with a song that yearns for you.
For you are the same in many places, the lord over all the tribes;
we invoke you in battles.
Seeking strength, we invoke Agni for protection in battles,
him who bestows wondrous wealth in the contests for booty.
For you are the ancient one, worthy of praise at the sacrifices; as the Hotṛ priest from of old, sit here as both ancient and new.
O Agni, satisfy your own body, and win for us prosperity through sacrifice.
O most powerful Indra, that exhilaration which is the greatest drinker of Soma and which takes notice [of us]—
that by which you strike down the devourer, for that we pray.
We implore that [power] by which you protected Daśagva, Adhrigu, Vepayan, and Svarṇara, and by which you protected the ocean.
We pray for that [power] by which you impelled the Sindhu and the great waters like chariots, so that the path of *ṛta* might be traversed.
O wielder of the stone, this hymn of praise, purified like clarified butter, is for our assistance—
that by which you have indeed grown mighty in an instant with your power.
O lover of songs, take pleasure in this; like the ocean it swells. O Indra, with all your aids you have grown great.
The god who from afar has granted us his friendship,
you have grown great, spreading it out like rain from heaven.
His banners have grown strong, and the thunderbolt is in his two hands,
when he, like the sun, caused the two worlds to swell.
O Lord of the Good, if a wicked man should bring a thousand buffaloes as an offering,
even then your great Indra-power has increased further.
Indra, with the rays of the sun, burns down the one who acts as a leech;
like Agni consuming the forest, he has grown victorious.
This newest prayer of yours, timely and full of devotion, goes forth;
serving you, much beloved, it measures out its course.
The embryo of the sacrifice, longing for the gods, purifies the ritual action in due order;
through the hymns of praise of Indra, he has grown strong and measures out [the rite].
Indra, the winner of friends, has spread himself out for the drinking of Soma;
like a forward-pointing axe, he measures it out for the one who presses the juice.
Whom the inspired poets, the Āyus who bring forth hymns of praise, have gladdened—
the truth that has swelled in their mouths like clarified butter.
And Aditi has brought forth a hymn for Indra, the self-ruling lord,
which is highly praised for his aid, being that which belongs to the Eternal Order (*ṛta*).
The bearers have shouted for help and for praise;
O God, your two bay steeds do not turn back from the path of Truth.
Whether, O Indra, you delight in Soma with Viṣṇu, or with Trita Āptya,
or whether you rejoice among the Maruts with the drops— [with all those] together.
Or if, O Śakra, you take delight in the far distance or upon the ocean,
rejoice indeed in our pressed juice together with the drops.
Whether you are the strengthener of the one who presses the juice, O Lord of the True, the sacrificer, or whether you take delight in his hymn along with the drops.
Praising each god for your protection, Indra after Indra,
they have now attained success for the sake of the victorious sacrifice.
With sacrifices they have strengthened Indra, who is borne by sacrifices; with Soma libations, him who drinks most Soma; with invocations, they have increased him and attained their goal.
Great are his guidances, and many are his praises;
all treasures have reached the one who offers oblations.
The gods placed Indra at their head to slay Vṛtra;
the voices of praise have shouted after Indra for his mighty power.
We [magnify] the great one with greatness through our hymns, him who hears our call;
with songs of praise we cry out unto him for his power.
Neither the two worlds nor the mid-air regions can contain the wielder of the thunderbolt;
at his very onset, they tremble before his overwhelming might.
O Indra, when the gods placed you at their head in the battle for supremacy,
then indeed your two beloved bay steeds carried you forward.
When you, O wielder of the thunderbolt, by your might slew Vṛtra who obstructed the rivers,
then indeed your two beloved bay horses carried you forward.
When Viṣṇu strode out his three steps by means of your power,
then indeed your two beloved bay steeds carried you forward.
When your two beloved bay steeds grew in strength day by day,
then indeed all beings submitted to you.
When the Marut clans submitted themselves to you, O Indra,
then indeed all the worlds submitted to you.
When you established that bright light, the sun, in the sky,
from that moment all beings submitted to your rule.
O Indra, this well-wrought hymn of praise for you, the inspired singer utters with his thoughts— like a kinswoman who brings success at the station, so may it further our sacrifice.
When they have sung together in his beloved abode, at the navel of the sacrifice, the milkings [of the soma] flow forth during the rite.
O Indra, grant us great heroism, abundance of horses, and plenty of cattle,
like a Hotṛ priest at the sacrifice for the sake of first thought.
When the Soma juices are pressed, Indra purifies his praiseworthy resolve;
he has found the power of the increasing strength, for he is great.
In the first heaven, in the dwelling place of the gods, he is the increaser,
easy to cross over, most renowned, and the conqueror of the waters.
I have invoked that Indra, the impetuous one, for the winning of booty and for the sake of victory;
may you be our closest friend for our welfare and for our increase.
O Indra, lover of songs, this gift from the one who presses the soma flows for you;
rejoicing in it, you shine forth upon this sacred grass.
O Indra, surely grant us now that for which we, pressing the Soma, entreat you:
bring us manifold wealth that finds the light of heaven.
When the far-seeing praiser causes your songs to burst forth with great vigor,
they grow like branches, for you take pleasure in them.
As of old, give birth to our songs; hear the call of the singer. At every exhilaration, you have grown strong for the doer of good deeds.
His joyful songs play like waters flowing down a slope— those by which he who is called the Lord of Heaven is praised with this prayer.
And he who is called the lord of the peoples, the one and only ruler— rejoice in the pressed juice with those who increase homage and seek your aid.
Praise the renowned and wise one, whose two bay steeds are victorious;
they go to the house of the worshipper who offers homage.
O you of great intellect, hastening with your dappled horses, come to the sacrifice with your swift steeds; for it is indeed for your well-being.
O Indra, most powerful Lord of the True, bestow wealth upon those who sing your praises; grant immortal fame and abundance of riches to our patrons.
We invoke you at the rising of the sun; we invoke you at midday of the day.
O Indra, being pleased, come to us with your steeds.
Come hither, run forward, and rejoice in the pressed soma mixed with milk;
spin out the ancient thread as it is known.
Whether you are in the distance, O Śakra, or whether you are nearby, O slayer of Vṛtra;
or whether you are in the ocean—you are the one who aids us with the soma-juice.
May our songs increase Indra; may the pressed Soma drops increase Indra.
Among the people who possess oblations, they have found delight in Indra.
Him indeed the inspired poets, seeking aid, have magnified with their flowing aids;
Indra, like branches, the people have made to grow.
At the Trikadruka rites, the gods performed the conscious sacrifice; may our songs increase that very sacrifice which ever prospers.
When the praiser, devoted to your service, offers hymns at the proper seasons,
he is called pure, purifying, and wonderful.
That mighty power of Rudra is conscious in the ancient abodes,
wherein the wise have established the mind.
If you choose my friendship, drink of this soma-juice,
by which we may overcome all enemies.
O Indra, lover of songs, when shall your praiser become most blessed?
When will you bestow upon us wealth in cattle and horses?
And indeed, your two well-praised, vigorous bay steeds carry the chariot of you,
the ageless one, to that most intoxicating [soma] which we implore.
We implore him, the much-praised, the youthful one, with ancient aids;
he has sat down twice upon the beloved sacrificial grass.
Grow strong, O you who are well-praised, with those aids lauded by the seers;
milk out for us swelling nourishment and protect us.
O Indra, wielder of the stone, you have indeed been our protector for one who praises you thus;
from the eternal Law (*ṛta*), I send forth to you this prayer yoked by the mind.
Yoking here those two bay steeds that share the feast, O Indra, for the drinking of Soma— those which bestow wealth, respond to our call.
May the Rudras who accompany you respond with their roar, they who possess glorious splendor;
and may the Marut-clans come toward the offerings.
These victorious charges of his have taken pleasure in his station in heaven; at the navel of the sacrifice they have established him, as is well known.
This [Agni], for long-lasting vision, while the forward-moving sacrifice proceeds, measures out the rite in due order, having looked abroad.
O Indra, your chariot is a bull; and your two bay steeds are bulls. You, O Śatakratu, are a bull; a call [to you] is a bull.
The pressing-stone is a bull, the exhilaration is a bull; this pressed Soma is a bull.
The sacrifice which you impel is a bull, and the invocation is a bull.
As a bull, I call upon you, the bull, O wielder of the thunderbolt, with your wondrous aids; for you have favored our hymn of praise—the bull is the call.
O Indra, if I were the sole lord of wealth just as you are,
my worshiper would be a possessor of cattle.
O Lord of Might, I would bestow upon this wise man and I would wish to give to him,
were I the master of cattle.
O Indra, your bountiful cow yields for the sacrificer who presses the soma both cattle and horses in abundance.
O Indra, there is no restrainer of your bounty, neither god nor mortal,
when you, being praised, desire to bestow wealth.
The sacrifice strengthened Indra when he spread out the earth,
fashioning a diadem for himself in heaven.
O Indra, we choose your protection— you who have grown mighty and have won all treasures.
In the exhilaration of Soma, Indra extended across the mid-air and the luminous realms when he split Vala asunder.
He drove forth the cows for the Aṅgirases, making manifest those that were hidden in the cave; he pushed Vala downward.
By Indra, the luminous realms of heaven were made firm and strengthened; they are steadfast and shall not be driven away.
Like a wave of waters, O Indra, the exhilarating hymn speeds toward you; your intoxications have shone forth.
For you, O Indra, are indeed the increaser of the *stoma* and the increaser of the *uktha*; you are the bringer of good fortune to those who offer praise.
May the two long-maned bay steeds bring Indra here to drink the Soma,
to this sacrifice of the bounteous giver.
With the foam of the waters, O Indra, you struck off the head of Namuci,
when you conquered all rival hosts.
O Indra, as they sought to escape by means of magic illusions and attempted to climb up to heaven, you shook down the Dasyus.
O Indra, you scattered the assembly that offered no libations in all directions,
becoming the superior drinker of Soma.
Sing forth to him who is invoked by many and praised by many;
with songs, seek to win over the powerful Indra.
He whose great power is twofold supports both heaven and earth,
the mountains, the plains, the waters, and the light with his virile strength.
As such, you rule, O much-praised one; alone you strike down the Vṛtras, O Indra, so that we may attain victories and glorious renown.
We praise that exhilarating draught of yours, the bull-like one who conquers in battles,
the world-maker, O wielder of the stone, who possesses the splendor of the bay horses.
By which [light] you found the luminaries for Āyu and for Manu;
rejoicing in this sacred grass (*barhis*), you shine forth.
Even today, the chanters of hymns praise that of yours according to the ancient way;
day after day, may you win the waters whose lord is the rain-god.
That great Indra-power of yours, your vigor and your wisdom—
the Dhiṣaṇā sharpens that most excellent thunderbolt.
O Indra, heaven increases your manly power, and earth increases your fame;
the waters and the mountains urge you on.
Viṣṇu, the lofty dwelling, Mitra, and Varuṇa praise you;
the host of Maruts exults after you.
You, O Indra, were born as the bull among people, the most bountiful;
you truly possess all blessings that bring good offspring.
Truly, O much-praised one, you alone strike down the Vṛtras;
no other than Indra performs a greater deed.
O Indra, when they invoke you from various sides with prayers for help,
conquer the light of heaven here with our men.
Sufficient for our great dwelling, entering into all forms,
gladden Indra, the Lord of Might, for victory.
Let the praiser extol with new songs Indra, the sovereign lord of the peoples, the hero who overcomes men, the most bountiful.
In whom all hymns of praise and all glorious deeds find delight,
like the favor of the waters in the ocean.
I invite him with excellent praise— the supreme king, the achiever in battle, the possessor of great strength— for the sake of winning vast prizes.
Whose exhilarations are unfailing, profound, vast,
and victorious, full of joy in the battle for heroes.
Him indeed they invoke for support when the spoils have been set out;
those on whose side Indra is, they conquer.
Him the people honor with mighty deeds and with their works;
he is Indra, the creator of wide space.
Indra is the priest, Indra is the seer, Indra is the one invoked by many;
great through his mighty powers.
He is worthy of praise, he is to be invoked, the true hero of many deeds; though he is alone, he is the conqueror.
The people, the inhabitants of the earth, magnify that Indra with hymns, with chants, and with *gāyatra* verses.
The leader toward greater wealth, the creator of light in battles, the one who utterly overcomes enemies in combat.
May he, the much-invoked Indra, our deliverer, carry us safely across all enemies by means of his ship.
As such, O Indra, favor us with spoils; grant us a path and lead us toward happiness.
Come hither, for we have pressed the juice for you; O Indra, drink this Soma! Sit upon this sacred grass of mine.
O Indra, let your two long-maned bay horses, yoked by prayer, bring you hither;
listen to our sacred invocations.
O Indra, we who possess the Soma, being priests and accompanied by you as our ally, call upon you, the drinker of Soma, as we have pressed the juice.
Come to us who have pressed the juice; come to our beautiful hymns of praise.
Drink well, O fair-cheeked one, of the soma-plant.
I pour it into your two sides; let it flow through your limbs. Seize the honey with your tongue.
May it be sweet for your enjoyment, honeyed for your body;
may Soma be a blessing to your heart.
O you who are active among all people, like a woman surrounded by her kin,
let this Soma flow forth toward you, O Indra.
With a powerful neck, a belly like a sacrificial vessel, and strong arms, Indra, in the exhilaration of the soma juice,
strikes down the Vṛtras.
O Indra, go forth at the head; you are the lord of all by your might.
O slayer of Vṛtra, strike down the obstacles.
Long be your hook, with which you bestow wealth upon the sacrificer who presses the soma.
O Indra, this Soma of yours has been purified upon the sacred grass; come hither, hasten to it, and drink!
O Śācigu, for you who are honored for your power, this [soma] is pressed for your delight;
O Ākhaṇḍala, you are being invoked.
O grandson, great-grandson of the bull-horned one, you who are worthy of the *kuṇḍapāyya* draught— may he fix his mind upon this [sacrifice].
O Vāstoṣpati, you are a firm pillar and a shelter for those who offer Soma. Drapsa is the breaker of eternal fortresses; Indra is the friend of the sages.
The worshipful Pṛdākusānu, seeking cattle, though being alone, overcame those who were more numerous;
with his swift grasp he led the impetuous horse Indra forward to drink the Soma.
Now indeed, let the mortal beg this unprecedented favor from these Ādityas at their impulse.
For unassailable is the path of these Ādityas; undeceived are their guardians, who increase our well-being.
May Savitṛ, Bhaga, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman grant us that wide-spreading protection which we implore.
O divine Aditi, whose sustenance is unimpaired, come with the gods; O you who are dearly beloved, come together with the patrons who provide excellent protection.
For these sons of Aditi know how to ward off hostilities; they are wide-ruling and free from malice, even against distress.
May Aditi protect our cattle by day, and Aditi, free from duplicity, by night;
may Aditi, the ever-increasing one, save us from distress.
And may that Aditi, our thought by day, come to us with her aid;
may she grant us peace and bliss, and drive away our enemies.
And may those two divine physicians, the Aśvins, grant us well-being; may they drive away from here our affliction and our adversaries.
May Agni make us well with his fires; may Sūrya warm us pleasantly. May the wind blow auspiciously and free from harm, driving away our adversaries.
Drive away disease, drive away misfortune, and drive away ill-will;
O Ādityas, keep us far from distress.
O Ādityas, keep the arrow away from us, and also keep off the curse; O possessors of all wealth, drive our enemies far away.
O Ādityas, grant us that protection which releases even the sinner from his sin,
O you of bounteous gifts.
Whatever mortal, through his demonic nature, seeks to harm us— may that man come to ruin by his own ways.
May that evil reach the mortal enemy who speaks ill of us,
he who is hostile toward us and double-tongued.
O gods, you are accessible to all; you know the mortal man within his heart, O Vasus, both the double-tongued and the single-minded.
We choose for ourselves the protection of the mountains and the shelter of the waters;
may Heaven and Earth drive away from us the injury we have committed.
O Vasus, with your auspicious protection, ferry us across all difficulties by means of your boat.
O Ādityas, most glorious ones, grant us this for our offspring and progeny: that we may live a longer life.
O Ādityas, the sacrifice is indeed within your reach; be gracious!
We belong to you alone in our kinship.
We implore the great protection of the Maruts, the divine savior Aśvins,
Mitra, and Varuṇa for our well-being.
O Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa, grant us a blameless, manly, and praiseworthy shelter with triple protection, O Maruts.
For we, O Ādityas, are indeed men who have death as their kin;
therefore, extend our lifespan so that we may live.
Sing praise to him, the one who brings light to men; the gods have established him as the divine messenger.
They have offered the oblation among the gods.
O sage Sobhari, invoke Agni, the bestower of abundant gifts, whose radiance is manifold,
the controller of this Soma-offering, the ancient one for the sake of the sacrifice.
We have chosen you, the most excellent sacrificer, the immortal god among the gods, the priest of this sacrifice, the one of skillful wisdom.
To the Son of Strength, the fortunate one, the brightly shining Agni of most excellent luster—
may he win for us the favor of Mitra, of Varuṇa, and of the Waters in heaven.
The mortal who has worshipped Agni with fuel, with oblations, and with sacred knowledge; he who, performing the rite well, has honored him with reverence.
His swift and fleet-footed horses hasten forward; his glory is most resplendent.
No distress wrought by the gods, nor any brought by mortals, shall reach him from any side.
May we, with good fires, be united with your fires, O Son of Strength, Lord of nourishments; may you, rich in heroes, be well-disposed toward us.
Praising him like a friendly guest, Agni is like a chariot known to all;
in thee abide secure and perfect dwellings; thou art the king of riches.
O Agni, that mortal who performs the rite of worship is truly fortunate; he is to be praised, and through his prayers, may he be a winner of wealth.
He for whose sacrifice you stand upright, O lord of heroes, succeeds;
he wins with his swift steeds, he wins with those who sing praises, and he wins the prize with his heroes.
In whose house Agni, the possessor of all desirable things, accepts the hymn with pleasure, or who, as a servant, zealously offers the oblations— him [Agni] favors.
O Son of Strength, at the gifts of the inspired singer who praises you most swiftly, O Vasu,
make the word of the one who has found [you] superior to the gods and close to mortals.
Whoever seeks to win over Agni, the highly skillful one, with offerings of oblations, with reverences, or with song—
him whose flame is like a prize-winning steed.

The mortal who, with kindled fuel and sharpened devotion, serves Aditi through his ritual foundations— he, being blessed, shall by his prayers and splendors pass beyond all people, even as one crosses over waters.
O Agni, bring us that splendor which shall overcome every devourer in our dwelling,
and the wrath of the evil-minded person.
That by which Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman perceive, by which the Nāsatyas and Bhaga perceive— that, O Indra, may we worship with your power as those who best know the path, being protected by you.
O Agni, those wise ones are indeed well-disposed who have established you, O inspired singer, as the one who beholds men—
those inspired singers, O God, who possess excellent wisdom.
They have prepared the altar for you, O Blessed One; they have prepared the oblation and the pressing of the soma in heaven.
They alone, who have directed their desire toward you, have won great wealth through their spoils.
Auspicious is our Agni when invoked; auspicious is the gift, O fortunate one; auspicious is the sacrifice;
and auspicious are the praises.
Make your mind auspicious for the conquest of Vṛtra, by which you may prevail in battles;
loosen the many firm [bonds] of those who are arrogant. May we win through your aids.
I praise with song the one established by Manu, whom the gods have appointed as their messenger and steward—
the most excellent sacrificer, the bearer of oblations.
To Agni, who has sharp fangs, who is youthful and resplendent, you sing forth an offering— Agni, who,
when invoked with offerings of clarified butter, fashions heroic power through his bounteous gifts.
When Agni, invoked with offerings of clarified butter, brandishes his axe up and down,
he is like an Asura displaying his robe.
The god established by Manu, who has sent forth the oblations with his fragrant mouth— He,
the immortal divine Hotṛ priest, performs the sacrifice well and strives to win desirable boons.
O Agni, son of strength, invoked with oblations, if you were a mortal and I were an immortal, O you of Mitra-like majesty— 8.19.25cd.
O Vasu, may I not deliver you over to calumny, nor to evil, O Truthful One;
may my praiser never be in want, nor ill-disposed, nor suffer misfortune through sin, O Agni.
Like a son well-nourished in his father’s house, may our oblation go forth to the gods.
O Agni, may I, a mortal, always enjoy your most immediate aids to my heart's content, O Vasu, the god.
By your wisdom may I win, by your gifts, O Agni, and by your praises;
for they call you alone my providence, O Vasu—O Agni, rejoice to give!
O Agni, he whom you choose as your friend prospers through your protections— protections that grant heroic sons and bring the spoils of war.
Your dark-blue drop, lowing at the proper season, kindled by the pious, has been taken up, O bounteous one.
You are the beloved of the great Dawns; you reign over the dawns of night.
To him, the thousand-testicled one, the most effective helper, the sovereign lord of Trasadasyu, we Sobharis have come for protection.
O Agni, you to whom other fires are subordinate like branches,
I win for myself the splendors of men like inspired songs, while increasing your sovereign powers.
O guileless Ādityas, you who lead the mortal man across to the further shore— O bounteous givers, [you lead] all those who are wealthy.
O kings, you who subdue the people, whoever among them rules over human beings—
may we, O Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman, be the charioteers of your *ṛta*.
Trasadasyu, the son of Purukutsa, has given me fifty brides;
he is the most generous noble, the lord of the virtuous.
And for me, at the ford of the Suvāstu river, Śyāva became the leader of Prayiyu and Vāyiya; he, the Vasu, became the lord of three times seventy gifts.
Come hither; do not fail us, O you who are ever on the march! Do not stay away, O you of one mind; you who bend even the firm things.
O Maruts, lords of the *Ṛbhus*, with your strong-fellied chariots and brilliant splendors, O Rudras— come today with food, you who are much-desired, to our sacrifice, you who long for the *Sobharis*.
For we know the fierce might of the sons of Rudra, of the impetuous Maruts,
and of the bounteous Viṣṇu, the swift one.
The islands flew asunder and the misfortune stood still; both heaven and earth were joined together.
The desert wastes were swept away when you, O bright-helmeted ones, self-luminous, went forth in your agitation.
Even the immovable mountains and the lord of the forest roar at your onset;
the earth trembles during your marches.
To let you pass through, O Maruts, the vast heaven has opened wide above for your approach,
where the heroes, possessing strength in their arms, display their powers upon their own bodies.
According to their own nature, the men— great, brilliant, impetuous, bull-like in form, and with unswerving forms— bear along their glory.
The arrow of the Sobharis is anointed with the milk of cows upon the golden seat of the chariot.
O well-born kinsmen of the cow, great ones, come for food and enjoyment, not merely for our protection.
O Maruts, you who possess spotted deer as steeds, bring forth your oblations for the mighty host,
for those who advance with vigor.
O Maruts, on your chariot with its powerful horses, its powerful motion, and its powerful nave—
come like winged falcons at will, O heroes, to enjoy our oblations!
Their ointment is the same; their golden ornaments shine upon their arms, and their spears flash brilliantly.
Those fierce ones, the bulls with fierce arms, have not exerted themselves over their own bodies;
firm are the bows and weapons upon your chariots, and glory rests upon your faces.
Whose name is like a vast, spreading flood, the one among many that is wondrous for our enjoyment— like ancestral vitality, their power is overwhelming.
Worship them, the Maruts; praise them, for of those roaring ones there is no last, as there is none among the spokes; such is their bounty, such is their greatness.
O Maruts, he was fortunate under your former protections at the break of dawn;
or indeed, he shall be so even now.
Or that hero to whom you go, O Vājins, to partake in his oblations—
may he, O shakers, attain your favor through splendors and through the winning of prizes.
Just as the sons of Rudra, the youthful ones, desire from the divine Asura, the Ordainer of heaven, so may it be for you two.
O Maruts, bounteous givers who deserve our praise, you who move among us as munificent lords—
come even from there with a most gracious heart, O youths, and turn yourselves toward us.
O Sobhari, sing with your newest song to the youthful, purifying bulls,
as one who ploughs sings to his oxen.
Those who are victorious like a fist-fighter, to be invoked in all battles among the hotṛ-priests—
those Maruts, truly most renowned, like shining bulls, do you indeed honor with your song!
Even the cows, O Maruts, being of one mind, kinsmen by common birth,
lick one another's humps.
O dancers with golden ornaments upon your breasts, even a mortal man attains brotherhood with you;
O Maruts, look upon us, for your friendship is forever steadfast.
O Maruts, you of liberal gifts, bring to us of the Marut host the medicine;
you are our friends and our steeds.

With those aids by which you protect the Sindhu, by which you overcome [the foe], and by which you show favor to Krivi— O you who bring delight, be a source of joy to us with your auspicious protections, O you whose enemies are never near.
Whatever medicine is in the Sindhu, whatever is in the Asiknī, whatever, O Maruts who possess the fair sacrificial grass, is in the oceans, and whatever medicine is in the mountains—
Beholding all things, you carry them within your bodies; with that, speak in our favor.
O Maruts, heal the injury upon the earth for us who are sick, and restore what has been shattered.
O matchless one, we, seeking your aid and bearing you like something solid, invoke you, the wondrous one, for the sake of booty.
Come near to us for aid in this rite, O fierce one, who hast boldly come to us as our protector;
for we, as friends, have chosen thee alone, O Indra, as our victorious helper.
Come here to these Soma drops, O Lord of horses, Lord of cattle, Lord of the fertile fields; drink the Soma, O Lord of Soma.
For we, the singer-poets who are without kin, have drawn you, O Indra, who possess many kinsmen.
O Bull, come with all those forms of yours for the drinking of the Soma.
Sitting like birds at honey-blended, intoxicating, and exhilarating mead,
O Indra, we cry out to you repeatedly.
We address you with this homage; why do you hesitate even for a moment? O Lord of Bay Horses, there are desires; you are the giver. We exist, and our prayers exist as well.
O Indra, we have indeed become yours anew through your protection;
for we have known you from of old as the possessor of abundant wealth, O wielder of the stone.
We know your friendship and your bounty, O Hero; those we seek from you, O Wielder of the Thunderbolt.
Furthermore, O Vasu, O fair-cheeked one, sharpen us for the prize consisting of cattle in this common struggle.
Him who in former times brought this and that wealth to us— him, Indra, I praise for you, O friends, for our protection.
The Lord of the virtuous, master of bay horses, subduer of the peoples—he indeed is the one who has rejoiced;
may that Maghavan bestow upon us, his worshippers, hundreds of cattle and horses.
With you as our ally, O Bull, may we indeed speak back to the one who snorts in defiance at the assembly of the cattle-owning folk.
O much-invoked Indra, may we, as performers, conquer in our performance; may we overcome the evil-minded. With our men, may we slay Vṛtra and may we flourish. O Indra, further our prayers.
O Indra, by your very birth you have from of old been without a rival, without kin, and without a friend;
yet through battle you seek companionship.
O Surāśva, you do not find one who possesses wealth for friendship; they revile you. But when you make the river roar, you gather [the waters] together, and then you are invoked like a father.
O Indra, let us not, like the foolish and aged, sit down together at the pressed juice in the friendship of one such as you.
O giver of cattle, Indra, let us not be excluded from your bounty, nor may we fail to receive it;
even the firm possessions of the noble foe, seize them and bring them to us, for your gifts cannot be thwarted.
Either Indra indeed bestows such wealth, or the fortunate Sarasvatī grants riches;
or you yourself, O Citra, [grant them] to the donor.
Truly wonderful is the King; indeed, all others are but petty kings who dwell along the Sarasvatī.
Like Parjanya with his rain, he has spread abroad, bestowing thousands and tens of thousands.
Hither I call today that most wondrous chariot for aid,
O Aśvins, you who are easy to invoke and whose paths are red, upon which you mounted for Sūryā.
The one of ancient life, easy to invoke, much-desired, Bhujyu, foremost in battles— him who is accompanied by blessings, O Sobhari, the one who drives away hatred and is free from harm.
Hither, with our salutations, we bring those two Aśvins, the most manifold beings, the gods,
to turn toward us for our protection, they who go to the house of the donor.
One wheel of your chariot moves around; the other speeds along its path. O Lords of Splendor, may your favor hasten toward us like a milch-cow.
O Aśvins, that chariot of yours which has three seats and golden reins,
renowned as it circles around heaven and earth— come upon it, O Nāsatyas.
Bestowing gifts upon Manu, you plow the ancient grain in the sky with the wolf;
as such, O Aśvins, lords of splendor, we shall praise you today with our hymns of devotion.
Come to us, O Lords of Wealth, by the paths of Truth, those paths by which you, O Bulls, quickened Tr̥kṣi, the son of Trasadasyu, for the sake of great dominion.
This Soma has been pressed for you with stones, O heroes, possessors of bull-like wealth;
come hither to drink the Soma, and drink in the house of the donor.
O Aśvins, lords of wealth, mount upon the golden seat of your chariot;
yoke your plenteous nourishments.

With those aids wherewith you helped Paktha, wherewith you helped Adhrigu, and wherewith you helped Babhru when he was bereft of his companions— with those same aids, O Aśvins, come to us quickly and swiftly, and heal whatever is diseased.
When we, the unrestrained ones, call upon the unrestrained Aśvins even at this time of day with our songs, we do so as those who praise them.
With those [powers], O bulls, come hither to my call—[the call] which provides all food and contains all that is desirable.
O heroes, most bountiful with nourishment and most abundant in being, come hither with those [powers] by which you strengthened Krivi.
Even now, at this very time of days, I address those two Aśvins with praise;
them indeed we implore with prostrations.
Those two at evening and those at dawn, O Lords of Splendor, those who travel on paths of light— O Rudras, rich in prizes, do not overlook us to the enemy mortal.
For the sake of easy passage, I, Sobhari, like a father, invoke the two Aśvins at dawn with their easy-rolling chariot, they who are capable of providing aid.
O bulls, swift as thought, distilling exhilaration, come with your most rapid aids;
even from afar, be present for our protection with your many ancient succors, O you who provide manifold nourishment.
O Aśvins, you who drink the sweet draught, O heroes, come to our dwelling bringing horses;
O wonder-workers, bring us cattle and gold.
Excellent protection, heroic strength, most desirable wealth— unassailable by the Rakṣas-demons—
at this approach of yours, O lords of ample riches, may we obtain all precious things from you both.
Invoke indeed the one worthy of worship; sacrifice to Jātavedas, whose smoke wanders abroad and whose radiance is ungraspable.
O Viśvamanas, with my song I praise Agni, the giver, who belongs to all people;
and I extol the competing chariots.
Those whose pressing is worthy of hymns, for whom food and strength are to be seized—
the bearer of the oblation finds wealth through their discovery.
The flame of him, the shining one, has risen up, ageless, from him whose jaws are glowing, who is well-beaming, and whose glory is his troop.
Arise, O you of well-performed sacrifice, being praised with divine beauty; shining brightly with great splendor, look upon us with your light.
O Agni, come with our excellent praises, as we offer the oblations in due order,
just as you have become the messenger, the carrier of the sacrificial offerings.
I invoke for you Agni, the ancient one, the Hotṛ-priest of the peoples;
him I laud with this speech, and him indeed I praise for you.
Him of wondrous power, whom they bring to perfection through sacrifices and with their prayers—
him who is well-established among the people devoted to Truth, like Mitra.
Those seeking the Truth have, with their song, approached him who is the observer of Truth and the accomplisher of the sacrifice;
they have found favor in the place of homage.
May our well-ordered sacrifices go forth toward him, the best of the Aṅgirases,
who is the most glorious Hotṛ among the people.
O Agni, those kindled flames of thine, ageless, are a great light;
like stallions, they are powerful and full of vigor.
As such, O Lord of Strengths, grant us wealth and heroic power;
protect us in battles for our children and grandchildren.
Or when the Lord of the People, sharpened and well-pleased among the human clans,
Agni repels all the demons.
O Hero, O Lord of the People, O Agni, listen with favor to this new hymn of mine;
burn down the guileful Rākṣasas with your heat.
Not even by means of magic can a mortal enemy prevail over him who has honored Agni with offerings of oblations.
The seer Vyaśva, desiring cattle, gratified you, the finder of wealth;
for great riches, we kindle you, even you.
Uśanas Kāvya established you as the Hotṛ-priest;
he established you, Jātavedas, the one who wins through sacrifice, for Manu.
For all the gods, being of one accord, have made you their messenger; O god, through your readiness to hear, you have become the first worthy of sacrifice.
Indeed, let a mortal hero make this immortal one his messenger— the purifier, whose path is black, who traverses the vast expanse.
With ladles uplifted, let us invoke him, the one of beautiful luster and bright radiance— Agni, the ageless and ancient one, worthy of praise by the people.
The mortal who has offered oblations to him with gifts of sacrificial food,
he bestows abundant nourishment and glory accompanied by heroic sons.
The ladle, laden with oblation, goes forth with reverence toward Agni Jātavedas, the first and foremost in sacrifices.
With these most excellent hymns, like those of Vyaśva, let us worship Agni,
whose radiance is bright, with our most bountiful thoughts.
Now indeed, O seer Vyaśva, sing with hymns like Sthūrayūpa to the wide-striding Agni, the lord of the household.
The inspired poets invoke for protection the ancient Agni, the guest of human beings and the son of the lords of the forest.
O Agni, great one, come toward all the invocations of men; sit down upon the sacrificial grass with reverence.
Win for us many desirable things; win riches sought by many—riches consisting of excellent heroism, abundant progeny, and glory.
