O Agni, you are the bestower; impel the gift for the people of Suṣāman, O most youthful Vasu, for every person forever.
For you are indeed a great overcomer; you [win] for us food consisting of cattle. O Agni, open up for us the attainment of great wealth.
O Agni, you are glorious; bring Mitra and Varuṇa hither—the two sovereign rulers, upholders of cosmic order, whose will is pure.
O friends, let us instruct a sacred prayer for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt;
I shall indeed praise you for him who is most heroic and bold.
For by your might you are renowned as the slayer of Vṛtra through the killing of Vṛtra;
O Hero, with your bounties you surpass even the liberal patrons.
Being thus praised, O Lord of the Bay Horses, bring us wealth of most wonderful renown— wealth that you, as a bountiful giver, bestow even upon the stranger.
O Indra, you who are praised, boldly bring us that which is unique and dear among men; O bold one, bring it with courage!
Neither your left hand nor your right hand do the destroyers restrain; O Lord of Bay Steeds, no adversaries can hold you back in the quests for cattle.
O wielder of the stone, I draw you toward me with songs as one fills a pen with cattle; fulfill the desire and the mind of the singer.
O slayer of Vṛtra, most excellent leader, O Vasu, come hither with your mind toward all our thoughts through your wisdom.
O Vṛtra-slayer, O Hero, may we partake of this newest gift of yours,
O Vasu, O much-invoked one, a desirable wealth.
O Indra, O dancer, for as much as your power is unassailable, so too,
O much-invoked one, is your gift to the donor unimpaired.
O most magnificent one, most manly, pour forth for great bounty; O Maghavan, though you are firm, be firm for the granting of wealth.
O wielder of the stone, our hopes have never gone elsewhere than to you;
O Maghavan, grant us this with your aids.
Truly, O dancer, I find no one other than you for the granting of bounty—
for wealth, for splendor, and for strength, O lover of songs.
Pour out the Soma-mead for Indra; let him drink it.
May he impel us with his bounty through his greatness.
I have addressed the Lord of the two bay steeds, the one who bestows skill; now, indeed, hear the one who praises you, the son of Aśva.
Truly, O Friend, even in the past no one was born more heroic than you; none is equal to you in wealth, nor in such deeds, nor in glory.
O Adhvaryu, pour out of this soma-juice that which is most intoxicating with sweetness;
for thus indeed is the hero praised, he who ever increases our prosperity.
O Indra, driver of the bay steeds, no one has ever attained your ancient praise through might, nor through glorious deeds.
Desirous of glory, we have invoked him for you, the Lord of spoils,
who is to be magnified by sacrifices that do not fail.
Come now, friends, let us praise Indra, the hero worthy of hymns,
who alone stands superior to all the peoples.
To him who does not withhold the cow, who seeks the cow, the celestial one— to him speak a wondrous word sweeter than clarified butter and honey.
His heroic powers are immeasurable; his bounty cannot be surpassed.
His sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) surpasses everything, like light.
Praise Indra like Vyaśva— him who is waveless, the possessor of vigor, the controller,
who bestows the wealth of the noble upon the worshipper.
O son of Vyaśva, thus now praise him who is the tenth and the newest,
the one well-knowing and worthy of celebration among those who move.
For you, O wielder of the thunderbolt, know how to avoid the snares of Destruction;
day by day, you are pure like one who has stepped out from the footprints.
O Indra, bring that [wealth] to us, by which you, O most wondrous one, struck down [the foe] for Kutsa; impel it doubly.
Therefore, we now implore you, O most wondrous one, for new wealth;
as such, may you be our conqueror of all adversaries.
O you of many manly powers, release us from the distress of the bear or from the weapon in the seven rivers;
humble the deadly bolt of the Dāsa.
Just as you brought wealth to Vara for Suṣāman and for the Sanis, O blessed one, rich in prizes, [bring it] to the Vyaśvas.
May the sacrificial fee of the noble son of Vyashva come to us, O Soma-drinkers;
may there be abundant bounty consisting of hundreds and thousands.
If one who has sacrificed should ask thee, "Where, O thou of wondrous deeds?"—
this Vala, having taken refuge there, stands by the Gomatī.
Those two guardians of the universe, the gods among gods worthy of sacrifice,
observers of cosmic order (*ṛta*) with purified will— them I worship.
Mitra and Varuṇa, who is of excellent wisdom, are like two chariot-drivers through their lineage;
they are of noble birth from of old, their offspring firm in their vows.
The great Mother Aditi, faithful to the Eternal Law, brought forth those two all-knowing ones for the sake of divine sovereignty with great majesty.
Great are Mitra and Varuṇa, sovereign kings, gods and Asuras; upholding the cosmic order, they proclaim the lofty Truth.
The two grandsons of great power, the two sons of Dakṣa, possessed of excellent wisdom, bestowing flowing gifts, they dwell upon the dwelling-place of nourishment.
You two who have gathered together the gifts— the celestial and terrestrial nourishments— let rainfalls accompanied by clouds come toward you both.
Those two who look down from the lofty heaven like herds, the observers of cosmic order (*ṛtāvānau*), the sovereign kings established for the sake of homage.
The two observers of cosmic order, of noble will, have sat down for sovereign rule;
the two Kṣatriyas, firm in their vows, have attained dominion.
Even more than the eye, you two are the best finders of the path; with unblinking vision, the keen-sighted ones have observed everything.
And may the goddess Aditi protect us, and the Nāsatyas;
may the Maruts of increased strength protect us.
O bounteous ones, protect our ship by day and by night; may we, unharmed, be accompanied by your guardians.
May we, remaining unharmed, serve the non-slaying Viṣṇu, the giver of good gifts.
O Self-moving Sindhu, hear us for our first thought!
We choose that desirable, most excellent, and worthy-of-protection boon, which Mitra, Varuṇa, and Aryaman guard.
And may Sindhu, the lord of waters, the Maruts, and those two Aśvins,
as well as Indra and Viṣṇu— the bounteous ones— be of one accord with us.
For those impetuous heroes indeed strike back against the hostile assault of any man, just as a sharp torrent strikes down obstacles.
This one alone thus looks upon many things as the lord of the people;
we follow his ordinances according to our will.
We follow the ancient, familiar ordinances of universal sovereignty—
the far-famed laws of Mitra and Varuṇa.
He who has measured out the ends of heaven and earth with his ray—
he has filled both worlds with his greatness.
Upward has that Sūrya extended his light from the shelter of heaven,
bright like Agni when kindled and offered oblations.
He who possesses speech that finds a long-lasting dwelling is the lord of booty consisting of cattle;
for he is indeed the master in the granting of wholesome food.
Therefore, O Sūrya, I address you and both worlds, heaven and earth, at evening and at dawn; rise ever toward us among those who provide enjoyment.
We have won the straight-running [steed] for Ukṣaṇyāyana, the silver one for Harayāṇa,
and the harnessed chariot for Suṣāmaṇ.
These two [steeds] of mine, the bestowers of bay horses, are the givers of tawny steeds;
and indeed, they are the bearers of men who bring about success.
With our newest hymn,
we, the inspired poets, have brought together the two great prize-winning steeds, which possess reins and whips.
I invoke your chariot for united praise among the patrons—
O bulls of unassailable power, possessors of bull-like wealth!
O Nāsatyas, you two come with your aids for Varo Suṣāman and for his great lineage, O bulls, O possessors of bull-like wealth.
We invoke you both today with oblations, O lords of ample wealth,
you who bestow many refreshments throughout the nights.
O Aśvins, heroes, let your most swift and famous chariot come hither;
behold the hymns of the zealous one for the sake of glory.
O Aśvins, possessors of bull-like wealth, even if you are provoked to anger, take heed;
for you two, O Rudras, shall carry us across our enemies.
For, O wonder-workers, you fly swiftly all around the universe with your rapid steeds; O Lords of Splendor, you who are honey-colored, you who quicken the prayer.
Come to us, O Aśvins, together with wealth that nourishes all, you bounteous lords, rich in heroes, and unshakable.
O Indra and Nāsatyas,
come today to this my offering, O gods, most worthy of being honored by the gods.
For we, like Vyaśva, call upon you two while seeking nourishment;
O sages, come here with your gracious favors.
O seer, praise the Aśvins; will they not hear your call?
Will they not drive away the Paṇis who are closer at hand?
O heroes, hear the call of Vaiyaśva; may you two take heed of this my prayer, together with Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman.
O wise ones, day by day grant me a portion of that which is bestowed by you and brought by you through the patrons, O bulls.
He who has encompassed you both with sacrifices, like a bride beneath her veil— him the Aśvins, serving him for his glory, have made [prosperous].
O Aśvins, he who perceives your most expansive protection for men— come around to his dwelling, well-disposed toward us.
O you who possess bull-like wealth, come to us for our protection;
like two seekers of the sacrifice, you have carried [the offering] by means of our song.
O Aśvins, may this most excellent hymn, the best of invocations, become for you two a messenger calling you, O heroes.
Whether you are there in the ocean of heaven or rejoicing in the home of nourishment,
hear me, O immortals!
And may this Śvetayāvarī river, the most swift-coursing of rivers for you two, the Sindhu with its golden path, [bring you].
O Aśvins, with this well-praised hymn and with this bright prayer, you who travel in splendor, come hither.
Yoke, O Vasu, your chariot-drawing steeds; harness those that bring prosperity.
O Vāyu, drink our honeyed mead; come to our libations.
O Vāyu, Lord of Cosmic Order, wonderful son-in-law of Tvaṣṭṛ, we choose thy protections.
We, having pressed the soma, seek Vāyu— the son-in-law of Tvaṣṭṛ, the lord of wealth— for splendor, as do other people.
O Vāyu, come from heaven auspiciously; bring us excellent horses. Bring [us] great wealth on your chariot with its broad sides.
For we invoke you, the most beautiful of forms, in the assemblies of men; we honor you with great bounty like a pressing-stone mounted upon a horse's back.
O divine Vāyu, being exhilarated in your mind as the foremost one, do you grant us strength, waters, and inspired thoughts.
Agni is the domestic priest at the hymn; the pressing-stones and the sacred grass are at the sacrifice.
With a verse I seek the Maruts, Brahmaṇaspati, and the gods for their desirable aid.
Sing forth to the cattle, to the earth, to the trees, to Dawn and Night, and to the plants!
And you all, O Vasus, possessors of all wealth, be the furtherers of our prayers.
May our sacrifice proceed forth, O Agni, as the foremost among the gods;
may it go forth among the Ādityas, among Varuṇa whose laws are firm, and among the Maruts who shine with universal splendor.

For all you who possess all knowledge have indeed become the increasers of man, O destroyers of enemies. O possessors of all wealth, protect us with unharmed guardians and grant us a dwelling free from wolves.
Come to us today with one mind, all of you in harmony; O Maruts, Goddess Aditi, come with our hymn and song to this great dwelling and home.
O Maruts, come toward our dear offerings for your horses; O Mitra, come forth to the oblations!
May Indra, Varuṇa, and the swift heroes, the Ādityas, sit upon our sacred grass.
We, having trimmed the sacrificial grass and prepared the offerings in succession,
having pressed the Soma, O Varuṇa, we invoke you like Manu, with our fires kindled.
Come forth, O Maruts, Viṣṇu, Aśvins, and Pūṣan, with a thought directed toward me!
May Indra come first with those who desire to win, he the bull, the slayer of Vṛtra, who is celebrated in song.
O guileless gods, grant us a flawless protection,
O Vasus, such that this shelter cannot be assailed from afar or even from near at hand.
For there is kinship with you, O destroyers of enemies; O gods, there is fellowship with you. Proclaim us for former prosperity, and swiftly [proclaim us] for new favor.
Now indeed I have sent forth this praise for you, now for the sharing of wealth—
O possessors of all knowledge, I, bowing in homage, have released it unto you like another [stream].
Up has risen for you that Savitṛ, the excellent leader, the one to be chosen; he stands upright.
Bipeds and quadrupeds, seeking their goals, have settled down, as have the winged birds.
God after god we invoke for your protection; god after god we call upon for our aid.
Singing with divine prayer, we invoke god after god for the winning of the spoil.
For all the gods, being of one mind with Manu, have granted their gifts together;
may they today and in the future be finders of wide space for our progeny.
I proclaim before you, O guileless ones, this assembly of hymns of praise.
No harm, O Varuṇa and Mitra, reaches that mortal who honors your divine ordinances.
He who offers gifts according to your will extends his dwelling and increases great nourishments;
he is propagated with offspring according to the cosmic law, and, remaining unharmed, he prospers in every way.
Without conflict he wins battles; he travels his paths by easy ways—he whom Aryaman, Mitra, and Varuṇa, acting in concert, protect with their bounty.
Even on level ground, you provide him a downward slope; even in difficult terrain, you create a smooth passage for him.
May this very thunderbolt go far away from him and perish, failing its mark.
O you who possess dear dominion, whatever truth (*ṛta*) you establish today when the sun rises, O all-knowing ones— whether at sunset, at dawn, or at midday of the sky.
Or when, O Asuras, at the arrival [of the day], you grant protection to the one who follows the *ṛta* and to the donor;
O Vasus, possessors of all wealth, may we abide in the midst of that [protection] of yours.
Whatever good you bestow today upon Manu when the sun has risen, at midday, or at its setting— O possessors of all wealth, you who have offered oblations for the sake of the wise and perceptive one.
O sovereign lords, we choose from you that protection which is like a son’s, providing much succor;
O Ādityas, may we, offering the oblation, attain that through which we may reach greater prosperity.
The thirty-three gods who have sat upon the sacrificial grass— may they indeed find us and sit down twice over.
Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, and the Agnis who bestow gifts together, accompanied by their wives and consecrated with the cry of *vaṣaṭ*.
May they be our guardians from the west,
from the north, from below, and likewise from the east, together with their entire host.
As the gods desire, so shall it be; no one at all diminishes this of theirs—not even a hostile mortal.
The seven have seven spears; seven are their splendors; they have assumed seven glories.
The one tawny, versatile, noble, and youthful [Soma] puts on his golden ornament.
One, the radiant and wise one, has sat within the womb among the gods.
One, firm among the gods, bears an iron axe in his hand.
One bears the thunderbolt placed in his hand; with it, he strikes down the Vṛtras.
One bears a sharp weapon in his hand; he is pure, fierce, and possesses healing medicines.
One man swells his wealth on the road like a thief; he alone knows of hidden treasures.
The Wide-Strider has taken three steps, where the gods rejoice.
The two move with their birds, one together with another; they dwell as if on a journey.
The two supreme sovereigns, who drink the clarified butter, have established their most excellent seat in heaven.
Some, chanting, conceived the great *sāman*; by means of it, they caused the sun to shine.
For among you, O gods, there is no one who is small, nor any who is a child; all of you are indeed great.
Thus have you been praised, O destroyers of enemies, you who are the thirty-three gods of Manu, worthy of sacrifice.
Do you protect us; do you help us; do you speak for us. Do not lead us far away from the ancestral path of Manu into distant realms.
O you gods who are present here, all you Vaiśvānaras,
grant us wide protection for our cattle and our horses.
He who sacrifices, has sacrificed, will sacrifice, and prepares the oblation—
he, as a priest, has found favor with Indra.
Whoever offers him the sacrificial cake and the pressed Soma mixed with milk—
Śakra indeed delivers such a person from distress.
His chariot shall be radiant, impelled by the gods, and he shall flourish,
overcoming all hostile powers.
In his house, the prolific and inexhaustible *iḷā*, rich in milch-cows, yields her milk day after day.
O Gods, those husband and wife who, being of one mind, press and wash [the Soma] with the constant mixture;
Facing each other, they sit together upon the sacrificial grass;
they do not falter in the contests for booty.
They do not withhold their favor even from the gods; they do not seek to conceal it; they strive to win great renown.
Possessing sons and possessing daughters, they enjoy the full span of life; both are adorned with golden ornaments.
May the two who accept the oblation, having bestowed wealth, grant their favor for the sake of the immortal;
may they strike down the hairy udder and perform service among the gods.
We choose the protection of the mountains and of the rivers;
we choose that of Viṣṇu, who dwells together with them.
May Pūṣan come, may wealth, and Bhaga come for our well-being—he who bestows all things; may the broad path lead to our welfare.
The unassailable Aramati, with the mind of every god,
is the one who is free from reproach among the Ādityas.
Just as Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa are our protectors,
so may the paths of Ṛta be easy to traverse.
I praise with song Agni for you— the ancient god among the Vasus—
serving him who is beloved by many, like Mitra, the one who establishes us in our fields.
Swift is the chariot of the one who favors the gods, like a hero in any battle whatsoever;
he who, as a sacrificer, strives to win the mind of the gods, shall surely overcome those who do not sacrifice.
O sacrificer, you shall not come to harm; O presser of the juice, nor you who are devoted to the gods.
He who, as a sacrificer, strives to win the hearts of the gods, shall surely prevail over those who do not sacrifice.
No one shall overtake him by his ritual act, nor shall he be left behind;
he who, as a sacrificer, strives to win the minds of the gods, shall indeed surpass those who do not sacrifice.
In this there shall be great heroic power, and that excellence of swift horses;
for he who, as a sacrificer, strives to win the mind of the gods, shall surely prevail over those who do not sacrifice.
O Kaṇvas, proclaim the deeds of the impetuous Indra with a song, while he is exhilarated by the soma.
He who, fierce, slew Sṛbinda, Anarśani, Pipru, the Dāsa Ahīśuva, and released the waters.
O Indra, you have struck down the lofty height and the dwelling-place of the great Arbuda; you have performed that manly deed.
Boldly, like a torrent rushing down from a mountain, I call upon the one with the beautiful helmet for your hearing and for his protection.
Rejoicing for the sake of those who offer Soma, O hero, you burst open the stall of cattle and horses as if it were a fortress.
If you have taken pleasure in my pressed juice or if you find delight in my hymn, come from afar according to your own nature.
O Indra, lover of songs, we indeed belong to you as your praisers;
O drinker of Soma, quicken us.
And bring us food, O bounteous one, bestowing upon us that which is inexhaustible; for abundant is your wealth, O Maghavan.
And make us possessors of cattle, of gold, and of horses;
may we grasp them firmly with our invocations.
We invoke Bṛhaduktha, whose hand is swift, for our protection—
he who acts effectively for our aid.
Even when the battle is joined, he of a hundred powers, the slayer of Vṛtra, rich in many treasures, makes these gifts for his singers.
May he, the powerful Śakra, indeed be able to help us— he who brings the Dānavas within his grasp— Indra, with all his aids.
Sing forth to that Indra, who is a great river of wealth, easy to cross, and the friend of the one who presses the soma.
To him who comes as a great and steadfast protector, victorious in battles through his fame,
the lord of abundance by his might.
No one is the restrainer of his powers, nor of his gracious gifts;
no one can say, "He does not give."
Surely there is no debt owed to the zealous priests who press the Soma;
the Soma has not been drunk in vain.
Sing to him who is worthy of praise; recite hymns to him who is worthy of praise; offer prayers to him who is worthy of praise.
The praiseworthy, unimpeded, and vigorous Indra, who is the increaser of the sacrificer, has shattered hundreds and thousands [of obstacles].
Go forth indeed according to your own will toward the invocations of the people;
O Indra, drink of the pressed juices!
Drink, O Indra, of the naturally flowing milks, both those that were with Tugrya and this one which is yours.
Pass by the one who utters insults while pressing the juice for his own enjoyment; drink this offered libation that has been pressed.
Go to the three distant realms; go beyond the five peoples, O Indra, looking toward the lowing cows.
As the sun sends forth its ray, so may my songs draw you hither,
like waters flowing together toward the lowlands.
O Adhvaryu, pour out the Soma for the hero with the handsome jaws;
bring the pressed juice for his drinking.
He who split the water-cask, who sent the rivers downward,
and who placed the cooked [milk] among the cattle.
O you who are worthy of praise, you slew Vṛtra, Aurṇavābha, and Ahīśuva;
with frost, you struck down Arbuda.
Sing forth the prayer bestowed by the gods to your fierce, formidable, unconquerable, and all-subduing one.
Indra, who among the gods takes heed of all sacred ordinances in the exhilaration of Soma’s juice, [is the one].
Hither let these two bay steeds, companions at the feast, with golden manes, carry you toward the prepared food.
O you who are praised by many, may the two bay steeds, lauded by the Priyamedhas,
bring you hither to drink the Soma.
O Vṛtra-slayer, we who have pressed the soma and spread the sacrificial grass, like waters, sit around you as your praisers at the outpourings of the filter.
O Vasu, when the Soma is pressed, the men who offer hymns sing out to you alone;
O Indra, when will you come to the pressed juice, thirsting for it as to your home, like a bellowing bull?
O bold one, with the Kaṇvas, do thou boldly strike out thousandfold booty; O Maghavan, O far-seeing one, we quickly implore thee for that wealth which is golden-hued and rich in cattle.
O Medhyātithi, protect the songs for Indra at the exhilaration of the soma-juice—
he who is joined with his two bay steeds, who is present at the pressed juice, the wielder of the thunderbolt, whose chariot is golden.
He who is excellent on the left and excellent on the right, the lord praised for his noble wisdom;
he who is the source of thousands, whose wealth consists of hundreds, Indra, who is honored as the breaker of fortresses.
He who is bold, he who is unrestrained, he who dwells upon his beard— possessing far-reaching splendor, the shaker, much-praised, mighty in will like a bull.
Who knows him as he drinks at the pressed juice? What vital power does he bestow?
It is he who, exhilarated by the soma-plant, shatters the fortresses with his might, O fair-cheeked one.
Like a wild elephant at the time of rutting, he has assumed his course in many places. No one can hold you back; come to the pressed juice! You move as a great one by your own might.
He who is fierce, unsubdued, firm, and prepared for battle—
if Maghavan Indra hears the call of the singer, he will not stay away but will come.
Truly, you are thus a bull; with a bull’s impulse, you are our unobstructed protector.
For you, O fierce one, are heard of as a bull in the distance, and as a bull you are renowned nearby.
O Maghavan, your reins are bulls; the golden whip is a bull. The chariot is a bull, O Maghavan, and the two bay steeds are bulls; you yourself, O Śatakratu, are a bull.
O Bull, let the presser press for you; O Bull, O you who possess the straight-flowing stalk, bring [the Soma]!
The Bull has flowed into the rivers for you, O driver of the two bay steeds.
O most powerful Indra, come for the drinking of the sweet Soma;
may this bountiful one, possessed of excellent wisdom, hear our songs, our sacred prayers, and our hymns of praise.
Let the bay steeds yoked to the chariot carry you, who stand upon the chariot;
O Vṛtra-slayer, O Śatakratu, pass even beyond the libations of the noble one, those of others.
O most magnificent one, accept our hymn today as your closest;
may our libations be most soothing for your exhilaration, O celestial drinker of Soma.
For neither in your teaching nor in mine, nor in that of another, does he find delight—
O Hero, who has brought us here.
Even Indra himself has said this: "The mind of a woman is impossible to control;
indeed, her resolve is fickle."
Even the two steeds, exhilarated by the intoxicating draught, draw the chariot as a pair;
even so is the yoke of the bull placed above.
Look downward, not upward; keep your feet close together. Let them not see your calves, for you have become a Brahmin woman.
O Indra, come hither with your bay steeds to the beautiful hymn of Kaṇva;
from that heaven you rule, you have gone to heaven, O you who dwell in light.
May the Soma-pressing stone, speaking here with its sound, draw you hither—
from that heaven which rules over heaven— O you who go to heaven, O you whose wealth is light!
Here their rim strikes out like a wolf shaking its breast;
by the command of yonder heaven, you have gone to heaven, O ye who dwell in light!
The Kaṇvas call upon you here for protection and for the winning of booty;
O you who rule from yonder heaven, you who have gone to heaven, O Divāvasu!
I offer to you, the bull, the first draught of the pressed juices, as one who rules from yonder heaven;
go to heaven, O you whose wealth is light!
Come to us with your wisdom, O you who are mindful of our cities; come for our protection from every side, O you who rule over that heaven, you who have gone to heaven, O Lord of Radiant Wealth!
Come to us, O most mighty one, with a thousandfold strength and hundredfold wealth;
from the command of yonder heaven, you who go to heaven, O Divāvasu!
May the Hotṛ priest, established by Manu and worthy of praise among the gods, bring you hither— from that heaven where you rule, O you who dwell in heaven, O Lord of Radiant Wealth.

May your two bay steeds, dripping with exhilaration, carry you hither like two wings carrying a hawk—from that very heaven, by the command of Heaven, O you who dwell in light! O you whose wealth is the day! Come to the heavens.
Come from afar, O noble one; Svāhā! For the drinking of the Soma.
From the command of yonder heaven, come to heaven, O you who are rich in light!
Come to us, having heard our call; take delight here in our hymns! O you who rule from yonder heaven, you who went to heaven, O Divāvasu!
Come to us with well-provided teams of like form, O you whose horses are well-groomed;
from the command of that heaven, come to heaven, O Divāvasu!
Come from the mountains, from the expanse above the ocean;
come from that heaven, O you who rule over heaven, O you whose wealth is light, you who have gone to heaven.
O Hero, burst open for us thousands of cattle and horses—
from that heaven which you rule, O you who go to heaven, O Lord of the Dawn!
Bring to us thousands, tens of thousands, and hundreds from that yonder heaven, O you who rule over heaven, you who go to heaven, O Lord of Radiant Wealth!
When Indra and I have received a thousand from Vasurocis—
the most powerful herd of horses— then...
Those steeds, straight-flying with the speed of the wind, ruddy and swift-moving,
shine like suns.
Standing in the midst of the forest, amidst the gifts of the Pārāvata, with swift, rolling wheels.
Together with Agni, Indra, Varuṇa, Viṣṇu, the Ādityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus;
being of one accord with Uṣas and Sūrya, O Aśvins, drink the soma.
With all our prayers, with the world, O possessors of vigor, together with heaven, earth, and the mountains,
in harmony with the Dawn and with Sūrya, drink the Soma, O Aśvins!
O Aśvins, together with all the gods—the thrice eleven—here with the waters, the Maruts, and the Bhṛgus; being of one accord with Uṣas and Sūrya, drink the soma.
May you two enjoy the sacrifice; be mindful of my invocation. O two gods, come here to all the libations.
Being of one accord with Uṣas and Sūrya, O Aśvins, bring us nourishment.
May you two enjoy this hymn like a youth with a maiden; O all-pervading gods, come here to our libations.
Being of one mind with Uṣas and Sūrya, O Aśvins, bring us nourishment.
O Aśvins, may you enjoy our songs; may you enjoy the sacrifice. O two gods, come here to all the pressings. Being of one mind with Uṣas and Sūrya, bring us nourishment, O Aśvins.
Like two *hāridrava* birds you fly toward the forest; like two buffaloes you descend to the pressed *soma*.
In harmony with Uṣas and Sūrya, O Aśvins, come three times on your circuit.
Like two swans you fly, like travelers on the road; like two buffaloes you descend to the pressed Soma.
In harmony with Uṣas and Sūrya, O Aśvins, come three times to our dwelling.
Like two hawks you fly for the giving of the oblation; like two buffaloes, you descend to the pressed Soma. In harmony with Uṣas and with Sūrya, O Aśvins, come three times on your circuit.
Drink and satisfy yourselves; come hither and bestow progeny and bestow wealth. Being of one mind with Uṣas and Sūrya, O Aśvins, grant us nourishment.
Conquer and be praised; protect us and bestow progeny;
grant us wealth, O Aśvins, being of one mind with Uṣas and Sūrya, and grant us vigor.
Slay the enemies and strengthen those who are our friends; bestow upon us progeny and bestow wealth.
Being of one mind with Uṣas and Sūrya, O Aśvins, grant us nourishment.
Accompanied by Mitra and Varuṇa, and by Dharma, and by the Maruts, come to the call of the singer.
Being of one mind with Uṣas and Sūrya, come, O Aśvins, together with the Ādityas.
Accompanied by the Aṅgirases, by Viṣṇu, and by the Maruts, come to the call of the singer;
O Aśvins, being of one mind with Uṣas, Sūrya, and the Ādityas, come hither.
O Ashvins, rich in *ṛbhus*, powerful bulls, accompanied by the Maruts and by strength, come to the call of the singer;
being of one mind with Ushas and Surya, come with the Adityas, O Ashvins!
Quicken the sacred word and quicken our thoughts; slay the demons and drive away diseases. O Aśvins, being of one mind with Uṣas and Sūrya, [protect] the one who presses the Soma.
Quicken the ruling power and quicken the men; slay the demons and drive away diseases.
O Aśvins, being of one mind with the Dawn and with Sūrya, [protect] the one who presses the Soma.
Quicken the milch-cows and quicken the people; slay the demons and drive away diseases. O Aśvins, being of one mind with Uṣas and Sūrya, [protect] the one who presses the Soma.
O Aśvins, like those of Atri, hear the ancient praise of Śyāvāśva, the presser of the soma that distills exhilaration; being of one mind with Uṣas and Sūrya, come across the day.
Like two creators fashioning streams, O Aśvins, who are exhilarated by the intoxicating draughts of Śyāvāśva as he presses the juice— being in harmony with Uṣas and Sūrya— come from across the day.
Like reins, hold fast the sacrificial rites of Śyāvāśva as he presses the juice, O you who flow with exhilaration; being of one accord with Uṣas and Sūrya, O Aśvins, come from beyond the day.
Drive your chariot hither; drink the Soma-sweetness.
Come, O Aśvins, arrive! Seeking your aid, I invoke you both; bestow treasures upon the donor.
When the sacrifice has been set forth with the cry of "homage," O Heroes, come for the drinking of the exhilarating draught!
Come hither, O Aśvins; approach! Seeking your aid, I invoke you both; bestow riches upon the donor.
O two gods, sate yourselves with the pressed soma-juice consecrated by the cry of Svāhā!
Come hither, O Aśvins; approach! Seeking your aid, I invoke you both; bestow riches upon the donor.
You are the protector of the one who presses the juice and spreads the sacrificial grass; drink the Soma for exhilaration, O Śatakratu!
You whom they have set apart as your portion—you who conquer all hostile armies, whose course is wide, who win the waters, Indra accompanied by the Maruts, Lord of the Good—[drink the Soma].

Protect the singer, O Maghavan; protect yourself. Drink the Soma for exhilaration, O Śatakratu, you who have established that portion for yourself which they have set apart—O Indra, Lord of the Good, accompanied by the Maruts, conqueror of all armies, wide-striding, winner of the waters.
With nourishment, O God, protect the gods; with might, drink the Soma for exhilaration, O Śatakratu!
You who have established that portion for yourself, overcoming all hostile armies, wide-ranging, winning the waters—O Indra, Lord of the Maruts, Lord of the Good!
The progenitor of heaven, the progenitor of earth—O Śatakratu, drink the Soma for exhilaration!

You who have established that portion which is yours, overcoming all hostile armies with your wide-reaching stride, O Indra, Lord of the Good, accompanied by the Maruts, you are the winner of the waters.
You are the progenitor of horses, the progenitor of cattle; O Śatakratu, drink the Soma for exhilaration!

You who have established that portion which they have set apart for you—you, the conqueror of all hostile armies, the wide-striding one, the winner of waters with the Maruts—O Indra, Lord of the Good, [drink].
O Lord of the Stone, make great the hymn of the Atris; drink the Soma for exhilaration, O Śatakratu!
You who have established that portion for yourself, conquering all hostile armies, you of wide range, winner of the waters—O Indra, Lord of the Maruts, Lord of the Good!
Listen likewise to Śyāvāśva as he presses the juice, just as you listened to Atri while he performed his rites;
O Indra, you alone aided Trasadasyu in the subduing of men, strengthening him with sacred prayers.

O Indra, Lord of Might, you have favored this prayer in the battles against Vṛtra; with all your aids, O slayer of Vṛtra, blameless wielder of the thunderbolt, drink of the Soma at the midday libation.
O fierce Indra, Lord of Might, overcoming the hostile armies with all your aids,
O Vṛtra-slayer, blameless wielder of the thunderbolt, drink of the Soma at the midday libation.
O sole ruler of this world, you reign, O Indra, Lord of Might, with all your aids.
O slayer of Vṛtra, blameless wielder of the thunderbolt, drink of the Soma at the midday libation.
O sole lord of power, Indra, you alone, accompanied by your hosts, separate [the enemies] with all your aids.
O Vṛtra-slayer, blameless wielder of the thunderbolt, drink of the Soma at the midday libation.
O Lord of Might, O Indra, you are the master of both security and exertion through all your aids;
O slayer of Vṛtra, O blameless wielder of the thunderbolt, drink of the Soma at the midday libation.
You have helped the ruling power, yet you have not helped us, O Lord of Might, Indra, with all your aids.
O Slayer of Vṛtra, blameless wielder of the thunderbolt, drink of the Soma at the midday libation.
Listen likewise to the chanting of Śyāvāśva as he performs his rites, just as you listened to Atri when he performed his deeds.
O Indra, you alone have protected Trasadasyu in the struggle for men, increasing his sovereign powers.
For you two are the officiating priests of the sacrifice, the winners in contests and ritual acts;
O Indra and Agni, take heed of that!
O bounteous ones, who travel in your chariot, slayers of Vṛtra, unconquered—
O Indra and Agni, take heed of this!
O Indra and Agni, the men have pressed this exhilarating honey-sweet mead for you with the stones; take heed of it!
May you both enjoy the sacrifice for its fulfillment; O Indra and Agni, heroes who share the same praise, come to the pressed Soma!
O Indra and Agni, heroes, may you take pleasure in these libations by which you have carried away the offerings; come hither!
O Indra and Agni, heroes, come to this well-praised hymn of mine, which follows the path of the Gāyatrī.
Come with the gods who travel at dawn, O lords of noble wealth,
Indra and Agni, for the drinking of the Soma.
O Indra and Agni, hear the invocation of Śyāvāśva as he presses the juice, and that of the Atris, for the drinking of the Soma.
Thus have I called you both for aid, just as the wise sages have called,
O Indra and Agni, for the drinking of the Soma.
I choose the protection of Indra and Agni, who are accompanied by Sarasvatī—
those two for whom the Gāyatra hymn is chanted.
I have praised Agni, the one worthy of hymns; I shall worship Agni with the *īḍā* invocation.
May Agni anoint the gods for us, for as a seer he moves between both assemblies on his mission as messenger. May all others, the base ones, perish!
O Agni, with our newest speech, suppress the praise of these men within their own bodies;
cast down the hostilities of the hostile, and let all the enmities of the enemy depart from here. Let the non-givers perish; let all others who are equal to them be destroyed.
O Agni, we offer these prayers to you like clarified butter into your mouth;
make them known among the gods, for you are the ancient, auspicious messenger of Vivasvat. Let all others perish!

Agni bestows that very vital power upon him, in whatever manner he prays; as an oblation of strength for the Vasus, he bestows well-being, prosperity, and joy for every invocation of the gods. Let all others perish!
He has been perceived through his most powerful and wondrous deed;
he is the Hotṛ-priest of all the eternal ones, encompassed by sacrificial fees. He impels that which is to be offered. May all others, however numerous they may be, perish!
Agni knows the births of the gods; Agni knows the secret of mortals.
Agni is the giver of wealth; Agni, when invoked with the newest [hymn], throws open the doors. Let all others, however many they be, perish!
Agni dwells among the gods; he dwells among the clans worthy of sacrifice.
With joy, that god, worshipful among the gods, nourishes many poetic insights as if with the whole earth. May all others, the base ones, perish!

The Agni who dwells among the seven human tribes and in all the rivers—to him we have come, to the one with three dwellings, the greatest slayer of Dasyus for Mandhātṛ, the ancient Agni at the sacrifices. May all others, however, perish!
Agni, the sage, dwells in the three triadic domains of the sacrifice;
may he, the inspired priest and our well-adorned messenger, worship and satisfy here the thrice eleven gods. May all others, the base ones, be destroyed.
O Agni, you alone rule over wealth among our people and among the gods, O Primordial One;
the waters flowing around you move along their own channels. May all others who are equal to them perish!

O Indra and Agni, you two, as conquerors, bestow wealth upon us well—that wealth by which we may overcome even the firm and solid [enemies] in battles, just as Agni consumes the forests with the wind. May all others who are equal [to us] be destroyed!
For we do not exclude you two; rather, we worship Indra alone, the most powerful hero among men.
May he come to us at any time with his steed for the winning of booty; may he come for the winning of wisdom. Let all others, however, perish!
For Indra and Agni dwell as lords over the midst of the offerings;
they, the two sages, being questioned with wisdom, bestow the gathered thought upon him who seeks their friendship, O heroes. Let all others perish!
Sing forth with a sacrificial song to Indra and Agni, as Nabhaka did;
they for whom this entire world and this vast heaven and earth bear wealth within their lap. May all others, the insignificant ones, perish!
Offer prayers like Nabhaka unto Indra and Agni;
they who have uncovered the ocean with its sevenfold bottom and its downward-opening gate—Indra, ruling by his might—let all others, however great, be shattered.
Tear it away as of old, like the tangled growth of a creeping vine; strike down the power of the Dāsa.
May we, together with Indra, divide that accumulated wealth of his. Let all others perish, even the lowly ones!

O Indra and Agni, when these people invoke you with various songs, may we, through our own men, overcome those who attack us and conquer those who seek to vanquish us; let all others perish, even the lowly ones.

The two white ones that rise from the sky with their splendors day by day—following the ordinance of Indra and Agni, the rivers flow forth as they are released from their bond. May all others who are base be destroyed!
Many are your aids, O Indra, and many are your praises, O Son of the Impeller, Lord of the Bay Steeds!
May the riches of the hero be unconfined; may our prayers now be fulfilled. Let all others who are base perish!

Sharpen him with well-fashioned hymns—the brilliant warrior worthy of praise—who indeed by his might shatters the eggs of Śuṣṇa; may he win the water-laden waters. May all others, the insignificant, be destroyed!
Sharpen him, the true one, the warrior of the seasons, who performs the perfect sacrifice;
he who indeed brings down the testicles of Śuṣṇa and wins the sunlit waters with his goats. May all others who are equal to him be destroyed!
Thus, for Indra and Agni, a new song has been proclaimed, like that of the fathers, like Māndhātṛ, and like Aṅgiras.
With your triple-layered protection, guard us; may we be masters of riches.
To him, for his great power—to Varuṇa and the Maruts, who are most wise—I sing praise;
he who protects the thoughts of men as one guards cattle. May all others, the insignificant ones, be destroyed!

Him indeed we celebrate with a common song and with the hymns of our fathers, with the praises of Nābhāka—him who dwells at the source of the rivers, he whose seven sisters are his companions; may all others, the base ones, perish!
He has embraced the nights; by his creative power he has established the dawns. He is visible all around.
Following his law, the three dawns have increased his two beloved ones. May all others who are base perish!

He who established the quarters upon the earth, he who is beautiful to behold—he is the mother of the ancient station; that is the domain of Varuṇa, for he is the guardian, like a noble steed. May all others, however, be destroyed!

He who is the upholder of the worlds, who knows the secret and hidden names of the dawns—he, the seer, nourishes many poetic visions like the sky with its manifold forms. May all others, the insignificant ones, perish!

In whom all poetic insights are centered as if upon a nave—honor Trita with your impulse! Like cattle in a pen, they have harnessed their horses for union; may all others perish, however great they be!

He who lies upon their garment, encompassing all their births, and touching all the domains of Varuṇa within his own dwelling—all the gods follow his ordinance. Let all others, the base ones, be destroyed.
He, the secret ocean, swift as heaven, ascends when he places the sacrificial formula (*yajus*) within these [waters].
With his flaming foot, he has scattered the illusions and ascended to the firmament. May all others, the lowly ones, perish!

He whose white, far-seeing [rays] have overspread the three earths, and who thrice filled the higher realms—he, the firm seat of Varuṇa, rules over the seven; let all others, however many they be, be destroyed.

He who, according to his laws, made the white one his upper garment and the black one his lower, he measured out the ancient abode; by his pillar he propped apart heaven and earth as the Unborn supported the sky. May all others, the petty ones, perish!
The all-knowing Asura propped up the sky; he measured out the breadth of the earth.
As sovereign lord, he took his seat over all worlds—all these are the ordinances of Varuṇa.
Thus do thou praise the lofty Varuṇa; pay homage to the wise guardian of immortality.
May he grant us a triple-layered shelter; may Heaven and Earth protect us in their lap.
O God Varuṇa, sharpen this prayer of one who strives for it; sharpen our will and skill.
May we mount the well-oared boat by which we may cross over all difficulties.
O Aśvins, the pressing-stones and the inspired singers have, through their prayers, caused you both to hasten hither for the drinking of the Soma, O Nāsatyas. May all others who are base perish!
Just as the sage Atri invoked you both with songs, O Aśvins,
for the drinking of Soma, O Nāsatyas— let all others who are base perish!
Thus have I called upon you both for aid, as the wise sages have called, O Nāsatyas, for the drinking of the Soma; let all others who are base perish!
These songs and hymns of the inspired sage, the wise Agni, who performs the sacrifice unimpeded, go forth.
To you, O Jātavedas, who are far-seeing and take delight in this [praise],
O Agni, I generate a beautiful hymn of praise.
Truly, O Agni, your sharp flames are like rays of light;
with your teeth you devour the forests.
The bay steeds, smoke-bannered and impelled by the wind, strive separately toward heaven like fires.
These various fires, once kindled, have appeared together like the banners of the dawns.
Black dust rises from the feet at the departure of Jātavedas,
when Agni spreads across the earth.
Making the plants his food and devouring them, Agni does not grow weary,
even as he goes back again to the young ones.
Bowing down with his tongues and flickering with his flame,
Agni shines resplendent among the forests.
O Agni, your seat is in the waters; you penetrate the plants, and being in their womb, you are born again.
O Agni, that flame of yours, when offered with clarified butter, has shone forth,
kissing the sacrificial ladles at its mouth.
To Agni, the ordainer, whose food is the bull and the cow, who bears Soma upon his back— to him we shall offer worship with hymns of praise.
And we, O Hotṛ of most excellent wisdom, approach you with homage, O Agni, with kindled fuel.
And we invoke you, O pure Agni, who are offered oblations, like Bhr̥gu, like Manu,
and like Aṅgiras.
For you, O Agni, are kindled by fire; as a sage by a sage, being what you are, you are kindled as a friend by a friend.
As such, O Agni, grant to the inspired singer who offers oblations thousandfold wealth and nourishment accompanied by heroic sons.
O Agni, brother, born of strength, with ruddy horses and pure vows,
take pleasure in this hymn of mine.
And may my praise, O Agni, reach you as cows seek the stall for a lowing calf that longs for them.
To you, O best of Angirases, all these well-settled people have turned separately, O Agni, out of desire for you.
The wise, the intelligent, and the inspired singers have, with their thoughts, impelled Agni to sit at the feast.
O Agni, those who extend the sacrifice invoke you— the swift steed in the races, the bearer, the invoker.
For you are the same in many places, the lord over all the tribes;
we invoke you in the battles.
Praise him who, when invoked with offerings of clarified butter, Agni shines forth brilliantly;
may he hear this our invocation.
As such, we invoke you, the attentive Jātavedas,
O Agni, who strikes away our enemies.
I praise this Agni, the king of the people, the wonderful overseer of the laws; may he indeed hear us.
We urge Agni, who stirs all life, like a prize-winning youth set to the race, as we urge a steed to win the prize.
Slaying the obstructors, driving away our enemies, and burning up the *rakṣas* every day,
O Agni, shine forth with your sharp [flame].
O Agni, best of the Aṅgirases, whom the people kindle like Manu— be mindful of my word.
O Agni, whether you are born of heaven or born of the waters, O you who are strengthened by power,
we invoke you with our songs.
For indeed, all these people, these various well-settled communities, send forth nourishment for thee to eat.
O Agni, may those who possess well-studied knowledge and who behold men indeed cross over all days; may we overcome all difficulties.
We implore with our joyful hearts Agni, the delightful one, dear to many, the fierce one with purifying luster.
O Agni, you who are rich in light, like the sun emitting its rays,
you boldly strike down the darknesses.
O powerful one, we beg of you that gift which never fails; from you, O Agni, comes desirable wealth.
Worship Agni with fuel; awaken the guest with offerings of clarified butter;
pour the oblations into him.
O Agni, take pleasure in my hymn; grow strong by this prayer of mine; graciously accept our well-spoken verses.
I place Agni at the forefront as my messenger; I address him, the bearer of oblations, so that he may seat the gods here.
O Agni, your lofty, bright flames rise up as you are kindled and shine forth.
O beloved Agni, let my ladles, dripping with clarified butter, approach you; graciously accept our oblations.
I praise Agni—the delightful invoker, the officiating priest, the one of wondrous luster, the possessor of light; may he indeed hear us.
The ancient Hotṛ, worthy of praise, Agni, beloved and possessed of a seer’s insight,
the glory of the sacrifices.
O Agni, best of the Aṅgirases, enjoying these oblations in due order,
lead the sacrifice according to the seasons.
O kindled one, O truthful one, O bright-flamed one, bring here the divine folk, for you are wise.
We seek the inspired singer, the guileless invoker, whose banner is smoke, the radiant one, the signal of sacrifices.
O Agni, protect us; O God, strike down those who seek to harm us. Shatter our enemies, O you who are born of strength!
Agni, adorning his own body with an ancient hymn,
the sage has grown great through the inspired singer.
I invoke Agni, the Son of Strength, whose radiance is purifying,
at this well-performed sacrifice.
O Agni, you who possess the majesty of Mitra, with your bright flame, sit down upon the sacrificial grass together with the gods for our sake.
The mortal who worships Agni, the god, within his own home—
unto him indeed shall he shine forth wealth.
Agni is the head of heaven, the summit, the lord of this earth;
he quickens the seeds of the waters.
O Agni, your pure, bright, and radiant beams rise upward;
your lights and flames surge forth.
For you, O Agni, Lord of Light, are the master of desirable gifts;
may I be your praiser under your protection.
O Agni, the wise impel you with their thoughts;
may our songs increase you.
We choose the friendship of Agni, who is undeceived, self-dependent, the messenger who ever utters praise.
Agni, whose vows are most pure, is the pure inspired singer, the pure sage; offered with oblations, he shines forth in purity.
And may my meditations and songs increase you at all times; O Agni, be mindful of our friendship.
O Agni, if I were you, or if you indeed were I,
then may your blessings here be fulfilled.
For you, O Agni, are the Vasu, the lord of treasures, and you possess radiant wealth;
may we abide in your benevolence.
O Agni, to you whose vows are firm, our songs of praise rise up like rivers flowing toward the ocean.
I adorn with my prayers Agni— the youthful lord of the people, the seer, the all-eater, and the one who stirs many things.
To Agni, the charioteer of sacrifices, the one with sharp jaws and firm strength— to him we offer nourishment through our hymns of praise.
O Agni, may this singer abide within you, O truthful one;
have mercy upon him, O Purifier.
For you, O Agni, are the steadfast one who sits at the feast, ever watchful like a sage; you shine in the sky.
O Agni, O Sage, before we fall into calamities and before our enemies,
prolong our lifespan, O Vasu.
Truly, those who kindle Agni and spread the sacrificial grass in due order—
those whose youthful Indra is their friend.
Great indeed is their fuel, abundant their praise, and wide their sacrificial post—
those whose youthful Indra is their friend.
Even without fighting, the hero goes forth with his warriors against those who have surrounded him in battle— those whose youthful Indra is their friend.
As soon as he was born, the slayer of Vṛtra took up his bow; he questioned his mother:
"Who are the fierce ones? Who indeed are renowned?"
Śavasī shall speak against you; like one fighting for water on a mountain, she will combat him who seeks enmity toward you.
Moreover, O Maghavan, listen to him who desires it from you; you fulfill that which he seeks. Whatever you make firm, that indeed becomes firm.
When Indra, the maker of battle, goes forth to the fray seeking good horses, he is the best of charioteers among all charioteers.
O wielder of the thunderbolt, utterly drive away all assailants from every side;
be for us the one most rich in glorious renown.
May Indra place our chariot at the front for the sake of victory—
a chariot which the malevolent cannot harm.
May we avoid your enemies; O Śakra, you are ready to give. O Indra, may we go to those who possess cattle.
O wielder of the stone, even when moving slowly, we possess horses and a hundredfold wealth; we are eloquent and free from blemish.
For upward, day after day, do your thousands and hundreds of true gifts rise; you bestow them upon those who sing your praises.
For we know you, O Indra, as the winner of wealth, who breaks even through firm obstacles,
like one who seizes a household.
O Sage, may the bold drops exhilarate you, even though you are preeminent—
when we, as seekers, approach you, the Paṇi.
O wealthy one, bring to us the knowledge of that man who, being stingy, has failed to satisfy you for the sake of bestowing riches.
These Soma-offering friends of yours, O Indra, look toward you,
like those who possess abundance looking for their cattle.
And though you are deaf, we call you from afar here for our protection, you who have ears that hear.
If you should hear this invocation, and if you should perform what is difficult to endure,
then be our closest kinsman.
For even though we have experienced distress when thinking of you,
O Indra, be a giver of cattle to us.
O Lord of Might, we have supported you as the aged support a pillar; we desire you to be present in our dwelling place.
Sing a hymn of praise to Indra, the warrior of many heroic deeds,
whom no one can withstand in battle.
O Bull, I pour out the pressed juice for you to drink;
satisfy yourself and enjoy the exhilaration.
Let not the foolish, seeking to harm you, nor those who mock you, deceive you; do not favor those who hate sacred prayer.
Here let the Soma, rich in cattle, exhilarate you for great bounty;
drink like a wild bull at a lake.
Those ancient and new deeds which the slayer of Vṛtra has performed in the distance—
proclaim them in the assemblies.
Indra drank the pressed juice of Kadru at the thousand-armed [contest];
there he displayed his manly prowess.
That truth is known among Turvaśa and Yadu as something not to be disregarded;
he has accomplished it for the sake of victory in his labor.
I shall praise together for you that common [Indra], the one who carries you across and who bestows booty consisting of cattle upon the people.
Like R̥bhukṣan, you are not to be restrained in our hymns— you, the increaser of Tugra’s son,
Indra— at the pressed Soma.
He who indeed cut apart the broad mountain for Triśoka so that it might open a path for the cattle to go forth from their stall.
Whatever you intend, whatever you meditate upon while exhilarated, and whatever you desire to bestow—do not do that, O Indra; have mercy!
For even a small deed performed by one such as you is heard of upon the earth;
O Indra, let your mind come hither.
These songs of praise and these eulogies are truly yours,
O Indra, since you show us mercy.
Do not slay us for one offense, nor for two, nor even for three; O Hero, do not strike us down for many.
For I am indeed afraid of one such as you, O fierce one, who shatters [the foe] from every side— the wondrous subduer of attackers.
O Lord of abundant wealth, may I not suffer the loss of a friend, nor the loss of a son;
let your mind be turned back toward us.
O men, who indeed, being unprovoked, has spoken thus to a friend: "Who among us is fleeing? 8.45.37cd. Who is it that flees from us?
Thus, O bulls, when the soma is pressed, you who are insatiable have brought many boons,
moving like a gambler toward the winnings.
I seize for you these two bay steeds, yoked by our word, together with the well-faring chariot,
so that you may give them to the Brahmins.
Shatter all enemies, drive away oppressors, and slay the mockers;
bring us that desirable wealth.
O Indra, whatever desirable wealth has been placed within that which is firm, that which is solid, or that which is in the stronghold— bring that hither!
Of you, whose vast gift the entire human race knows,
bring here that desirable wealth.
O Indra, Lord of abundant wealth, we belong to one such as you, our leader; we are yours, O driver of the two bay steeds.
For we know you, O wielder of the stone, to be the true giver of nourishments;
we know you to be the giver of riches.
O you of a hundred aids, O Lord of a hundred powers, whose greatness the poets celebrate with their songs.
Truly, that mortal is well-guided whom the Maruts, Aryaman, and Mitra— free from malice— protect.
Possessing wealth in cattle and horses along with great heroic power, he, impelled by the Ādityas, prospers; he is always enriched with much-desired riches.
We beg that Indra for bounty—him who is powerful and fearless;
we beg him, the lord of wealth.
For in him are all fearless aids combined;
let the bay steeds, the swift coursers, bring that possessor of many riches to the pressed juice for exhilaration.
That exhilaration of yours which is most excellent, O Indra, which is the greatest slayer of Vṛtra;
that which you took up with the men as light, and which is invincible in battles.
O you who are invincible, possessor of all boons, worthy of renown, and the victor in battles—O most powerful one, O Vasu, come to our libations; may we go to a stall filled with cattle.
O most magnificent one, as you did for us in the past, grant us wealth in cattle, horses, and chariots;
bestow upon us wide space.
O Hero, I truly find no end to your bounty;
O Maghavan, wielder of the stone, you have always favored our prayers with spoils of war.
He who is lofty, the friend who makes [his name] heard—he, the much-praised, knows all generations.
All human beings of every age call upon that powerful Indra with uplifted ladles.
May he, the possessor of many riches, the Maghavan, the slayer of Vṛtra, be our protector in battles and our leader from the front.
Sing forth with your song to your hero during the exhilarations of the soma-juice— to the great and wise one, to the famous Indra by name, the powerful one, just as the word commands.
O you who are invoked by many, you have given wealth for the body, you have given riches, and you have given a prize-winning steed in the contests;
even now, indeed.
He who rules over all treasures, who indeed prevails through this very form—
now he truly surpasses those who seek his favor.
We praise you greatly for our sustenance—for the bounteous one who comes readily and moves swiftly.
With sacrifices and songs, you seek to win the favor of the Maruts who are present at all human rites; with reverence and song, I sing to you.
They who cause [the waters] to flow with their rushes over the ridges of the mountains—
[we seek] the sacrifice of those who roar mightily, the favor of those who roar loudly, at the rite.
O most powerful Indra, bring us wealth that shatters the evil-minded, a wealth suited to us, O you who impel the mind— impel the best wealth, O you who impel the mind!
O winner, O excellent winner, O fierce one, O wondrous and most brilliant, O bounteous one!
O sovereign ruler, by thy might, [bring] the victorious, the subduing Bhujyu, the foremost in battles.
May he who, being godless, has taken this much bounty come hither;
even as Vaśa Aśvya took it at the break of dawn for Pṛthuśravas Kānīta.
Sixty thousand [cows] for the horses, ten thousand for the seat, twenty hundred camels;
ten hundred dark-brown mares, ten [hundred] of those with three red spots, and ten thousand cows.
Ten dark bay horses, successful in winning wealth, swift and with flowing manes,
have turned the felly downward by their speed.
The gifts of Pṛthuśravas, the son of Kānīta, who is most bountiful—by giving a golden chariot, he has become the most liberal patron; he has achieved most exalted renown.
O Vāyu, come to us for great continuity, for the sacrifice, and for splendor;
for we have performed much for you to give, even so as to grant great bounty this very day.
He who travels with horses, clothed in the rays of dawn, [master] of thrice seven times seventy [steeds]—
with these soma-pressers and these soma-libations, O Soma-drinker, drinker of the bright and purified juice, come for the sake of giving.
He who himself has gladdened even me, the wonderful one, for the sake of giving—
at Araṭva, at Akṣa, at Nahuṣa, the doer of good deeds, he who is most skillful in action and possesses excellent wisdom.
He who is the self-ruler in the wondrous hymn worthy of praise, and you too, O Vāyu, who bathe in clarified butter—
this impulsion by horses, this impulsion through the mid-air, this impulsion by dogs, that very thing is now here.
Then, for the vigorous one, there was a beloved gift of sixty thousand—
like stallions, indeed like vigorous steeds.
Like a herd of cows, the castrated ones come together; the castrated ones come unto me.
And when he bellowed for a hundred camels in the herd moving along,
and for twenty hundred among the white ones.
A hundred [gifts] the inspired singer Tarukṣa received from Dāsa Balbūtha.
These people here, O Vāyu, rejoice for you; protected by Indra they rejoice, protected by the gods.
Then this great woman, turning toward Vaśa Aśvya, is led forth, adorned with golden ornaments.
Great is the aid that you, the great ones, Varuṇa and Mitra, grant to the donor.
O Ādityas, the evil shall not reach him whom you protect from malice; yours are the aids free from danger, yours are the well-bestowed aids.
O Ādityas, gods, you who know the removal of evils;
like birds spreading their wings above, grant us protection. Unfailing are your aids; well-aiding are your aids.
Spread out that protection over us; fly forth like birds with your wings.
O possessors of all-knowledge, we meditate upon all your secure shelters. Your aids are free from harm; your aids are truly well-bestowed.
To whomsoever the wise ones have granted a dwelling and a means of life—to that man, indeed, all these Ādityas are masters of wealth. Unfailing are your aids; well-aiding are your aids.
May evils avoid us on every side, as a charioteer avoids difficult paths.
May we abide in the protection of Indra and under the favor of the Ādityas; yours are the aids that are free from danger, yours are the aids that are well-bestowed.
The person who avoids the food given by you perishes;
O Gods, Adityas, he whom you have favored has obtained much. Your aids are unfailing; your aids are well-bestowed.
Neither a sharp dart nor a heavy burden shall overcome him whom you, O Ādityas, have granted wide protection; for yours are the blameless aids, yours are the well-aiding aids.
O gods, we belong to you, like warriors in their armor. Protect us from great sin and from small; yours are the aids that bring no harm, yours are the well-bestowing aids.
May Aditi protect us; may Aditi grant us shelter—she who is the mother of Mitra, of the wealthy Aryaman, and of Varuṇa. Your aids are faultless; your aids are well-bestowed.

O Gods, that shelter which is a refuge, that which is auspicious, that which is free from disease, that triple-layered protection—grant all that to us! Unfailing are your aids; well-aiding are your aids.
O Ādityas, look down upon us as spies look over the riverbank;
lead us along a good path, like spirited horses to a fine ford. Your aids are free from danger; your aids are well-bestowed.
There is no blessing here for the one who harbors demons, nor for the one who seeks to harm us, nor even for the one who approaches with malice.
But there is blessing for the cow and for the milch-cow, and for the hero who strives for glory. Unfailing are your aids; well-aiding are your aids.
O Gods, whatever evil deed exists—whether it be manifest or hidden—all that, O Trita Āptya, place far away from us! Your aids are unfailing; your aids are well-bestowing.
Whatever evil dream is among our cattle, and whatever, O Daughter of Heaven, is against us—that, O Radiant One, carry far away to Trita Āptya! Unfailing are your aids; well-aiding are your aids.
Whether they bestow a golden ornament or a garland, O Daughter of Heaven, we entrust all evil dreams to Trita Āptya. Your aids are free from blemish; your aids are truly well-bestowed.
To him who approaches with that food, with that labor, seeking that portion—to Trita and to Dvita—carry away the evil dream! Your aids are unfailing; your aids are well-aiding.

Just as we pay back a sixteenth part, just as an eighth part, just as a debt, so do we pay back all evil dreams upon Āptya; for yours are the aids that bring no harm, yours are the aids that are well-bestowed.
We have conquered today; we have prevailed; we have become free from sin.
O Uṣas, may that evil dream from which we were afraid be dispelled by your light. Free from danger are your aids; auspicious are your aids.
Wise and devout, I have partaken of the sweet food that provides ample space,
of which all the gods and mortals come together, calling it honey.
Passing within, may you become Aditi; may you be the one who averts the divine wrath.
O Indu, enjoying the friendship of Indra, may you succeed toward wealth like a draft-animal following its yoke.
We have drunk Soma; we have become immortal; we have reached the light; we have found the gods.
What can hostility now do to us? And what, O Immortal One, can the malice of a mortal do?
Be gracious to our heart when drunk, O Indu; O Soma, be as kind as a father to his son. Like a friend to a friend, O wise one of wide renown, prolong our life-span, O Soma, that we may live.

These juices, when drunk, bring me glory and deliverance; like oxen harnessed to a chariot, they have bound me together at my joints. May these drops protect me from a fracture of the limbs and keep me far from lameness.
Like fire churned forth, kindle me; grant us vision and make us more prosperous.
For then, O Soma, in your exhilaration, I consider myself like a wealthy man; move forward toward nourishment.
With an eager mind, may we partake of your pressed juice, as if of ancestral wealth. O King Soma, prolong our lifespans, as the sun lengthens the days and the mornings.
O King Soma, be gracious unto us for our well-being; we are your devotees, so take note of that.
O Indu, our skill and our zeal are stirred; do not deliver us over to the will of the enemy.
For you, O Soma, are the guardian of our bodies; as one who beholds men, you have settled within every limb.
If we violate your sacred laws, O God, be gracious to us as a good friend for our ultimate welfare.
May I be united with that friend whose heart is soft, who, when drunk, shall not harm me, O Lord of the Bay Horses.
This Soma which has been placed within us—for its sake I go to Indra to extend my life.
Away have fled those deficiencies and maladies; the darknesses have perished and were struck with fear. Soma has ascended unto us, all-pervading; we have gone to where they prolong our life.
O Fathers, that immortal drop which, when drunk, has entered into the hearts of mortals—for that Soma let us worship with an oblation; may we abide in his mercy and his good favor.
O Soma, you who are in harmony with the Fathers have extended yourself across heaven and earth. To you, O Indu, we pay worship with this oblation; may we become masters of riches.
O protecting gods, speak for us; let neither sleep nor idle chatter master us.
May we, forever dear to Soma, with heroic sons, proclaim our wisdom at the assembly.
O Soma, you are the bestower of vital strength upon us from every side; you, the watcher of men, enter us as the finder of light.
O Indu, being of one mind with us through your aids, protect us from behind and also from the front.
Sing forth to Indra, the giver of goodly gifts, as he is known to you— he, the bounteous lord of many riches, who bestows upon his singers like a thousandfold gift.
Like Śatānīka, he advances boldly; he slays the Vṛtras for the sake of the donor. Like the streams from a mountain, the gifts of him who provides much nourishment overflow.
O Indra, lover of songs, may the pressed Soma drops, which are intoxicating, come to you;
O hero, wielder of the thunderbolt, they fill you for the sake of bounty, as waters fill a lake that is their home.
Drink this most sweet honey, which is faultless, furthering, and eloquent;
so that, being exhilarated, you may bestow upon us gifts boldly of your own accord, as if toward small things.
Come swiftly toward our hymn of praise, like a horse urged by its drivers;
O self-dependent Indra, the milch-cows provide for you that which the Kanvas offer as gifts.

Like a fierce hero, we have approached you with homage—you, the pervasive one whose wealth is inexhaustible. O wielder of the thunderbolt, like water poured from a well, our prayers flow forth toward you, O Indra.
Whether you are now [here], or at the sacrifice, or upon the earth— from that place,
O great-minded one, come to our sacrifice with your swift and fierce steeds, O fierce one!
Thy swift bay steeds, which are fleet and impetuous like the winds—
with them thou goest around the offspring of Manu, and with them all the light of heaven to behold.
For this much of thy bovine favor we entreat thee, O Indra:
just as thou didst protect Medhyātithi, O Maghavan, and as thou didst protect Nīpātithi in the contest for wealth.
As you did for Kaṇva, O Maghavan, for Trasadasyu, for Paktha Daśavraja, and as you were present for Gośarya Ṛjiśvan, so, O Indra, grant us wealth in cattle and gold.
Sing forth for our assistance to the renowned Śakra,
the bounteous giver, who bestows desirable wealth upon the one who presses the Soma and praises him, as if with a thousandfold gift.

The weapons of this Indra are hundredfold and invincible; his great impetuous powers swell like a mountain rich in nourishment for the sake of the bounteous patrons, when the pressed juices have exhilarated him.
When the pressed drops have exhilarated him for his beloved [friend], then, O Vasu, the libation has been established for me like waters; it flows for the donor like milch-cows.
For you, the faultless one, invoked for aid, our prayers flow like streams of honey.
O Vasu, the Soma drops, being invoked, have been set near you at our hymns of praise.
Come to us at our Soma sacrifice, O performer of good rites; hastening like a courser, you bestow your gifts.
You, whom your own praises delight as they offer them to you, O giver of wealth—you take pleasure in the invocation of the worshipper.

Forward [I call] the fierce hero, the separator, the winner of wealth, the lord of great bounty. Like a well from a spring, O wielder of the thunderbolt, you have ever overflowed with riches for the donor.
Whether you are now in the far distance, or upon the earth, or in heaven— O Indra, great-souled one, harnessing your bay steeds, come hither with your lofty companions.
Your bay steeds, swift as charioteers and tireless, surpass the vigor of the wind;
with them you strike down the Dasyu from men, and with them you encompass the sun.
O Vasu, O Hero, may we recognize as much of this from you as something ever new, so that you might protect Etaśa in the decisive contest for wealth, and Vaśa in Daśavraja.
As you did for Kaṇva at the sacrifice, O Maghavan, in the rite of Dīrghanītha the householder;
as you did for Gośarya, O wielder of the stone, so may you bestow upon me a wealth of cattle, resplendent with bay horses.
Just as you, O Indra, drank the pressed Soma with Manu Sāṃvaraṇi,
so too, O Maghavan, [you drank it] with Nīpātithi, Medhyātithi, Puṣṭigu, and Śruṣṭigu.
Pārṣadvāṇa established Praskaṇva— who was lying there,
worn out and cast aside— the R̥ṣi, protected by you, won thousands of cattle from Dasyave Vr̥ka.
He who does not find [satisfaction] through hymns, yet is wise and the inspirer of seers—
to that Indra speak with a new song, like one seeking to provide for a guest who is free from harm.
To him for whom they have chanted the seven-headed hymn, three-layered, in the highest station—he, indeed, has roared through all these worlds; from him, manly power was born.
Him who is the giver of riches to us, that Indra we invoke;
for we know his most recent favor—may we go to a stall full of cattle.
O Vasu, he for whom you strive to grant a gift attains an abundance of wealth.
O Indra, Maghavan, lover of songs, we, having pressed the Soma, invoke you.
Never art thou barren, O Indra; never dost thou fail the worshipper.
More and more, O Maghavan, does thy divine bounty increase.
He who has reached out with his might against Krivi, making *Śuṣṇa* cry out with his weapons;
when he propped up and spread out that heaven, then indeed was the earthly one born.
He whose every nobleman and Dāsa servant is a protector of his treasure— though he be far away among the Aryas or the Ruśamas, that wealth is driven toward you alone.
The inspired singers, hastening, have sung their hymn of praise, rich in sweetness and dripping with clarity.
For us, wealth and manly strength have spread abroad; for us, the pressed Soma drops flow.
O Śakra, just as you drank the pressed soma when Manu Vivasvat was king,
and just as you, O Indra, took pleasure in the hymn at Trita’s place, so do you rejoice together with Āyu.
O Indra, you rejoiced in the pressed juice when Pṛṣadhra, Medhya, and Mātariśvan were pressing it—
just as you did with Soma at the hands of Daśaśipra, Daśoṇya, Syūmaraśmi, and Ṛjūnas.
He who has established the hymns as his own, who has boldly drunk the Soma—
for him Viṣṇu strode out three steps according to the ordinances of Mitra.
O Indra, Lord of a hundred powers, you who take pleasure in the hymns of him who is a prize-winner among prize-winners—
such as you we invoke, seeking glory, like milkers calling upon a cow that yields abundance.
He who gives to us is our father; he is great, formidable, and the maker of sovereignty.
May the formidable Maghavan, possessor of many riches, grant us cattle and horses when he comes not to us.
O Vasu, he to whom you grant wealth for the sake of giving increases his abundance of riches.
Seeking wealth, we invoke Indra—the Lord of Wealth and the Lord of a hundred powers—with our hymns of praise.
Never do you neglect; you protect both generations. O Āditya, the fourth [part] of your invocation is your Indra-power; immortality has taken its stand in heaven.
O Maghavan Indra, lover of songs, you who are skilled and bestow gifts upon the worshipper—to him you grant his wish;
O Vasu, hear our songs, our fair praise, and our call, as you did for Kaṇva.
The ancient hymn has been praised; speak the sacred prayer to Indra.
Many lofty songs of Truth have resounded; the inspirations of the singer have been poured forth.
Indra has shaken together vast riches, he has brought together the two worlds and the sun.
The bright, pure Soma juices, mixed with milk, have exhilarated Indra.
We implore you, O Indra, Lord of wealth, the peerless among the wealthy, the eldest among the bulls, the foremost destroyer of forts, the finder of cattle, and the sovereign ruler of riches.
You who, growing stronger day by day, struck down Āyu, Kutsa, and Atithigva—
such as you are, O Lord of tawny steeds, Lord of a hundred powers, we invoke you while seeking booty.
May all the pressing-stones pour out for us the essence of the honeyed juice—
those drops which are pressed among people far away, and those which are pressed nearby.
Strike down all hostilities and drive them far away; let all win wealth.
Even among the Śīṣṭas are your exhilarating stalks where you satisfy yourself with Soma.
O Indra, come closer to us with aids that are well-measured;
come, O most auspicious one, with most auspicious protections, O most sleep-inducing one, with those things that bring deep sleep.
Make the lord of the virtuous, the conqueror in battle, the one who observes all people, a sharer of fortune among our progeny.
Further promote with your powers those who, chanting hymns, continually purify their will according to your ordinance.
May we be those who are most effective for your aid; may we be yours in the battles.
Through our priestly offerings and invocations of the gods, having won the prize, we celebrate you.
For I, O Lord of Bay Horses, seeking booty, ever go to your sacred prayer with my hymns as if to battle;
indeed, desiring horses and cattle, I place you alone at the forefront of the churning-sticks.

O Indra, the poets celebrate this heroic power of yours with their songs; chanting their hymns, they have brought forth strengthening food dripping with clarity; the Pauras have reached you with their inspired thoughts.
They have approached Indra for protection through their skillful deed—those at whose pressed juices you take delight;
as you rejoiced at Saṃvarta and as you did at Kṛśa, so, O Indra, exhilarate yourself among us.
O all you gods, being of one accord, come hither unto us;
may the Vasus and Rudras come to our aid, and may the Maruts hear our call.
May Pūṣan, Viṣṇu, and Sarasvatī protect my invocation, along with the seven rivers;
may the waters, the wind, the mountains, the lord of the forest, and the earth hear my call.
O Indra, most bountiful one, with that wealth which is yours, your own munificence, be our companion at the feast for our prosperity; O Vṛtra-slayer, as Bhaga, grant us gifts.
O Lord of the assembly, O Lord of men, you indeed, O wise one, bring us to the prize!
Having won through the invocations of the Hotṛ-priests and through the gatherings of the gods, they have become renowned.
For the noble blessings, O Indra, and the life-span of people are yours.
Come to us, O Maghavan, for our protection; milk out for us swelling nourishment.
O Indra, may we worship you with hymns; O Śatakratu, bestow upon Praskaṇva a great, solid, enduring, and abundant gift that knows no shame.
The abundant heroic power of Indra has been revealed as it approaches; O Dasyave Vṛka, this is your gift.
A hundred white bulls shine like stars in the sky; by their greatness, they have propped up the heavens as if they were pillars.
A hundred bamboos, a hundred dogs, a hundred tanned skins;
a hundred tufts of *balbaja* grass for me, and four hundred ruddy mares.
O descendants of Kaṇva, you are well-disposed toward the gods; moving from strength to strength, you stride like horses.
Then indeed they celebrated the great glory of the sevenfold, the perfect one;
the dark mares, outstripping the paths, could not be overtaken even by the eye.
O Dasyave-vṛka, your gift has been manifested,
bold as heaven, with a majesty as vast as the sky.
