Dasyave-vṛka bestowed ten thousand from his own wealth upon me, the son of Pūtakratu.
A hundred donkeys are mine, a hundred woolly ewes,
and a hundred slave-girls adorned with flower garlands.
There too, she was led forth for Pūtakratu, manifest like a mare belonging to a herd of horses.
Agni has perceived; he, the wise bearer of oblations, has shone forth with his auspicious chariot.
Agni, with his bright radiance, has shone loftily like the sun; the sun has shone in heaven.
O Gods, joined with your ancient wisdom and with your powerful chariot, O worshipful ones, come hither with your mighty powers, O Nāsatyas; drink this third libation.
The thirty-three gods, the truthful ones, have beheld you two in the presence of Truth.
O Aśvins, enjoying our sacrifice and libation, drink the Soma, you whose fires shine brightly.

O Aśvins, that deed of yours is worthy of praise: the bull [was raised] from heaven, the mid-air, and the earth. And those thousand who were in the quest for cattle—all of them you approached to drink.
This portion has been set out for you two, O worthy of sacrifice; come hither to these songs, O Nāsatyas!
Drink the honeyed Soma among us; protect the donor with your powers.

That which the officiating priests, being of one mind, fashion in many ways and carry as this sacrifice—who was that learned Brāhmaṇa who was yoked [to it]? What indeed is the understanding of the sacrificer in that regard?
Agni is indeed one, kindled in many ways; the Sun is one, pervading the universe with its light.
Dawn is indeed one; she shines upon all this. Verily, this one has become all this.
I invoke for you that light-filled, banner-bearing, three-wheeled chariot, easy to mount and providing many boons,
upon whose harnessing the goddesses of wondrous wealth were born— to drink the overflowing draught.
These portions of yours flow forth, O Indra and Varuṇa; at the libations, we invoke you both for greatness.
At every sacrifice, you hasten to the pressings when you bestow your favor upon the sacrificer who pours the juice.
The obstructing plants and waters stood still; O Indra and Varuṇa, you have attained greatness.
You two who have sped along the path beyond the firmament—for you, no godless enemy dares to prevail.

O Indra and Varuṇa, that is true: for you, the seven voices of Kr̥śa milk forth a wave of honeyed sweetness. With those [voices], O Lords of Splendor, protect the donor who, unassailable, guards you with his thoughts.
The seven sisters, sprinkling ghee, gentle, and quick-giving, abide in the seat of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*).
O Indra and Varuṇa, with those [streams] of yours that drip with ghee, bestow [wealth] and grant aid to the sacrificer.
For great good fortune, we have proclaimed the true, Indra-like majesty belonging to those two brilliant ones.
O Indra and Varuṇa, lords of splendor, protect us who drip with clarity through the three sevens.
O Indra and Varuṇa, when in the beginning you bestowed upon the seers inspired thought, the word, the hymn, and sacred learning;
those wise ones, while performing the sacrifice, beheld through fervor the various stations which they created.
O Indra and Varuṇa, bestow upon the sacrificers a benevolent and undisturbed abundance of wealth.
Grant us progeny, nourishment, and prosperity; extend our span of life for the sake of long-lived existence.
O Agni, come with the fires; we choose you as the Hotṛ.
Let the extended ladle full of oblation anoint you, the most excellent sacrificer, to sit upon the sacrificial grass.
For toward you, O son of strength, O Aṅgiras, the ladles move at the sacrifice.
We pray to Agni, the son of vigor, whose hair is ghee, the foremost in sacrifices.
O Agni, you are the sage, the ordainer, the purifying invoker worthy of sacrifice;
you are the delightful one, the best of sacrificers at the rites, to be praised by the inspired singers with their pure hymns.
O most youthful one, bring here the guileless gods who desire [the sacrifice], O eternal one, for the feast.
O Vasu, come toward the well-prepared offerings; rejoice, being well-disposed through our prayers.
O Agni, you alone are far-extending, O protector, a seer of the *ṛta*;
O kindled and shining one, the inspired sages and wise ordainers seek to win you over.
Shine forth, O most radiant one; beam out joy for the people; grant wealth to the singer—for you are great.
Under the protection of the gods may my wise patrons abide, they who overcome enemies and maintain the sacred fires.
Just as you, O Agni, utterly consume even a thick mass of dry wood upon the earth,
so, O you of Mitra-like greatness, burn whoever seeks to harm us, the evil-minded one who plots against us.
Do not deliver us over to the mortal enemy, nor to the one who possesses demons, nor to the one who utters evil speech.
O most youthful one, protect us with your tireless, crossing, and auspicious guardians.
Protect us, O Agni, with one [hymn], and protect us with a second;
protect us with three songs, O Lord of Strength, and protect us with four, O Vasu.
Protect us from every malicious demon; aid us in the contests for booty.
For we approach you alone as our nearest kinsman for the service of the gods, that we may prosper.

O Agni, O Purifier, grant us wealth that increases our vigor and is worthy of praise; and, O Supreme Lord, bestow upon us through your excellent guidance that which is much-desired and most glorious in its own splendor.
By which we may overcome those who defy us in battles, crossing over the hostile designs of the enemy—O Lord of Power, increase us with that nourishment; quicken our thoughts that find wealth.
Like a bull sharpening his horns, Agni brandishes them;
his jaws are keen and not to be withstood, for he is the mighty son of strength with beautiful teeth.
O Bull Agni, your jaws are not to be resisted when you spread yourself abroad;
as such, O Hotṛ, make our oblation well-offered and win for us many desirable things.
You lie within the two mothers' wood; mortals kindle you together.
Unwearied, you carry the oblations of those who prepare the sacrifice; then indeed, you reign among the gods.
The seven priests invoke you alone, O Agni, you who are easy to win and not to be shamed.
You cleave the rock with your heat and your flame; O Agni, rise up above all people.
With trimmed sacrificial grass and with oblations prepared, we invoke Agni after Agni, the unrestrained one;
we call upon Agni, the invoker of all peoples, at every sacrifice throughout all ages.
O Agni, he who is wise attends to you with his thought for protection and for the sake of the fair sacrifice;
bring to us, through your impelling power, food of many forms and the nearest strength for our aid.
O Agni, singer, lord of the people, burning away the demons, O god, you are the great master of the house who never departs; you are the guardian of heaven, dwelling within the home.

Let not the Rakṣas, O thou who art rich in glowing heat, enter us; let not the sorcery of those who practice sorcery reach us. Drive away hunger and want beyond the cattle-pasture, O Agni, and keep the possessors of demons at bay.
May Indra hear both these words of ours from nearby;
may the most powerful Maghavan come with his focused thought for the drinking of the Soma.
For the two worlds have fashioned him as the self-ruling bull for the sake of power;
moreover, you sit as the foremost among the supreme ones, for your mind desires Soma.
O Indra, Lord of many riches, pour forth [the draught] of the pressed soma-juice;
for we know you, O Lord of the bay steeds, as the conqueror in battles, who strikes down even the unassailable foe.
O Maghavan, let it be so according to your truth that is unassailable; O Indra, act with such wisdom as you desire.
O fair-cheeked one, wielder of the stone, may we quickly win booty through your protection as we hasten toward it.
O Indra, Lord of Might, may you grant us aid with all your protections;
for we follow after you, O Hero, the glorious finder of wealth, as if following Bhaga himself.
O God, you are the first possessor of horses, the multiplier of cattle, and a golden spring;
for no one can exhaust the gift within you. Whatever I ask of you, bring that to me.
Come indeed to the singer; find wealth for the sake of granting riches.
Pour it forth, O Maghavan, for the quest of cattle; pour it forth, O Indra, for the quest of horses.
You bestow for our gift many thousands and hundreds of herds.
We have brought Indra, the shatterer of forts, hither with inspired words, singing for his protection.

Whether it be a non-sage or a sage who has fashioned this speech for you, O Indra—let him, O Lord of a Hundred Powers, exult in his devotion to you; O you of forward-moving might, let him not come to harm.
If the fierce-armed Purandara, the smiter of the wicked, would hear my call—
seeking wealth, we invoke Indra, the lord of wealth and possessor of a hundred powers, with our hymns of praise.
We do not consider ourselves sinners, nor impotent, nor dull-witted,
when we now make the bull Indra our companion at the pressed juice.

We have harnessed the fierce one, the conqueror in battles, the debt-claimer, the undeceivable; he knows even the most anxious [thought], the best of charioteers who wins the prize—he whom we have indeed attained.
O Indra, from whatever we fear, grant us freedom from that fear. O Maghavan, be gracious; with your aids, drive away our enemies and destroy those who oppose us.
For you, O Lord of bounty, are the master of great wealth for the one who serves you;
as such, O Maghavan Indra, lover of songs, we, having pressed the soma, invoke you.

O Indra, be pleased; you are the slayer of Vṛtra, our protector from afar, and most worthy of choice. May he protect our last [member], may he protect our middle, and may he guard us from behind and from the front.
O Indra, protect us from behind, from below, from above, and from the front—guard us on every side.
Keep the divine fear far away from us, and keep the godless weapons far away.
O Indra, protect us today and every day, tomorrow and every tomorrow, and in the future; O Lord of the Good, may you guard all our singers throughout the days, by day and by night.
The breaker-down, the hero, Maghavan, the possessor of abundant wealth, is united for heroic deeds.
O Śatakratu, both your arms are virile, they which have grasped the thunderbolt.
Bring forth a hymn of praise for him who shall take pleasure in it;
with their chants, the Soma-pressers increase Indra’s majestic power. Blessed are the gifts of Indra.
Unequaled and peerless among men, the tireless one alone has surpassed many peoples;
he has grown great beyond all created beings by his might. Blessed are the gifts of Indra!
Even with an untrained steed, the swift-giver desires to win;
Indra, that deed of yours is worthy of proclamation as you perform heroic exploits—blessed are the gifts of Indra.

Come hither, O Indra; let us perform for you the strengthening prayers (*brahmāṇi*) by which, O most powerful one, you may take pleasure. Here, for the seeker of glory, there is prosperity; auspicious are the gifts of Indra.
O Indra, when you make even the bold mind more bold for one who honors you with potent Soma juices and adorns you with prostrations— blessed are the gifts of Indra!
The one who desires the hymn looks down like a man from a well;
having taken pleasure in the skill of the Soma-presser, he makes him his companion and ally—blessed are the gifts of Indra.
O Indra, all the gods have granted you heroic power and mental resolve.
You have become the protector of the universe, O much-praised one; auspicious are the gifts of Indra.
I praise that supreme power of yours, O Indra, for the assembly of the gods—that you slay Vṛtra with your might, O Lord of Might. Blessed are the gifts of Indra.
As if making human generations appear beautiful and equal, Indra has made that manifest sign known; indeed, the gifts of the renowned Indra are auspicious.
O Indra, they have raised up your born might, and they have raised you up, and your mental power;
O possessor of much cattle, O Maghavan, they have increased greatly under your protection. Blessed are the gifts of Indra.
O slayer of Vṛtra, both I and you shall join together for the sake of gains;
even the ill-disposed, O wielder of the stone, shall acknowledge us, O Hero—for auspicious are the gifts of Indra.
Truly indeed do we praise that Indra, and not falsely:
great is the destruction for him who pours no soma, while many lights belong to him who pours it; auspicious are the gifts of Indra.
That ancient Vena has been anointed with the rites of the great ones;
through whose doors Manu’s father anointed his prayers among the gods.
Like the measure of heaven, the stones with Soma upon their backs have taken their seat;
they are to be praised with hymns and sacred prayers.
As the wise one, Indra opened up the cows for the Aṅgirases;
I praise that manly deed of his.
Like of old, may that Indra, the increaser of the sage and the bearer of the word, come to us for our protection, being auspicious at the offering of the hymn.
Now indeed, O Indra, let those who sacrifice according to their desire cry out "Svāhā! after your will; let the singers chant their strengthening hymns for you to grant the enclosure of cattle.
In Indra are all heroic deeds, both those already accomplished and those yet to be done— he whom the hymns know as the sacrifice.
When the shouts of the fivefold people were released toward Indra, he,
the lord of the dwelling, by his own power, overthrew the inspired songs of the noble man.
This is your hymn of praise; you have performed those heroic deeds;
you have protected the track of the wheel.
The wide stride of this bull has extended for us to live;
he has gathered [the world] for himself as cattle gather barley.
Receiving that [gift], seeking aid through you, O sons of Dakṣa,
may we be for the increase of the Maruts.
O Hero, we praise you with hymns for the sake of the seasonal power;
O Indra, may we be victorious with you as our ally.
May the Rudras, the liberal ones, and the mountains be united with us in the slaying of Vṛtra when the call is raised for booty;
may those gods, with Indra as their chief—those who have been established as a firm support for him who recites and praises—protect us.
May the hymns of praise gladden you; bestow bounty, O wielder of the stone;
strike down those who hate the sacred word.
With your foot, trample down the stingy Panis; you are great, for there is no one who can withstand you.
O Indra, you rule over the pressed juices; you rule over the unpressed;
you are the king of the people.
Come hither, go forth; your dwelling is in heaven, sounding aloud among the people; you fill both the worlds, heaven and earth.
Even that mountain, the peak with its hundreds and thousands [of treasures],
you shattered for the sake of your worshippers.
We indeed invoke you by day at the pressing, and we invoke you by night;
fulfill our desire.
Where is that bull, the youth, with powerful necks and unbowed?
What priest honors him?
Whose libation does the bull Indra approach with delight?
And who indeed has yearned for Indra?
Whom have your gifts reached, O slayer of Vṛtra? Whom your great heroic powers? And who indeed is the one most intimate with your hymn of praise?
This Soma is pressed for you among the human race, among the Pūrus;
come hither, hasten to it, and drink!
This [Soma] of yours is dear at Śaryaṇāvat, at the Suṣomā, and most intoxicating at Ārjīkīya.
Him, for great bounty today, the lovely one for exhilarating joy, for the impetuous— come here, O Indra, run and drink!
O Indra, whether you are summoned by men from the east, the west, the north, or the south,
come quickly with your swift steeds.
Whether you exhilarate yourself at the fountain of heaven, O Svarṇara,
or in the ocean of the soma-juice;
With songs I call upon you, the great and wide one, as one calls a cow for nourishment;
O Indra, come for the drinking of the Soma.
O Indra, let your bay horses, bearing your greatness, bring your majesty, O God, upon your chariot.
O Indra, you who are praised, you who are great, fierce, and the maker of dominion, I laud you; come and drink our pressed soma.
We, possessing pressed juice and offering oblations, invoke you;
may you sit upon this sacred grass of ours.
For even though you, O Indra, are common to all the many,
we invoke you as such.
The men have milked this sweet Soma for you with the stones;
O Indra, being pleased, drink it.
Pass by all the wise enemies; come hither quickly!
Bestow upon us lofty renown.
The King, the giver of spotted deer accompanied by gold, may he, the bounteous one,
O gods, never come to harm.
Upon a thousand spotted deer, I have received a great, broad, bright, and shining piece of gold.
The grandsons of Durgaha, who are most bountiful, have established my fame among the gods with a thousand gifts.
With our praises, we call upon Indra, the finder of wealth, for your protection;
at this sacrifice where the soma is pressed, singing loudly, I invoke him as a prize-winner for the one who strives.
Whom neither the fierce nor the steadfast obstructors can hold back in the exhilaration of the soma-juice—
he, the fair-cheeked one, who, taking heed, bestows upon the laboring presser and the singer a praiseworthy gift.
Whether it be the powerful *mṛkṣa* of the horse, or the golden *kīja*,
Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, causes the opening of the stall of cattle to tremble.

He who, as the wielder of the thunderbolt with beautiful jaws and bay horses, sows even buried wealth that has been gathered by many for the sake of the donor— may Indra, according to his will, act as he desires.
Whatever you have accepted in the past, O much-praised hero among men,
that very sacrifice, hymn, and swift speech we bring together for you, O Indra.
O much-invoked wielder of the thunderbolt, drinker of the celestial Soma, come with the Soma juices for exhilaration;
for you alone, O giver of desirable wealth, have become the most generous bestower of riches upon the one who prepares the sacred prayer and presses the juice.
We have indeed strengthened this wielder of the thunderbolt here both today and yesterday;
therefore, bring him today the pressed juice in equal measure, and now pay homage to the one renowned for his deeds.
Even the wolf, the obstructer, the shaker of the breast, abides within his appointed courses;
O Indra, come to this our hymn with favor, rejoicing in it through inspired thought.
What manly deed of this Indra remains unaccomplished?
By what glory has the slayer of Vṛtra not been heard of from his very birth?
When indeed are his great, unassailable powers? And when is the Vṛtra-slayer invincible?
Indra surpasses all the Bekanāṭas who see by day, and by his will he overcomes the Paṇis.
O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, O much-invoked wielder of the thunderbolt, we indeed bring to you these most abundant prayers, as if presenting a tribute never before seen.
For many indeed are the hopes placed in you, O you of mighty deeds; the calls for help invoke you, O Indra. Even past the libations of the enemy, come, O Vasu; O most powerful one, hear my call!
O Indra, we indeed are yours; we, the inspired singers, belong to you alone.
For there is no other at all besides you, O much-invoked Maghavan, who is a gracious comforter.
From this lack of understanding and from hunger, protect us from the curse;
with your aid and your wondrous thought, O most powerful one, grant us help, for you are the finder of the path.
O Kāleyas, let this Soma be pressed for you; do not be afraid.
This destroyer of darkness departs; he shall surely depart by himself.
We now implore those Kṣatriyas, the Ādityas, for their protection— those who are most gracious, for our assistance.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, and Aryaman carry us across distress, as the Ādityas know best.
For theirs is a wondrous, praiseworthy protection for the donor who serves the Ādityas with devotion.
Great is the aid of you great ones, O Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman; we choose for ourselves your protections.
O Ādityas, let your breaths sustain us alive before we meet with slaughter; for how can you be those who hear our invocation?
Whatever protection you have for the weary one who presses the soma, whatever shelter there is— by that, speak in our favor.
O gods, there is wide room from distress; there is wealth for the sinless one—O Ādityas, you whose offenses are wondrously removed.
Let not this bond bind us; may it release us for our great purpose.
For Indra alone is renowned as the sovereign lord.
O gods, you who desire to help us, do not let us be touched by the weapon of our treacherous enemies. Do not strike us down.
And I, O Aditi, invoke you, the great goddess,
for the sake of mercy and for my protection.
O you whose sons are fierce, rescue us from the one who seeks to slay us in the deep abyss; let no harm come to our offspring.
O sinless one, wide-pastured and far-reaching, grant us freedom to spread abroad;
make it so for our offspring to live.
Those who are the heads of the settlements, undeceived, self-glorious, and free from malice, they guard the sacred laws.
O Ādityas, release us from the jaws of the wolves,
like a bound thief, O Aditi.
O Ādityas, let this arrow, this ill-will, go away from us—
let it pass by without striking us.
For evermore, O Ādityas, bounteous givers, we have indeed enjoyed your protections— both in the past and now.
O wise ones, O gods, you grant eternal life even to him who has committed a transgression.
O Ādityas, may that new favor of yours be even better than the old, which shall release us from bondage like one bound, O Aditi.
O Ādityas, that [power] of ours is not for leaping over;
have mercy upon us.
O Ādityas, let not the missile of Vivasvat, nor the artificial arrow, strike us before old age has come.
O Ādityas, drive away hatred, drive away distress, and drive away all that is gathered against us; cast away evil in every direction.
Like a chariot, we bring you hither for our protection and for our favor—
you, O Indra, most powerful Lord of the True, the performer of many deeds who overcomes the attackers.
O you of mighty strength, of great wisdom, and of powerful deeds, with your all-pervading thought, you have filled [the world] with your majesty.
By whose greatness, O Mighty One, your two hands reached around the golden thunderbolt as it moved across the earth.
I invoke with my courses for aid Viśvānara, the lord of wealth, whose power is unbending, and who is the master of the people and of chariots.
For our desired aid, men invoke from various sides for protection him who is ever-increasing and who is praised in the contests for light.
Indra, who transcends all measure, who is worthy of praise, the fierce one, the bestower of great wealth—
the very lord of riches.
I urge that very Indra toward great bounty and toward drinking—
the dancer who rules over the ancient hymn of praise and over the people.
O mighty one, no mortal has ever attained your friendship; no one can reach the full extent of your powers.
Aided by you, with you as our ally, may we win great wealth in the waters and in the sun; may we conquer in battles, O wielder of the thunderbolt.
We seek you with sacrifices, we seek you with songs, O you who are most fond of song;
O Indra, just as you have protected Purumīḷha in the battles for booty.
O wielder of the stone, he whose friendship with you is sweet, whose guidance is sweet, for him the sacrifice is to be extended far.
Grant wide space for our bodies, grant us wide space for our dwelling;
grant us wide space that we may live.
We contemplate the wide path for men, the wide path for cattle, and the wide path for the chariot— the feast for the gods.
Six men, two by two, stand near me, exhilarated by Soma; they are bounteous givers of sweet things.
Indrota received from the son of Ṛkṣa two bay horses, and from the son of Aśvamedha two ruddy ones.
To Ātithigva, [you gave] well-yoked chariots; to Arkṣa, [you gave] those with beautiful reins;
to Aśvamedha, those that are well-adorned.
Six horses with mares, O Ātithigva,
you won together from Indrota at the sacrifice of Pūtakratu.
Among these dappled horses, the ruddy mare, accompanied by stallions, is conspicuous—
she who possesses her own reins and is equipped with a whip.
O you who are bound by the prize, not even a mortal man wishing to revile you could ever attribute blame to you.
Forward, forward [goes] the *triṣṭubh* hymn as nourishment for the exhilarated hero, for Soma.
With prayer and with wisdom, he seeks to win you for the acquisition of the sacrifice.
I seek you as the lord of the lowing cows, the lord of those who are in heat,
and the master of your inviolable milch-kine.
These dappled cows, yielding milk for the preparation, mix the Soma;
they are the clans at the birth of the gods, in the three luminous realms of heaven.
Sing forth with song to Indra, the lord of cattle, as he is known—
to the son of truth, the lord of the virtuous.
The bay steeds have been let loose upon the ruddy [mares] on the sacrificial grass,
where we raise our voices together in song.
For Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the cows milked the sweet *āśira* mixture,
when he found it in his hiding place.
When we two, Indra and I, go up to the dwelling-place on the summit of the sun, having drunk of the honeyed mead, let us both attend together upon the Friend in the thrice-seven places.
Sing praises, sing forth; O Priyamedhas, sing praises!
Let your sons also sing, and sing boldly as if against a fortress.
The gargara resounds downward; the lizard has cried out all around;
the piṅgā has chirped all around—the prayer is raised up for Indra.
When the dappled cows, easy to milk and unflinching, come running hither,
seize the unflinching Soma for Indra to drink.
Indra has drunk, Agni has drunk; all the gods have become exhilarated.
Varuṇa indeed dwells here; to him the waters have cried out in unison, like mother cows lowing toward their calf.
You are a good god, O Varuṇa, you whose seven rivers flow along the palate as if into a hollow pipe.
He who made the well-yoked coursers spring forward for the donor— he, the leader, like a swift antelope, is the wondrous form that was released as the highest.
Truly, the mighty Indra has surpassed all his enemies;
he, the young one, split apart the porridge being cooked beyond the mountain with his song.
Like a small child, he mounted the new chariot;
he brought the mighty buffalo-deer, possessed of sovereign power, for his father and mother.
O fair-cheeked lord of the house, mount your golden chariot;
then let us two accompany the heavenly, thousand-footed, ruddy, well-faring, and peerless steed.
To him indeed, the self-radiant one, the worshipful ones sit down in this manner;
for they bring back his well-placed purpose so that he may come to bestow gifts.
Following the ancient dwelling of these Priyamedhas,
those who have spread the sacrificial grass and prepared the offerings have attained the first gift according to the ancient custom.
He who is the king of the peoples, who advances with his chariots unrestrained,
the overcomer of all hostile armies— he who is praised as the eldest, the slayer of Vṛtra.
O Puruhanman, glorify that Indra for his protection,
he upon whose two-fold supporter the beautiful thunderbolt was placed in his hand, like the great sun in the sky.
No one can equal him in deed who has made him ever-increasing—
Indra, who is praised by all, the skillful, the unassailable, and possessed of daring might, as if through sacrifices.
The invincible, fierce one, the conqueror in battles, at whose birth the great, far-reaching milch-cows lowed together; the heavens and the earths lowed in unison.
O Indra, even if there were a hundred heavens and a hundred earths belonging to you,
O wielder of the thunderbolt, neither the thousand suns nor the two worlds could equal you at your birth.
O Bull, most powerful one, you have filled all things with your greatness, your manly vigor, and your might.
O Maghavan, wielder of the thunderbolt, favor us with your wondrous aids in the search for a stall full of cattle.
O long-lived one, no godless mortal shall attain nourishment;
even he who yokes the swift-moving Etaśas, even Indra himself, yokes his two bay steeds.
For your sake, I call upon that great Indra, the one worthy of worship, the powerful one for the granting of gifts—
he who is to be invoked in shallow waters and in the deep, who is to be invoked in the contests for booty.
O Vasu, O Hero, raise up for us great wealth;
O Maghavan, raise it up for the great gift of riches; O Indra, raise it up for great glory.
O Indra, you who seek the truth, you satisfy yourself with our offerings while warding off the slanderers;
O you of many heroic deeds, clothe yourself between your arms and strike down the Dāsa with your blows.
May the mountain, our own kinsman, shake down the one who follows another's law, the non-human, the non-sacrificer, and the godless; may the mountain shake down the Dasyu for easy slaughter.
O most powerful Indra, do you take hold of these in our hands for us to give away—like roasted grains; take hold of them twice, O well-disposed one, take hold of them, O well-disposed one.
O friends, seek out his will: how may we accomplish the praise of Śara, the liberal patron and wise lord who is free from shame?
You shall indeed be praised by many seers who have spread the sacrificial grass,
when you thus bestow the calves one by one.
Maghavan, son of Śūradeva, having seized him by the ear, brought back our calf from the three [rivers],
just as a wise patron brings a goat to be milked.
O Agni, with your great powers, protect us from every hostile force and from the enmity of mortal man.
For human wrath has no power over you, O you who are born of love; you alone, O Lord of the Night, are the master.
O Son of Strength, with your auspicious radiance, together with all the gods, grant us wealth that contains all desirable things.
O Agni, the enemies do not deprive that mortal of wealth whom you, as a protector, favor for his offerings.
O inspired sage Agni, that man whom you urge on toward wealth in the contest for the prize of wisdom,
through your protection, shall attain cattle.
O Agni, grant wealth consisting of many heroes to the mortal who offers oblations; lead us forward toward what is better.
O Jātavedas, protect us; do not deliver us over to the one who intends evil, nor to the mortal of malicious intent.
O Agni, let no godless man ward off the bounty of you, the god;
for you are the lord of all treasures.
O Son of Strength, bestow upon us of that abundant wealth;
O Friend, O Vasu, grant it to those who sing thy praise.
May our songs go forth toward him of piercing brilliance, the beautiful one;
may our sacrifices with homage go toward the possessor of many riches, the one praised by many, for his protection.
Agni, the son of strength, Jātavedas, for the granting of desirable boons—
he who has become doubly immortal among mortals, the most delightful invoker in the clan.
I choose Agni for you with the sacrifice to the gods; I choose Agni when the ritual is set in motion.
I choose Agni as the first in our prayers, Agni for the swift steed, and Agni for the successful attainment of the field.

May Agni grant us nourishment in his friendship, for he is the lord of all desirable things; we constantly implore Agni for our offspring and progeny—he who is the Vasu and the protector of our bodies.
Invoke Agni with songs for protection, him of the piercing flame;
O Purumīḷha, invoke the renowned Agni for wealth, and the men [invoke] Agni for a well-lit dwelling.
We praise Agni so that he may drive away our hatred; we praise Agni so that he may grant us well-being and prosperity.
To be invoked like a protector among all the tribes, may he be the illuminator of the dawns.
Prepare the oblation; let the Adhvaryu priest come again;
he, being wise, follows his instruction.
The Hotṛ has sat down upon the mind, toward the sharp stalk,
taking pleasure in his friendship.
They seek him within the people, the Rudra who is beyond the reach of thought;
they seize the essence with their tongue.
The bestower of strength heated the bow of kinship; he climbed the forest tree and struck the rock with his tongue.
Moving here, the bright calf finds no one to tether him;
he seeks his mother to praise her.
And now, his great and vast chariot-yoke, accompanied by horses, has been seen— the tethering-rope of his chariot.
The seven milk the one; two cause the five to flow at the ford of the river, upon its resonance.
With the ten [fingers] of Vivasvat, Indra shook down the vessel from heaven with his threefold hammering.
The newest flame goes threefold around the sacrifice;
the Hotṛ-priests anoint it with honey.
With reverence they pour out the water that flows around in a high wheel,
downward-flowing and inexhaustible.
The pressing-stones have indeed brought forth the honey poured into the cup at the release of the spring.
O cows, come hither; you two great ones are the overflowing vessels of the sacrifice, with both ears made of gold.
Pour the glory upon the pressed juice, the glory that overspreads heaven and earth;
may the Rasa receive the Bull.
They recognize their own dwelling place; like calves with their mothers, they meet together with their kinsmen.
As they devour [the offerings] at the jaws, they establish a support in heaven;
to Indra and Agni be homage and light.
The noble one has milked forth swelling nourishment and strength, consisting of seven steps,
by means of the seven rays of the sun.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, the risen sun has taken up the Soma;
that is the medicine for the sick man.
And now, that place of his, the beloved one’s abode,
he has extended with his tongue beyond the sky.
Arise for the one who follows the Truth; yoke your chariot, O Aśvins!
May your protection be near at hand.
O Aśvins, come even with your swiftest chariot, which is faster than a blink of an eye; let your protection be near at hand.
O Aśvins, you spread cold over the heat for Atri;
may your protection be near at hand.
Where are you? Where have you gone? Where have you flown like two hawks?
May your protection be near at hand.
If today, at whatever time, you two should hear this invocation,
may your protection be present near us.
O Aśvins, you who are most swift to answer the call for the journey, I go to you, the closest kin; let your protection be near at hand.
O Aśvins, you two have made a home for Atri; may your protection be near at hand.
You two chose Agni as a source of heat; he spoke beautifully for Atri. May your protection be present nearby.
Saptavadhri, through his prayer, won the stream of Agni. May your protection be near at hand.
Come here, O you who possess raining wealth; hear this my invocation.
Let your protection be near at hand.
What is this that is being praised of you two, as if for two who are ancient and like those who have grown old? May your protection be near at hand.
Common is your kinship, common is your bond, O Aśvins; let your protection be near at hand.
O Aśvins, may that chariot of yours which traverses the realms and the two worlds, Rodasī, come near; let your protection be present.
Come to us with thousands of cattle and horses; let your protection be near at hand.
Do not overlook us with regard to our thousands of cattle and horses; may your protection be near at hand.
The ruddy-hued Dawn has appeared; the upholder of cosmic order has made light.
May your protection be near at hand.
O Aśvins, look out clearly, like one with an axe at a tree;
let your protection be near us.
O bold one, shatter the fortress as if with a black host when you are pressed;
let your protection be near at hand.
Seeking strength, we praise with hymns of power your Agni, the beloved guest of every house, who dwells within our dwellings.
Him whom people, bearing oblations, praise with eulogies like Mitra who receives the offering of clarified butter.
To the most praiseworthy Jātavedas, who, when the deities were raised up,
sent the oblations to heaven.
We have come to Agni, the best slayer of Vṛtra, the eldest descendant of Manu,
whose face is nourished by Śrutarvan, the great son of R̥kṣa.
The immortal Jātavedas, visible even through the darkness, who is invoked with offerings of clarified butter and worthy of praise.
These people, beset by difficulties, worship Agni with oblations,
offering gifts with uplifted ladles.
This newest hymn has been offered to you, O Agni, from us— O joyous one, well-born, of noble will, unerring, wondrous guest!
O Agni, may this [hymn] of yours be most peaceful, most pleasing, and dear;
through it, being well-praised, may you increase.
May she, resplendent with splendors, bestow great renown upon our fame; may she grant us glory in the conquest of Vṛtra.
Him who possesses horses, cattle, and fills the chariot— him, the brilliant lord of the people, like Indra— whose glories you celebrate and whose every praiseworthy deed the folk extol.
O Agni Aṅgiras, you whom Gopavana has gratified with his song— he,
O Purifier, hear our call.
O you whom the people, pressing forward in their zeal, invoke for the winning of booty— be mindful of us in the conquest of Vṛtra.
I, being invoked by Śrutarvan, the son of R̥kṣa,
the shedder of exhilaration, shall wipe away the heads of four [men], like the herds of woolly sheep.
May the four swift, running horses of the most powerful one, with their fine chariots, carry me toward the offerings like birds carrying the son of Tugra.
Truly, O great river Paruṣṇī, I have pointed you out to him;
there is no mortal who gives horses more than he, O most powerful one.
Yoke, O Agni, like a charioteer, the horses that best invoke the gods; sit down as the ancient Hotṛ-priest.
And so, O God, as one who knows best, speak for us to the gods;
grant us full confidence in all desirable things.
O youngest son of strength, when you have been invoked,
you have become the observer of cosmic order (*ṛtāvā*) and worthy of sacrifice.
This Agni is the lord of thousandfold and hundredfold booty; he is the sage, the head of riches.
O Aṅgiras, bow down to him with joint invocations, as the Ṛbhus bend the felly; come closer to the sacrifice.
To him, the bull who shines toward heaven, O Virūpa, now urge forth a well-fashioned hymn with your eternal speech.
Whom indeed shall we strike down with the missile of this Agni, who looks from afar— the Paṇi, while he is still among the cattle?
O gods, let not the clans of the gods abandon us, like cows that have bathed leaving behind a weakling; let not the inviolable ones forsake us.
May the affliction of the malicious one who hates us all not strike us down,
as a wave strikes a ship.
Homage to your power, O Agni; O God, the peoples sing your praise. With your flames, afflict the enemy.
O Agni, will you not surely bestow wealth upon us for our quest for cattle? O maker of wide space, make room for us.
Do not abandon us in this great contest, like a bearer of burdens; win the wealth that gathers all together!
O Agni, let this misfortune, driven by fear, pursue someone other than us; increase our power with irresistible might.
Whose *śamī* wood— whether that of one who offers homage or of one who performs the sacrifice— Agni has taken pleasure in, him indeed he causes to prosper.
From the distance of the further shore, come hither across to us;
protect those where I am.
For we have known you, O Agni, from of old as our father’s protector;
therefore, we now seek your favor.
Now I invoke this Indra, the master of magic, who rules by his might;
accompanied by the Maruts, do not withhold him from me.
This Indra, with the Maruts as his companions, split asunder the head of Vṛtra with his hundred-knotted thunderbolt.
Growing strong with the Maruts as his companions, Indra drove Vṛtra apart,
releasing the waters of the ocean.
This very Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, by whom this light of heaven was won, [is summoned] for the drinking of Soma.
We invoke with songs Indra, who is accompanied by the Maruts, the consumer of the Soma dregs, the powerful, and the exuberant.
We invoke Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, with an ancient hymn,
for the drinking of this Soma.
O bounteous Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, O lord of a hundred powers, praised by many, drink the Soma at this sacrifice.
For you alone, O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, O wielder of the stone, these pressed Soma juices are offered from the heart with hymns of praise.
O Indra, friend of the Maruts, drink the pressed Soma at the celestial sacrifices,
whetting your thunderbolt with might.
Rising up with vigor, having drunk, you shook your jaws,
O Indra, after drinking the Soma pressed in the ladle.
Both heaven and earth cried out after you as you roared,
O Indra, when you became the slayer of the Dasyus.
From Indra I have measured out my body— the speech that has eight feet, nine corners, and touches the Eternal Order (Ṛta).
As soon as he was born, the hundredfold powerful one questioned his mother thus: "Who are the fierce ones? Who indeed are renowned?"
Then he spoke of him to Śavas, of Aurṇavābha and Ahīśuva: "Let them be your sons, O Niṣṭhura."
The Vṛtra-slayer struck them down together as if with an axle-pin, like spokes in a wheel;
having grown great, he became the destroyer of the Dasyus.
In a single draught Indra drank thirty lakes at once, desiring the Soma.
Indra pierced the Gandharva in the bottomless regions for the sake of the increase of the sacred formulations (brahmāṇi).
From the mountains he cast forth [the demon] and held fast the cooked rice;
Indra [seized] the most tightly bound *bunda* weapon.
Your arrow has a hundred barbs; it is unique with its thousand feathers, O Indra, which you have made your ally.
With that, O Ribhusthira, born at once, bring [wealth] to the male singers and for the women to eat.
These most exalted deeds of yours have been performed with fullness;
O steadfast one, you have sustained them with your heart.
All those things Viṣṇu, the wide-striding one, brought when impelled:
a hundred buffaloes, rice cooked with milk, and a boar that had stolen from Indra.
Powerful is your well-fashioned, pleasant bow; excellent is your golden arrowhead.
Both your arms are worthy of battle, well-prepared, increasing even that which is soft, O you of gentle form.
O Indra, bring us a thousandfold of the pressed juice and our sacrificial cake; O Hero, bring hundreds of cattle.
Bring us a distinguishing mark: a cow, a horse, and ointment;
along with that, golden ornaments.
And bring us many ear-ornaments, O bold one; for you, O Vasu, are renowned as the one who hears us.
O Indra, no one is a better increaser for you than Vṛdhīka—neither a skilled presser nor a liberal giver; indeed, O Hero, no other priest is like you.
Indra is not to be warded off, nor is the powerful Śakra to be resisted;
he hears everything and sees everything.
He, the undeceived one, seeks to restrain the wrath of mortals;
before the onset of reproach, he desires to act.
Truly, by his power, the belly of the swift one who ordains all is full—
of the slayer of Vṛtra, the drinker of Soma.
In you, O Soma, all treasures and all blessings are gathered together—
bounteous, unassailable, and never to be turned back.
To you alone does my desire, seeking barley, seeking cattle, and seeking gold, turn; to you it speeds, seeking horses.
O Indra, through hope in you, I have even taken a sickle in my hand;
O Maghavan, fill me with a handful of barley, whether it be what has been reaped or what has been gathered.
This Soma is the achiever, ungraspable, all-conquering, and the piercer; he is the seer and the inspired singer through his poetic wisdom.
He covers what is naked; he heals everything that is afflicted. Through him, the blind has seen and the cripple has emerged.
O Soma, you are the one who extends wide protection against the hostilities of our own bodies and those wrought by others.
O impetuous one, through your wisdom and your skillful powers, you reach from heaven to earth; you drive away even the hatred of the sinner.
If those seeking wealth go to obtain their goal, may they find the bounty of the giver;
may they satisfy the desire of the thirsty.
When he recovered what was lost from of old, he raised up the one who lives by the *ṛta*; he extended the life that had not yet been completed.
O Soma, be very gracious to us, showing mercy, with a mind free from arrogance and unsubdued; be a source of well-being for our heart.
O Soma, do not terrify us; O King, do not cause us to tremble with fear. Do not strike our heart with your fiery wrath.
When I behold the ill-will of the gods within my own dwelling, O King, drive away our enemies; O Bounteous One, drive away those who seek to harm us.
For there is no other comforter than you, O Śatakratu;
therefore, O Indra, have mercy on us.
O Indra, you who have constantly protected us from of old, never failing when we sought for booty— such as you are, O Indra, be gracious to us.
How much more, then, as the impeller of the weary, will you be the helper of the one who presses the juice?
O Indra, will you not surely be able for us?
O Indra, O wielder of the stone, protect our chariot even if it is behind;
place it for me in front.
Come now! Why do you sit still? Make our chariot foremost, O seeker of strength, even as the highest glory.
Favor our chariot that seeks the prize; it is easy for you to do so—what need is there for hesitation? Make us truly victorious.
O Indra, be steadfast; you are a fortress. This auspicious prayer, timely and perfect, approaches your appointed place.
Let not the blameless one come to reproach; the goal is wide, the prize is set, and the obstacles have been removed.
When you perform that which is worthy of sacrifice, called the fourth, then we desire that; from that time on, you are celebrated as our Lord.
He has strengthened you, O immortals, and has gladdened you—the gods who dwell for a single day, as well as those who are goddesses.
Bestow upon him a glorious gift; may he, enriched by prayer, come quickly in the morning.
O Indra, do thou gather for us a wonderful, food-filled prize with thy mighty right hand.
For we know you as one of many exploits, of many gifts, and of great wealth,
possessing vast measure through your protections.
O Hero, neither the gods nor mortals can restrain you when you desire to give,
just as one cannot hold back a terrifying bull.
Come now, let us praise Indra, the lord of wealth, the self-ruling sovereign;
may he not neglect us with his bounty.
May he praise you and sing your praises; may he hear the Sāman being sung;
may he reward us with bounty.
Bring to us with your right hand; touch us with your left.
O Indra, do not exclude us from wealth.
Come near, O bold one; bring [the wealth] with courage from among the people—the possession of him who is most reluctant to give.
O Indra, whatever strength you possess that is to be won by inspired poets—
win that well for us.
May those swift steeds of yours, O Vājas, who are all-gladdening, quickly neigh for us according to our desires.
Run forth from afar and from near at hand, O slayer of Vṛtra,
toward the bringing of the sweet draught!
The Soma juices are strong; come hither! These pressed juices are exhilarating. Drink, O steadfast one, as you desire!
Rejoice in this nourishment; it is sufficient for your choice and your wrath. O Indra, may it be a blessing to your heart.
Come here, O you who have no enemies; you are invoked by our hymns of praise in the highest luminous realm of heaven.
For you this [Soma] has been pressed with stones and purified with milk for exhilaration;
O Indra, Soma is offered forth to you.
O Indra, hear my call well; partake of this pressed juice mixed with milk that belongs to us, and attain full drinking and satisfaction.
O Indra, the Soma which has been pressed for you in the cups and in the vats—
drink of this, for you are its lord.
He who, like the moon in the waters, is seen within the vessels—of him you shall drink; for you are the master thereof.
That which the falcon brought to you with his foot, across the regions, untouched—drink of this; you are its master.
We choose for ourselves that great protection of the gods;
may it be for our aid from the bulls.
May they— Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman— be our constant allies, as well as the wise ones who grant us increase.
Carry us across many perils, as if across waters with ships;
you are the charioteers of the Eternal Order (*ṛta*).
May there be for us what is desirable, O Aryaman; may there be what is desirable and praiseworthy, O Varuṇa; for we choose that which is desirable.
For you, O wise ones, are the lords of desirable wealth, O destroyers of enemies;
none of us, O Ādityas, shall fall into the power of evil.
O bounteous gods, whether we are dwelling at home or traveling on the road, we invoke you for our prosperity.
O Indra and Viṣṇu, look upon these kinsmen of ours;
O Maruts and Aśvins, come hither!
O bounteous ones, we maintain our brotherhood from of old, even in the common womb of our mother.
For you indeed, O bounteous ones, with Indra as your chief, are directed toward heaven;
therefore I address you now.
I praise Agni, your dearest guest, beloved like a friend, who is to be known like a chariot.
Him, like a wise seer, the gods have established among mortals from of old.
O youngest one, protect the men who offer oblations; hear our songs, and by your own self, guard our offspring.
With what [hymn], O Agni Aṅgiras, son of strength, may we offer praise to you, O God, according to your will and desire?
With what intention shall we serve the sacrifice, O Son of Strength?
And what indeed shall we utter as this homage?
Therefore, do you indeed grant us all secure dwellings,
and [grant] our songs [the attainment of] wealth consisting of booty.
Whose abundant prayers do you now quicken,
O Lord of the Household, you whose songs win cattle?
They groom him, the one of skillful intellect, the leader in battles, the prize-winner in his own dwellings.
He dwells in secure peace through virtuous means; no one slays him, but he slays others. O Agni, he prospers with excellent heroes.
O Nāsatyas, Aśvins, come to my invocation, you two,
for the drinking of the sweet Soma.
O Aśvins, hear this hymn of mine, hear this my invocation,
for the drinking of the sweet Soma.
O Aśvins, possessors of abundant wealth, this Kṛṣṇa here invokes you both for the drinking of the sweet Soma.
O Heroes, listen to the invocation of the singer Kṛṣṇa as he praises you,
for the drinking of the sweet Soma.
O Heroes, grant protection that is inviolable to the inspired singer who praises you,
so that he may drink the sweet Soma juice.
Come to the house of the donor who thus praises you, O Aśvins,
for the drinking of the sweet Soma.
Yoke the donkey to the chariot with its strong-limbed frame, O you two who possess bull-like wealth,
for the drinking of the sweet Soma.
Come, O Aśvins, on your three-seated, triple-wheeled chariot,
to drink the sweet Soma.
O Nāsatyas, O Aśvins, do you now favor my songs for the drinking of the sweet Soma.
For you both are the wonder-working physicians who bring delight; you both have become the masters of skillful speech.
Viśvaka invokes you both for the preservation of his body; do not sever our friendship, but release us from distress.
How indeed shall I now praise you two when my mind is troubled? You have bestowed wisdom upon us for the attainment of greater wealth.
Viśvaka invokes you both for the protection of his body; do not sever our friendship, but release us from distress.
For you two indeed gave this nourishment, beneficial to many, to Viṣṇāpū so that he might attain greater wealth.
Viśvaka invokes you both for the protection of his own body; do not sever our friendship, but release us from [all] bonds.

And we invoke for protection that hero, the winner of wealth, who drinks the soma-dregs, even though he is far away—he whose most sweet favor is like that of a father. May you two not withdraw from our friendship; release us!
By the *ṛta* the god Savitṛ brings peace; the horn of *ṛta* has spread far and wide.
*Ṛta* has conquered even the great assailant. Do not sever our friendship; release us!
O Aśvins, this glorious hymn of yours is like the pouring of Krivi; come hither!
O Heroes, drink of the pressed honey-sweetness which is dear in heaven, as two wild bulls drink at a watering-place.
Drink the honeyed *gharma*, O Aśvins; sit upon the sacred grass, O heroes.
Rejoicing in the dwelling of man, protect our vitality with your wisdom.
The Priyamedhas have invoked you both with all your aids;
come to the dwelling of him who has strewn the sacrificial grass, to the beloved sacrifice during the rites of the seekers of heaven.
Drink the honeyed Soma, O Aśvins; sit upon the sacred grass with favor.
Having grown strong, come to our excellent praise from heaven, like two wild bulls to a watering place.
Come now, O Aśvins, with your dappled horses! O wonder-workers on golden paths, lords of splendor, increaseers of Truth, drink the Soma.
For we, the inspired singers, longing for praise, invoke you both for the winning of booty.
O Aśvins, you who are beautiful, wondrous, and rich in deeds—come with heedful ears, drawn by our prayer!
We celebrate with songs that Indra for you— the wondrous one, the subduer of enemies, who rejoices in the exhilarating juice of wealth— just as cows low toward their calf in the stalls.
We quickly implore him who dwells in heaven, the bountiful giver, encompassed by powers, who is like a mountain rich in many enjoyments—
him for foodful booty, hundredfold and thousandfold, abounding in cattle.
Neither the great nor the solid mountains, O Indra, can restrain you when you wish to bestow wealth upon a singer like me; no one can diminish that power of yours.
You are a warrior by your wisdom, O Śavas, and by your wondrous power, surpassing all created beings in your might.
May this hymn which the Gotamas have produced turn you hither for our protection.
For you have indeed cast yourself forth with might from the very ends of heaven. O Indra, the earthly realm has not contained you; you have grown great according to your own inherent power.
O Maghavan, there is no one who can obstruct your bounty when you bestow gifts upon the donor. Be the inspirer of our hymn of praise, most liberal for the winning of booty.
Sing a great song for Indra, O Maruts, the most effective slayer of Vṛtra,
by whom the upholders of cosmic order generated light— the god who is ever-watchful for the sake of the gods.
He blew away the curses, for he is the slayer of the slanderer; then Indra became resplendent in glory.
O you of great luster, leader of the Marut host, the gods have striven for your friendship, O Indra.
O Maruts, sing a prayer for your lofty Indra!
Let the Vṛtra-slayer, the lord of a hundred powers, slay Vṛtra with his hundred-knotted thunderbolt.
Boldly strike out, O you of bold mind; let your fame be lofty indeed.
Let the waters, the mothers, flow forth with speed; slay Vṛtra and win the light of heaven!
When you were born, O matchless Maghavan, for the slaying of Vṛtra,
then you spread out the earth and you propped up the sky.
From that your sacrifice was born; from that the hymn and the joyful laughter.
Therefore you are the overcomer of all that is born and all that is to be born.
Within the raw [clouds] you have placed the cooked [rain]; you have caused the sun to ascend to heaven.
Like a cauldron heated by a chant, heat it with well-fashioned hymns—a lofty song, pleasing to the lover of praise.
May Indra, who is to be invoked in all battles, be present for us;
may the slayer of Vṛtra, the supreme victor worthy of praise, attend our prayers and the Soma libations.
You are the foremost giver of riches; you are the true one who acts as a sovereign lord.
We choose the alliance of the greatly glorious Śavas, the son of great power.
O Indra, lover of songs, these unsurpassed prayers are being fashioned for you.
O Lord of bay horses, Indra, take pleasure in these, which we have meditated upon as your yoke-lengths.
For you, O Maghavan, are true and unbending; you strike down many Vṛtras. Therefore, O most powerful one, wielder of the thunderbolt, bring wealth hitherward to the donor.
O Indra, you are glorious, the drinker of the *ṛjīṣa*, Lord of Might.
You alone, O sustainer of the people, slay the irresistible Vṛtras that have never been overcome.
O Asura, we now entreat you, the wise one, for bounty as if for our own portion. Like a great, protective cloak, O Indra, may your favors reach us.
The maiden, drawing down the water, found the Soma in the strainer;
bringing it to her home, she said, "I shall press you for Indra; I shall press you for Śakra."
O little hero, you who go there, looking about from house to house— drink this pressed with the jaws, accompanied by parched grain, by groats, by cakes, and by hymns of praise!
We cannot even discern you, nor do we grasp you at all;
O Indu, flow slowly, very gently, for Indra.
What will he accomplish? What will he do? Will he make us more prosperous?
Might we, as those who have been hostile toward their husbands, now come together with Indra?
O Indra, cause these three regions to sprout:
that head, the field, and this [place] here within my belly.
And that field of ours which is there, and this body of mine,
and also the head of Tatas— make all of those hairy.
O Śatakratu, through the hole of the chariot, the hole of the wagon-pole,
and the hole of the yoke, you, O Indra, having purified Apālā three times, made her skin like the sun.
Sing forth unto Indra while he drinks of your soma-juice—
him who conquers all, the lord of a hundred powers, the most bountiful among the peoples.
Call him "Indra"— the one invoked by many, praised by many, the leader of songs, and the one of ancient renown.
O Indra, you are the giver of great spoils to us, the dancer;
as the mighty one, may he lead us with his forefeet.
Indra, the broad-chested one, has drunk of the soma-juice— the well-prepared, skillful, and exhilarating drop— mixed with barley.
Sing forth to that Indra so that he may drink the Soma;
for this indeed is his means of strengthening.
Having drunk of his exhilarating draughts, the god, by the might of the god,
has surpassed all worlds.
Bring hither for our protection that ever-conquering one of yours, who is drawn toward all our songs.
The warrior who is invincible, the drinker of Soma, the unshakable,
the hero whose will is irresistible.
O Indra, you who know much, bestow wealth upon us, O worthy of praise;
help us in the decisive contest for booty.
From there, O Indra, come to us with food that brings a hundredfold strength,
with food that brings a thousandfold strength.
O Śakra, seeker of cattle, may we, through our inspired thoughts, direct the prayers of the wise;
O wielder of the thunderbolt, may we conquer in battles with our swift steeds.
O Śatakratu, we cause you to delight in our hymns, as cattle do in pastures.
For all our desires, O Lord of a hundred powers, have been fulfilled according to our wish;
we have attained our hopes, O Wielder of the Thunderbolt.
O Son of Strength, those who desire your favor have turned toward you;
O Indra, nothing surpasses you.
O Bull, with your most bountiful, formidable, and swift-moving wisdom, favor us with your abundant providence.
O Indra, O Śatakratu, that exhilaration of yours which is truly the most glorious— by means of that, do you now indeed rejoice in intoxication.
O Indra, that exhilaration of yours which possesses the most wonderful renown, which is the greatest slayer of Vṛtra, and which bestows the most power— [that is the one we choose].
For we know, O wielder of the thunderbolt, you who are true to the Soma-drinker and bestow gifts;
O wonder-worker, among all the peoples.
For Indra, who delights in the intoxicating draught, let our songs resound all around;
let the poets sing the hymn of praise.
In whom all glories rejoice, in whom the seven assemblies delight— that Indra we invoke when the soma is pressed.
At the Trikadruka rites, the gods performed the conscious sacrifice; may our songs of praise increase that very sacrifice for us.
May the drops enter you as rivers flow into the ocean;
O Indra, nothing exceeds you.
O mighty bull, you have disclosed with your greatness the draught of Soma, O watchful one—
that which, O Indra, is within your bellies.
O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, let the Soma be sufficient for your belly; O Indu-drops, be sufficient for your vital powers.
Śrutakakṣa sings sufficiently for the horse, sufficiently for the cow,
sufficiently for the domain of Indra.
For you, O Indra, are indeed ready for our pressed Soma juices;
O Śakra, you are ready to grant us gifts.
O wielder of the thunderbolt, even from afar our songs reach you;
may we come before you in due season.
For thus indeed you are one who seeks heroes, thus a hero, and thus steadfast;
thus indeed may your mind be successful.
Thus has this gift been established by all the ordainers, O Lord of abundant wealth;
and so, Indra, it is truly with me.
O Lord of spoils, do not be sluggish like a priest; exhilarate yourself with the pressed juice mixed with milk.
O Indra, let not the hostilities of the sun reach us during the nights;
with you as our ally, may we conquer them.
O Indra, with you as our ally, may we answer back against our rivals;
you are ours, and we are yours.
For indeed, O Indra, the singers who love you follow after you as they move along, your friends, O Indra.
O Sūrya, you indeed rise up toward the bull of renowned bounty, the performer of manly deeds, the archer.
He who by the strength of his arms shattered ninety-nine fortresses,
and as the slayer of Vṛtra, struck down the serpent.
That Indra is our auspicious friend; he milks for us wealth consisting of horses, cattle, and barley, like a wide-streaming cow.
O Vṛtra-slayer, whatever has risen today and wherever the sun shines— O Indra, all that is under your control.
Or when you, O exalted Lord of the Good, think "I shall not die," even that thought of yours is indeed true.
O Indra, you go to all those Soma juices that are pressed, whether they be in the distance or nearby.
We incite that Indra for the slaying of the great Vṛtra;
may he become the bull, the showerer of blessings.
Indra is he who has been made for the act of giving; he is the most powerful, established in the exhilaration of the soma; he is resplendent, worthy of praise, and beloved by the Soma.
Like a thunderbolt fashioned by song, powerful and unshakable, the lofty and invincible one has grown great.
O Indra, lover of songs, being praised, make even our difficult path easy to traverse;
and you, O Maghavan, shall have your own will.
O you whose sovereign rule no one at all disregards,
neither god nor humble man [can violate it].
Then the two goddesses, heaven and earth, O fair-cheeked one, revere your irresistible might.
You have established this bright milk in the dark cows and in the ruddy ones, and in the speckled cows.
When all the gods stepped forth from the serpent’s brilliance,
they found that terror of the wild beast.
And then the Vṛtra-slayer became my protector; he has displayed his manly power—he who has no enemy and is unsubdued.
I have heard of you as the greatest slayers of Vṛtra, the preeminent host of the peoples; I call upon you for great bounty and for strength.
O you of many names, much-praised one, through this prayer for cattle,
since at every Soma libation you have been present.
May the Vṛtra-slayer, who is abundantly invoked, be mindful of us;
may Śakra hear our prayer.
With what aid, O Bull, do you gladden us? With what [aid] will you bring [wealth] to those who praise you?
At whose pressed juice does the bull, accompanied by his team, rejoice—
the Vṛtra-slayer, for the drinking of the Soma?
Rejoicing, do thou indeed bestow upon us thousandfold wealth;
be the giver to the worshipper.
These pressed juices, accompanied by their wives, go eagerly to the feast;
the gliding one has entered the waters.
The desired oblations have been poured forth; the strengthening offerings have flowed toward Indra at the sacrifice, with power, unto the purificatory bath.
Hither let these two bay steeds, companions at the feast, with golden manes, carry you toward the prepared food.
For you, O Radiant One, these Soma juices have been pressed and the sacred grass strewn;
bring Indra hither for the sake of those who praise you.
Bestowing skill upon you and radiant jewels upon the donor,
praise Indra for the sake of those who offer hymns of praise.
O Śatakratu, we place within you all our hymns of praise and your own power;
O Indra, be gracious to those who sing your praises.
O Śatakratu, bring us every blessing— food and strength—
when you, O Indra, show us mercy.
O Śatakratu, bring us all prosperity,
for you, O Indra, will be gracious to us.
O best slayer of Vṛtra, we who have pressed the soma call upon you alone;
O Indra, when you show us mercy.
Come to our pressed juice with your bay horses, O Lord of intoxications;
come to our pressed juice with your bay horses.
Indra, who from of old is the greatest slayer of Vṛtra, whose power is a hundredfold—
come with your bay steeds to our pressed juice!
For you, O slayer of Vṛtra, are the drinker of these Soma juices;
come to our pressed juice with your two bay horses.
May Indra grant us for our nourishment wealth that is *ṛbhu* and ruled by the *ṛbhus*;
may the prize-winner grant us a prize-winning steed.
The cow, seeking glory, suckles the Maruts— the mother of the bounteous ones—
yoked as the bearer of their chariots.
In whose lap all the gods maintain their vows—
the sun and moon, so that they may be seen.
Therefore, all the noble singers always praise us well for that— O Maruts, [come] for the drinking of the Soma!
This Soma has been pressed; the Maruts drink of it, as do the self-ruling Aśvins.
Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa drink their fill of the purified [Soma] that dwells in the three abodes and brings forth progeny.
And now may Indra, according to his pleasure, delight in this pressed juice mixed with milk; at dawn he shall exhilarate himself like a Hotṛ priest.
When did the wise ones shine forth? Like waters, they flow across their adversaries, they whose will is purified.
Of you great gods, whose splendor is wondrous, what favor do I choose for myself today?
The Maruts, who have spread out all the earthly realms and the luminous spaces of heaven, [come] for the drinking of Soma.
I now call you Maruts from heaven, you whose will is purified,
for the drinking of this Soma.
I now call those Maruts who have propped apart the two worlds,
for the drinking of this Soma.
I now call upon that host of Maruts, dwelling on the mountains, the bull-like troop,
for the drinking of this Soma.
O lover of songs, may our hymns rise up to you like a charioteer when the Soma has been pressed;
they have lowed toward you in unison, O Indra, as mother cows low toward their calf.
The bright pressed juices have drawn you hither, O Indra, lover of songs.
Drink of this food, O Indra; it is prepared for you among all [the people].
Drink the Soma for exhilaration, O Indra, the pressed juice brought by the falcon;
for you are the lord and king of all the eternal tribes.
Hear the call of Tiraścī, O Indra, who honors you.
Fill us with wealth consisting of great heroism and cattle; for you are great.
O Indra, [the seer] has generated for you a newest, delightful song—
a prayer born of an observant mind, ancient, and swelling with the Truth (ṛta).
Let us praise that Indra whom songs and hymns have strengthened;
desiring to win his many manly deeds, we shall prevail.
Come now, let us praise Indra, the pure one, with a pure *sāman*;
may he, who has grown strong through pure hymns, being pure himself, be exhilarated by the pure draught.
O Indra, come to us pure, with pure aids;
being pure, bestow wealth upon us; being pure and worthy of the Soma, rejoice.
O Indra, being pure, grant us wealth; being pure, grant treasures to the donor.
Being pure, you slay the Vṛtras; being pure, you seek to win the prize.
For him the Dawns have lengthened their course; for Indra, the nights with their fair voices have flowed through the darkness.
For him the seven mother waters stood still—the rivers easy to cross—so that men might ford them.
Pierced through by his unsteady weapon, the thrice-seven ridges of the mountains were shattered;
neither god nor mortal could surpass that which the grown bull performed.
The iron thunderbolt of Indra is firmly joined; in the two arms of Indra lies the greatest strength.
In the head of Indra, his powers are uniquely concentrated; they seek him out nearby through the hearing of his fame.
I deem you worthy of sacrifice among those worthy of sacrifice; I deem you the shaker of the unshakable.
I deem you, O Indra, the banner of heroes; I deem you the bull of the people.
When you, O Indra, take the mace that distills exhilaration into your arms for the sake of slaying the serpent,
the mountains resounded, the cattle lowed, and the priests drew near to Indra.
Let us praise him who brought forth all these created beings that are inferior to him;
through our songs may we win Mitra with Indra, and let us approach the Bull with prostrations.
Fleeing from the snort of Vṛtra, all the gods who were your friends abandoned you;
O Indra, let there be friendship between you and the Maruts, and then you shall conquer all these hostile armies.
The sixty-three Maruts, worthy of sacrifice, have increased you like heaps of dawns;
we approach you—grant us our portion, for with this oblation we shall honor your might.
The sharp weapon is the vanguard of the Maruts; O Indra, who has dared to withstand your thunderbolt?
Weaponless are the Asuras, the godless ones; O wielder of the *ṛjīṣa*, sweep them away with your wheel!
Send forth a well-fashioned hymn to the great, fierce, and powerful one, most auspicious for our cattle;
bestow many songs upon Indra, who is borne by songs, for his own body—surely he will take notice of this.
Send forth our prayer to the far-reaching one who bears the hymns, as one crosses to the further shore of rivers with a boat.
Touch the body of the famous one, most dear to us, with your thought; will he indeed perceive it?
Perform that for him which Indra will enjoy; praise him with a beautiful hymn and win him over with homage. Draw near, O singer, do not cry out; let your voice be heard, for he surely knows.
The dark Drop descended into the Aṃśumatī river, hastening with ten thousand [followers].
Indra, by his power, protected him as he blew [the fire]; the hero-minded one cast away the dripping waters.
I beheld the drop moving in the distance, in the secret hiding place by the river Aṃśumatī; like a black cloud, he stood firm. O heroes, I urge you on: fight in the battle!
Then Drapsa, flashing forth, took his place upon the lap of Aṃśumatī;
with Bṛhaspati as his ally, Indra overcame the godless tribes that were attacking.
At your very birth, O Indra, you became the enemy of those seven who were without enemies;
you discovered the hidden Heaven and Earth and bestowed joy upon the vast worlds.
O wielder of the thunderbolt, you indeed boldly struck down that incomparable power with your bolt;
you shattered the strength of Śuṣṇa with your weapons, and by your might, O Indra, you found the cattle.
O Bull of the people, you indeed became the mighty slayer of Vṛtras;
you set free the obstructed rivers and you won back the waters that had Dāsa lords for their masters.
He is the one of noble wisdom who delights in the pressed juices, whose fury is unsurpassed, and who is as wealthy as the day;
he alone is the doer of manly deeds, the slayer of Vṛtra—others, they say, are his opposite.
That Indra is the slayer of Vṛtra and the sustainer of the people; him, the one to be invoked, we shall call with excellent praise.
He is our protector, the bounteous lord, the advocate, and the giver of strength that brings renown.
That Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra and lord of the Ṛbhus, as soon as he was born, became worthy of invocation;
performing many manly deeds, like Soma when drunk, he is to be invoked by his friends.
O Indra, those enjoyments which you, possessor of the light, brought from the Asuras—
O Maghavan, increase the singer of this hymn and those who have spread the sacrificial grass for you.
O Indra, that horse and cow, the imperishable portion which you hold, bestow it upon the sacrificer who presses the soma and gives the sacrificial fee; do not place it with the miser.
O Indra, that unrighteous one who, being godless, has slept through sixty winters—may he perish by his own ways; place that nourishing wealth far away from him.
Whether you are in the distance, O Śakra, or whether you are nearby, O slayer of Vṛtra—
therefore the one who has pressed the soma seeks to win you over with long-maned songs that ascend to heaven, O Indra.
Whether you are in the luminous realm of heaven, upon the surface of the ocean,
in a terrestrial dwelling, O greatest slayer of Vṛtra, or in the intermediate space— come hither!
O Soma-drinker, Lord of Might, at our pressed soma-juices,
rejoice with your bounty and with wealth that is full of truth, O Indra, with abundant riches.
O Indra, do not turn us away; be our companion at the feast.
You alone are our protection, you alone are our kinship; O Indra, do not turn us away.
O Indra, sit with us by the pressed juice to drink the honey;
O Maghavan, grant great protection to the singer—be with us, O Indra, by the pressed juice.
Neither gods nor mortals have attained you, O wielder of the stone;
you surpass all created beings in might—neither gods nor mortals have attained you.
In unison, they fashioned and brought forth Indra, the hero who overcomes all hostile armies, so that he might rule as king;
him most excellent in wisdom, the filler of the wide space, the fierce, the strongest, the powerful, and the swift.
The singers have raised their voices together for Indra to drink the Soma—him, the Lord of Light—for his increase; for he, whose vows are firm, is indeed powerful with might and with his aids.
With their vision, the inspired singers bend the felly toward the ram with their chants;
you who are well-shining, free from guile, and swift, they bring [the hymns] close to your ear along with the singers of verses.
I invoke that Indra, the bounteous and fierce one, who ever possesses irresistible powers;
may he, the most generous and worthy of sacrifice, turn toward us with his songs and, wielding the thunderbolt, make all paths easy for our wealth.
O Indra, most powerful Śakra, you, the wise one, have from of old destroyed these forts with your might in order to annihilate them.
O wielder of the thunderbolt, all beings tremble at your fear, and both heaven and earth shake.
O Indra, O hero, O wondrous one, may that truth protect me; O wielder of the thunderbolt, carry us across many difficulties as if across waters.
O King Indra, when will you grant us wealth—wealth that provides for all and is worthy of longing?
Sing forth a lofty Sāman for Indra, the inspired singer, the great one— the Sāman for the upholder of the Law, the wise, and the one worthy of praise.
O Indra, you are the conqueror; you caused the sun to shine.
You are the maker of all, the god of all; you are great.
Shining with light, you went to the sun, to the luminous realm of heaven;
O Indra, the gods strove for your friendship.
O Indra, come to us as our beloved, the ever-conquering one who cannot be hidden,
broad on all sides like a mountain, the lord of heaven.
For you, O truthful drinker of Soma, have surpassed both worlds;
O Indra, you are the strengthener of the one who presses the juice, the Lord of Heaven.
For you, O Indra, are the shatterer of eternal fortresses; you are the slayer of the Dasyu, the prosperer of Manu, and the lord of heaven.
Now indeed, O Indra, lover of songs, we have released our great desires toward you,
like those going upward with water.
O Hero, as the waters increase the ocean with their currents, so do our prayers increase you,
O wielder of the stone, even though you have already grown great day by day.
They harness the two bay steeds of the impetuous one with song upon the broad, wide-yoked chariot— the two bearers of Indra, yoked by a word.
O Indra, bring to us strength and manly valor, O Lord of a hundred powers, O far-seeing one;
bring a hero who conquers in battle.
For you indeed, O Vasu, have become our father and our mother, O Śatakratu;
therefore, we seek your favor.
O impetuous one, much-invoked, lord of a hundred powers, I address you who are eager for the prize;
as such, grant us heroic strength.
O wielder of the thunderbolt, eager men have made you swell with drink yesterday and today;
as such, O Indra, hear us here, you who are borne by hymns, and come to our dwelling place.
Rejoice, O fair-cheeked Lord of Bay Steeds; this we implore of you. The wise ones wait upon you;
O Indra, lover of songs, your glories are supreme and worthy of praise when the juices are pressed.
Turning toward him as if toward the sun, may we all enjoy the riches of Indra;
at his birth and at every new birth by his might, we look toward our portion as if toward a share.
Praise him who bestows wealth and whose bounty is never-failing; auspicious indeed are Indra’s gifts. He does not frustrate the desire of the one who serves him, but stirs his mind toward giving.
O Indra, in battles you prevail over all rival hosts; you are the slayer of the malevolent, the progenitor, and the conqueror of all. Do you overcome those who seek to overcome us.
The two worlds followed after your surging strength, like two mother cows following their calf;
all your rivals yielded to your wrath when you, O Indra, overcame Vṛtra.
Hither for your aid [we call] the ageless one, the sender who is not sent;
the swift victor, the hurler, the best of charioteers, the unvanquished one who increased the Tugryas.

We invoke for our protection the common Indra, the maker of what was unmade, the one made by force, who possesses a hundred aids and a hundred powers— the possessor of wealth, the one who hastens toward riches.
Here I come before you in person; all the gods follow behind me.
When you have assigned a portion to me, O Indra, then through me alone shall you perform heroic deeds.
I place before you a draught of honey; let the pressed Soma be your allotted portion.
And you, as my friend, shall be at my right hand; then we two shall slay many Vṛtras.
Bring forth a hymn of praise, seeking booty, for Indra—true praise, if indeed there is truth.
"Indra does not exist"—only some say this; who has seen him? Whom shall we praise?
Here I am, O singer; behold me here! I surpass all created beings in my greatness.
The quarters of the world increase me; bursting them open, I rend the worlds asunder.

When the yearnings of Truth ascended toward me as I sat alone upon the back of the beloved one, even my mind spoke back to me from my heart; my friends, possessing young offspring, cried out in response.
All those deeds of yours are to be proclaimed at the libations, O Maghavan Indra, which you performed for the one who presses the juice—
when you opened up the wealth gathered from afar for Śarabha, the kinsman of the seers.
Now run forth each in a different direction; let him who has held you back here not remain!
Indra has hurled his thunderbolt down upon the vital organ of Vṛtra.
Moving with the speed of thought, he crossed the iron fortress;
having gone to heaven as a fair-winged bird, he brought the Soma for the wielder of the thunderbolt.
Within the ocean, the thunderbolt lies enveloped by the waters;
