they bring him tribute from the forward-flowing streams in constant succession.
When Vāk, the joyous queen of the gods, sat down speaking words that are beyond human thought, she milked out fourfold nourishment and waters; where indeed has her highest part gone?
The gods generated divine speech; animals of every form speak it.
May that cow-like Speech, yielding us joy, refreshment, and vigor, come to us with fair praise.
O friend Viṣṇu, stride out further; O Heaven, grant space for the hurling of the thunderbolt.
Let us two slay Vṛtra and release the rivers; let them flow forth, set free by the impulse of Indra.
Truly, that mortal has indeed labored successfully for the service of the gods,
who now has brought Mitra and Varuṇa near for his protection and for the offering of oblations.
O heroes of most exalted sovereignty and wide vision, O kings of far-reaching fame,
you two, like arms through your wondrous deeds, move upon your chariot together with the rays of the sun.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, he who ran forth as your swift messenger— the iron-headed one, impetuous in his joy— has sped along.
He who does not seek to associate, nor delights in being summoned again, nor in conversation—from him protect us today through our encounter; protect us with your arms.
O you who abide by the Eternal Law (*ṛtāvasu*), sing forth a helpful, protective, and pleasing word— a hymn of praise— to Mitra, to Aryaman, and to Varuṇa among the kings.
They have sent forth the ruddy, noble treasure, the single son of the three;
those immortal and undeceivable ones look down upon the dwellings of mortals.
Come to my uplifted words, most brilliant deeds to be performed;
O Nāsatyas, come both of you together with one accord to enjoy the offerings.
When we invoke your unassailable bounty, O you who possess abundant wealth,
come hither, O Heroes, praised by Jamadagni, accepting our forward-offered oblation.
O Vāyu, come with benevolent thoughts to our sacrifice that touches the heavens;
being mixed above the filter, this bright [soma] is offered to you.
The Adhvaryu priest comes by the straightest paths to receive the oblations for his enjoyment;
therefore, O Lord of the teams, drink of both our offerings—the pure Soma mixed with milk.
Truly, O Sūrya, you are great; truly, O Āditya, you are great.
The greatness of you who are so great is celebrated; indeed, O God, you are great.
Truly, O Sūrya, you are great in fame; indeed, O God, you are great.
By your greatness, you are the divine Asura, the high priest of the gods, the pervasive and invincible light.
This [song], which is directed downward and rich in praise, fashioned by Rūpā Rohiṇī,
has appeared like a marvel as it moves within the ten arms.
Three generations have passed beyond this world; others have settled around the sacred song.
The Great One has taken his stand within the worlds; as Pavamāna, he has entered the golden rays.
The mother of the Rudras, the daughter of the Vasus, the sister of the Ādityas, the navel of immortality—I proclaim this now to the person who understands: do not slay the cow, the sinless Aditi!
The mortal of feeble intellect has driven away the goddess Cow, who knows speech, who utters her voice, who attends upon all sacred thoughts, and who has come forth from among the gods.
O Agni, you, the god, bestow great vital strength upon the donor;
you are the sage, the young master of the house.
O Agni, bring hither the gods with our invocation and our service,
you who are wise and radiant.
O youngest one, with you as our ally, who are most swift to urge us on, may we prevail for the winning of the prize.
Like Aurva and Bhr̥gu, like Apnavāna, I invoke the pure Agni, who is clothed in the ocean.
I invoke the seer who sounds like the wind, the power that roars like Parjanya, Agni, whose garment is the ocean.
I call upon Agni, who is clothed in the ocean, like the impulse of Savitṛ and like the enjoyment of Bhaga.
I praise Agni for you, who increases the sacrifices, the most frequent among gods,
toward the powerful grandson.
May he come to us just as Tvaṣṭṛ comes with forms to be fashioned,
through the inspired wisdom of this glorious one.
This Agni rules over all splendors among the gods;
may he come to us with strengths.
Praise here the most glorious one among all the Hotṛ-priests,
Agni, the foremost in sacrifices.
Sharp and purifying in his radiance, he who is the eldest in the homes has shone forth, he whose fame is most far-reaching.
O sage, praise him who is like a prize-winning steed, the impetuous one,
who stirs men to action like Mitra.
The sisterly songs of the oblation-bearer, pointing the way, have settled near you at the face of Vāyu.
He for whom the threefold sacrificial grass has been spread out, unbound and firmly established—
even the waters have set down their station there.
The station of the bounteous god, with his unassailable aids,
is auspicious to behold like the sun.
O Agni, O God, glowing with the heat of your flame through the offerings of clarified butter,
bring the gods here and worship them.
Thee, the sage, the immortal bearer of oblations, the gods and the mothers brought forth, O Aṅgiras.
O sage Agni, they have established you— the wise one, the excellent messenger,
the bearer of oblations— as their priest.
For I have no cow to offer, nor an axe for the wood-cutter;
yet such as this I bring to you.
O Agni, whatever logs we lay upon you, however many they may be—
enjoy them, O youngest one!
Whatever the upajihvikā eats, whatever the ant crawls over—
that may all be ghee for you.
Kindling Agni with his mind, a mortal should attend upon the prayer;
I have kindled Agni with the rays of light.
He has been seen, the best finder of the way, in whom they have established their sacred vows.
Let our songs reach Agni, the newborn who increases the prosperity of the noble one.
The son of Divodāsa, Agni, has gone forth toward the gods with his might;
he has spread himself across the mother earth and stands upon the ridge of the firmament.
From whom the people tremble when he performs his wondrous deeds— he who wins a thousandfold like one victorious in the contest for wisdom— honor that Agni with your prayers as if with your own self.
O Vasu, the mortal whom you wish to lead toward wealth and who offers gifts to you—
he, O Agni, by his own self receives a hero who recites hymns of praise and who prospers with a thousandfold increase.
He pierces even the firm stronghold for booty with his steed; he wins imperishable fame.
O Lord of many riches, we ever place all desirable things in you among the gods.
He who distributes all wealth, the joyous invoker of men—
to that Agni the hymns of praise go forth like the first vessels of honeyed mead.
Like a chariot-horse, those who give good gifts and seek the gods polish [you] with their songs, O wondrous Lord of the people;
protect both our children and our progeny, and bring us the bounty of the wealthy patrons.
Sing forth to the most generous one, the observer of cosmic order (*ṛtāvan*), the great one with brilliant radiance—
to Agni, you who offer praise.
May the bountiful one, kindled and invoked with splendor, win for us fame accompanied by heroes. Will his most recent favor come toward us with strengths?
Praise Agni, the most beloved of those dear to us, the guest who comes from afar, the driver of chariots.
He who, worthy of sacrifice, brings forth wealth— whether it be proclaimed, censured, or known—
he whose waves are difficult to overcome as they flow down the slope, seeks to win the prize through his inspired thought.
May the guest Agni, the Vasu, praised by many, not be angry with us—
he who is a good invoker and a master of the sacrifice.
O Vasu Agni, let none who approach you with invocations be harmed by any of your ways;
for even the poor man, having offered oblations, prays to you as his messenger, performing the sacrifice well.
O Agni, come as a friend of the Maruts with the Rudras for the drinking of Soma;
come to the excellent praise of Sobhari and rejoice, O Svarṇara.
